title: Early and Long-Term Outcomes of Carotid Endarterectomy in Patients With Carotid Near-Occlusion Versus Preocclusive Carotid Stenosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The clinical role of carotid endarterectomy (CEA) in patients with carotid near-occlusion (CNO) remains a subject of ongoing debate, and comparative data regarding its long-term efficacy versus preocclusive carotid stenosis is limited. This study aimed to evaluate and compare the perioperative and long-term outcomes of CEA in these two distinct subsets of high-grade carotid disease. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on a prospectively maintained database of 1775 consecutive CEAs performed at a single center between January 2014 and September 2025. The study cohort included 81 procedures for CNO (Group 1) and 144 for preocclusive carotid stenosis > 95% with distal lumen recovery (Group 2). CNO was defined by distal internal carotid artery caliber reduction and further stratified by the presence of full distal collapse. RESULTS: Results showed that patients in Group 2 were significantly older than those in Group 1 (76 ± 8 vs. 72 ± 8 years; p < 0.001). Symptomatic presentation was more frequent in Group 1 (35.8% vs. 24.3%; p = 0.06), and concordant ipsilateral ischemic brain lesions were significantly more common in CNO patients (24.5% vs. 9%; p = 0.001). Regarding perioperative safety, no 30-day deaths or major neurologic events occurred in Group 1, while Group 2 had a 30-day stroke/death rate of 3.4% (p = 0.08 vs. Group 1). During a median follow-up of 30 months (range 1-140), the estimated 6-year overall survival was 84% for Group 1% and 73% for Group 2 (p = 0.1). Notably, ipsilateral stroke at 6 years occurred in 0% of CNO patients compared with 8.5% in the preocclusive group (p = 0.03). Stroke-free survival at 6 years was 84% in Group 1% and 71% in Group 2 (p = 0.09). While freedom from restenosis was comparable (78.5% vs. 86.3%; p = 0.2), late carotid occlusion was significantly more frequent in the CNO group (6% vs. 0%; p = 0.02). CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center series, patients undergoing CEA for carotid near-occlusion demonstrated favorable perioperative safety and a lower observed incidence of long-term ipsilateral stroke during follow-up compared with those treated for preocclusive stenosis, even in the presence of full distal collapse. The absence of a medically managed control group and the small number of events made these findings hypothesis-generating. However, the higher incidence of late restenosis and occlusion in near-occlusion highlights the importance of a personalized, intensified postoperative surveillance, particularly for patients with full distal collapse.

This study aimed to evaluate and compare the perioperative and long-term outcomes of CEA in these two distinct subsets of high-grade carotid disease. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on a prospectively maintained database of 1775 consecutive CEAs performed at a single center between January 2014 and September 2025.

title: A comparison of the efficacy and safety of direct oral anticoagulants with low molecular weight heparin for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total hip arthroplasty : a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: AIMS: To evaluate differences in the efficacy and safety of low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) used for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after elective total hip arthroplasty (THA). METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis reviewed MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL from conception to 13 December 2025, for any randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing the efficacy (VTE risk) and safety (bleeding risk) of LMWH and DOACs after elective THA. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) of VTE, bleeding, reoperation, and mortality risks were assessed. RESULTS: A total of 22 RCTs involving 28,112 participants were included. The risk of VTE in the DOAC group was lower compared with the LMWH group (OR 0.62 (95% CI 0.47 to 0.82); p = 0.002), driven by a reduction in deep vein thrombosis (DVT) risk (OR 0.60 (95% CI 0.42 to 0.86); p = 0.008). The findings remained consistent in the subgroup analysis restricted to anticoagulants and dosages licensed for use in the UK. Overall bleeding risk was higher in the DOAC group (OR 1.19 (95% CI 1.03 to 1.38); p = 0.023), but no difference was seen when comparing only UK-licensed anticoagulants and doses (OR 1.06 (95% CI 0.95 to 1.18); p = 0.279). Reoperation risk (OR 1.21 (95% CI 0.75 to 1.93); p = 0.351) and mortality (OR 1.03 (95% CI 0.46 to 2.33); p = 0.937) did not differ between groups. CONCLUSION: DOACs reduce the risk of VTE and DVT following elective THA compared with LMWH without increasing bleeding risk, for UK-licensed agents and doses. Switching to DOACs could save the NHS £8.6 million per year. New clinical trials are needed to compare the safety and efficacy of UK-licensed DOACs and LWMH with modern postoperative rehabilitation protocols.

title: A Versatile, Patient-Centred Approach to Surgical Wound Closure: A Single-Centre Case Series on the Use of a Synthetic Electrospun Fibre Matrix in Vasculopathic Patients.
abstract: Patients with vascular disease often suffer from lower extremity ulcerations that may require surgical intervention to remove non-viable or infected tissues. Post-operatively, these patients still present with a high risk of non-healing due to poor blood flow and chronic inflammation. Advanced wound healing matrices may be considered to support tissue regenerative and reduce the risk of further wound complications. A synthetic electrospun fibre matrix (SEFM) (Restrata, Acera Surgical Inc.) is a fully synthetic, extracellular matrix that encourages cellular infiltration and neovascularization with minimal inflammatory response. In the present study, a single vascular surgeon retrospectively reviewed data of vasculopathic patients treated with SEFM during surgical management of various wound aetiologies. Ten patients were identified and data on time to closure, closure approach and post-operative complications were collected and analysed. SEFM was utilized to either support neo-vascularization for subsequent autografting or re-epithelialization through secondary intention healing. All patients in this series achieved either definitive closure or complete re-epithelialization in an average of 6.8 weeks. One instance of superficial infection was successfully managed with antibiotics. No instances of unplanned re-operation or other wound complications were observed. Early experience suggests practical application of SEFM for surgical wound management in vasculopathic patients.

title: Effectiveness of Tomazoni Measurement Method for Central Catheter Tip Positioning in Neonates: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Accurate peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC) tip positioning in neonates remains challenging, with high rates of malposition reported using traditional measurement methods. AIM: To evaluate the effectiveness of the Tomazoni method for PICC positioning in neonates compared with the traditional method. STUDY DESIGN: Pragmatic, parallel-group randomised clinical trial with stratified block randomisation, conducted in a neonatal intensive care unit in Brazil between June 2024 and April 2025. RESULTS: Of 62 randomised procedures, 55 were evaluable (27 in the experimental group, 28 in the control group). Central positioning was achieved in 21 of 27 procedures (77.8%) in the experimental group versus 5 of 28 (17.9%) in the control group (p < 0.001). PICC insertion procedures assessed using the Tomazoni method were 4.36 times more likely to achieve central tip placement (RR = 4.36; 95% CI: 1.91-9.88). Catheter withdrawal was required in 3 of 27 procedures (11.1%) in the experimental group versus 16 of 28 (57.1%) in the control group (p = 0.001; RR = 0.19; 95% CI: 0.06-0.59). CONCLUSIONS: The Tomazoni measurement method was associated with substantially higher rates of central PICC tip positioning and reduced need for catheter withdrawal compared with the traditional method. RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: The Tomazoni method offers a reproducible, low-cost measurement strategy that can be implemented in neonatal intensive care units to improve catheter positioning accuracy and reduce procedure-related manipulations, with potential implications for patient safety. The trial, titled 'Comparison between measurements of peripherally inserted central catheters in children and newborns', was registered in the Brazilian Clinical Trials Registry under the identifier RBR-55zwb45. TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial is registered in the Brazilian Clinical Trials Registry (ReBEC) under the identifier RBR-55zwb45.

title: Learning Manipulation Features for Quantitative Assessment and Skill-Level Classification in Robot-Assisted Intervention: In Vivo Rabbit Studies.
abstract: Robot-assisted vascular interventions demand precise manipulation within tortuous millimeter-scale vessels, where surgical outcomes remain critically dependent on surgeon skill. Conventional metrics such as completion time or navigation success are too coarse to capture the subtle, yet decisive control differences between experts and novices, while sensor-heavy external approaches obscure the surgeon's intrinsic dynamics. This article introduces a task-aware spectral modeling (TASM) framework that directly extracts skill signatures from joystick control signals, revealing how surgical expertise manifests in the time-frequency domain. In vivo rabbit experiments demonstrate that expert manipulation emerges as smooth, deliberate low-frequency rhythmic control, whereas novice performance degenerates into fragmented, high-frequency corrections. Spectral analysis indicates that approximately 96% of control energy lies below 5 Hz, suggesting that low-frequency components may serve as an indicative spectral characteristic associated with expert-novice differentiation under similar experimental and task conditions. By deriving interpretable spectral descriptors, the framework achieves an average ROC-AUC of 0.992 across nine classifiers. Clinically, the proposed framework may support quantitative assessment of surgical skill and control stability in robot-assisted endovascular procedures, with potential value for identifying inconsistent control behaviors and informing future training and evaluation pipelines.

title: Biological sex differences in the United States CTEPH Registry.
abstract: RATIONALE: Biological sex underpins phenotypic differences in many cardiopulmonary conditions. In pulmonary hypertension, most studies have focused on the "sex paradox" in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), where females are more susceptible to PAH but have better right ventricular function, better response to PAH medications, and better survival than males. Sex differences have also been observed in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) but are less well characterized. OBJECTIVES: To investigate sex differences in males and females diagnosed with CTEPH in the United States. METHODS: Using the multicenter United States CTEPH Registry, we explored sex differences in a CTEPH population at baseline and follow-up. We collected data every 6 months for a total of 48 months. Sex was determined from self-reported "male," "female," or "transgender" categories recorded on case report forms. We report descriptive analyses comparing male and female characteristics. We examined prespecified variables of interest using regression modeling, including adjustment for age, body mass index (BMI), and interaction terms (sex vs age, sex vs BMI). Survival analysis was performed with Cox proportional hazards modeling. RESULTS: Females (n = 367, 49.1%) had greater BMI than males (median [IQR] F: 32 kg/m2 [26.6, 38.8] vs M: 28.7 kg/m2 [25.5, 33.8]). Males were more likely to have a recognized history of acute deep vein thrombosis (OR 2.6; CI 1.9-3.5). Males had better baseline PH-specific health-related quality of life (HRQoL) by EmPHasis10 (-3.3; CI -5.0- (-1.7), World Health Organization functional class (FC III/IV OR 0.52, CI 0.37-0.74) and longer 6-minute walk distance (+82.3 m, CI 56.4-108.2). Males were less likely to have distally located disease (OR 0.53, CI 0.35-0.78) and were less likely to have inoperable CTEPH (OR 0.62, CI 0.40-0.96). Post-PTE, females had persistently worse HRQoL and function, with increased need for adjunctive therapies. There was no difference in overall survival between males and females (HR 1.11; CI 0.71-1.75). CONCLUSIONS: Males and females may have distinct CTEPH phenotypes, which impact access to and feasibility of PTE. There are sex-associated disparities in the experience of CTEPH as a disease state, and differential impacts on HRQoL that warrant further investigation.

In pulmonary hypertension, most studies have focused on the "sex paradox" in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), where females are more susceptible to PAH but have better right ventricular function, better response to PAH medications, and better survival than males. Sex differences have also been observed in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) but are less well characterized.

title: Outcomes post-thrombectomy in children: A multi-site assessment of a new non-lytic endovascular device combined with anticoagulation for management of adolescents with extensive acute lower limb deep vein thrombosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Adolescents who develop extensive lower extremity deep venous thrombosis (DVT) are at high-risk for adverse outcomes including post-thrombotic syndrome (PTS) with anticoagulation alone. New mechanical thrombectomy devices, such as the ClotTriever® device, have been reported to reduce PTS in adults, however, there is limited data in adolescents with lower extremity DVT. AIM: To assess outcomes of adolescents post-mechanical thrombectomy with a ClotTriever® device for extensive lower extremity DVT in a multisite Canadian cohort. METHODS: Adolescents (age 10- < 18 years) who underwent mechanical thrombectomy with a ClotTriever® device for extensive lower extremity DVT between 01/2023-03/2026 at 5 Canadian centres were reviewed retrospectively. Data collected included demographics, DVT symptoms/risks, imaging, anticoagulation, procedure details and bleeding (major and clinically relevant non-major (CRNM)). Outcomes on imaging and PTS assessments (CAPTSure© score) were completed at 6 and/or ≥12 months post-thrombectomy. RESULTS: Twenty-one patients were identified with 20/21 undergoing thrombectomy <2 weeks from symptom onset. 20/21 had follow-up imaging after anticoagulation therapy with 12/20 showing full resolution of thrombus. No patients had major or CRNM bleeding post-thrombectomy even with intensive periprocedural anticoagulation. All patients completed PTS assessments with CAPTSure© scores at 6 and/or ≥12 months post-thrombectomy (median 12 months) with 19/21 having no PTS, 1/21 having mild PTS and 1/21 having moderate-severe PTS. CONCLUSIONS: Results suggest adolescents with extensive lower limb DVT who underwent thrombectomy with ClotTriever® in combination with anticoagulation had a high rate of thrombus resolution and a low rate of PTS. Lack of bleeding events may be an advantage over endovascular thrombolysis in this population.

New mechanical thrombectomy devices, such as the ClotTriever® device, have been reported to reduce PTS in adults, however, there is limited data in adolescents with lower extremity DVT. AIM: To assess outcomes of adolescents post-mechanical thrombectomy with a ClotTriever® device for extensive lower extremity DVT in a multisite Canadian cohort.

title: Imaging-Based Assessment of Plaque Modification Following Intravascular Lithotripsy in Femoropopliteal Disease: A Prospective Single-Centre Observational Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) is designed to treat calcified peripheral arteries with steno-occlusive disease; however, its effect on plaque morphology remains incompletely understood in vivo. This study evaluated plaque modification and luminal changes following IVL in femoropopliteal disease using computed tomography angiography (CTA) and intravascular ultrasound (IVUS). METHODS: This was a prospective single centre observational study. Consecutive patients with symptomatic femoropopliteal disease undergoing IVL between December 2024 and October 2025 underwent pre- and post-procedural (within five days) CTA with quantitative plaque analysis. IVUS was performed before and immediately after IVL, prior to drug coated balloon angioplasty (applied in all patients) or stenting (used only as bailout). The primary endpoint was change in calcified plaque volume on CTA. Secondary endpoints included luminal gain, haemodynamic changes, procedural success, and 6 month clinical outcomes. RESULTS: 2 Thirty nine patients were included; median age was 71 years. Calcified plaque volume showed a modest reduction (median proportional reduction 12.2%, p < .001) on post-procedural CTA. IVL resulted in luminal expansion, with IVUS measured lumen area increasing from 5.78 to 16.11 mm(p < .001) immediately after IVL alone and CTA intraluminal volume increasing 52.7% (median). Haemodynamic improvement was observed (ankle brachial index: 0.80 to 1.00 (median); toe brachial index: 0.40 to 0.62 (median); p <.001) between baseline and 30 days. Intra-procedural dissections were detected in 18% of cases on IVUS; only two lesions (5%) were flow limiting and required stenting. At 30 days, no mortality or target lesion revascularisations were observed, while restenosis at 6 months occurred in 5% of cases. Chronic total occlusion was associated with residual stenosis in multivariable analysis (OR 6.2, 95% CI 1.11 - 34.48, p = .038). CONCLUSIONS: IVL was associated with modest apparent plaque modification and significant luminal gain in calcified femoropopliteal lesions. Combined CTA and IVUS imaging suggest luminal expansion is primarily driven by plaque fracture, altered vessel compliance, and remodelling rather than debulking.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) is designed to treat calcified peripheral arteries with steno-occlusive disease; however, its effect on plaque morphology remains incompletely understood in vivo. This study evaluated plaque modification and luminal changes following IVL in femoropopliteal disease using computed tomography angiography (CTA) and intravascular ultrasound (IVUS). METHODS: This was a prospective single centre observational study.

title: Safety of Janus kinase inhibitors, ustekinumab, and anti-interleukin-23 in older patients with immune-mediated diseases.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Data on the safety of newer advanced therapies (AT) for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs) remain limited in older patients, and how the underlying IMID type influences treatment safety is unknown. METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed/MEDLINE and Embase for studies evaluating the safety of anti-IL12/23 and -IL23 agents, and JAKi in older patients with IMIDs, including inflammatory bowel disease, rheumatoid arthritis, and psoriasis. Eligible studies included patients who initiated therapy at age ≥50 years and reported outcomes in comparison with (1) younger patients receiving the same therapy, (2) older patients receiving non-AT, or (3) older patients receiving a different AT. Data on infections, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), venous thromboembolism (VTE), malignancy, and mortality were extracted. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model. RESULTS: Seventy-nine studies were included. Compared to other AT, JAKi were associated with a higher risk of infections (OR 1.38; 95% CI, 1.22-1.55) and serious infections (1.27; 1.06-1.52). No increase in MACE, VTE, or malignancy risk was seen overall. Among adults > 60 years, there was an increased risk of VTE in rheumatologic cohorts (3.28; 1.16-9.27) that was absent in IBD (0.99; 0.58-1.70) (p for difference = 0.045). Compared with anti-TNF, Anti-IL-12/23 and -IL-23 agents had a lower risk of serious infections (0.76; 0.68-0.84). CONCLUSION: In older patients with IMIDs, anti-IL-12/23 and -IL-23 agents had lower serious infection risk while JAKi had an increased risk. JAKi showed a possible disease-specific thromboembolic signal in rheumatologic but not IBD cohorts.

title: COLLATERAL EMBOLIZATION IN THE ENDOVASCULAR TREATMENT OF PORTAL CAVERNOMA CHOLANGIOPATHY: A POTENTIAL CAUSE OF SEVERE BILIARY OBSTRUCTION.
abstract: Management of complicated portal cavernoma cholangiopathy (PCC) remains nonstandardized. When biliary drainage fails, portal vein recanalization with transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (PVR-TIPS) is increasingly considered and may require collateral embolization during the procedure. This work describes two patients with complicated PCC in whom collateral embolization during or after PVR-TIPS caused severe biliary obstruction requiring long-term biliary drainage. A narrative review was conducted, identifying 18 published studies describing patients with PCC who underwent endovascular treatment. Collateral embolization was inconsistently reported, and its biliary consequences were rarely described. Severe biliary obstruction following peribiliary collateral embolization may therefore be an underrecognized complication; however, its incidence remains unknown based on the available literature. Thus, when collateral embolization is considered during endovascular treatment of PCC, its potential biliary risk should be weighed, and the anatomical relationship between the targeted collaterals and the bile duct carefully assessed.

This work describes two patients with complicated PCC in whom collateral embolization during or after PVR-TIPS caused severe biliary obstruction requiring long-term biliary drainage.

title: Stent Configurations in Aortoiliac Occlusive disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate which endovascular stent configuration at the aortic bifurcation offers superior outcomes for aorto-iliac occlusive disease (AIOD). METHODS: Studies reporting outcomes for endovascular reconstruction for AIOD, for TransAtlantic Inter-Society Consensus (TASC) C and D lesions were included in the review. Data for primary, primary-assisted and secondary patency were extracted (full-text articles or reconstructed from published Kaplan Meier curves). RESULTS: This review included 12 studies, including 1027 patients (177 Covered Endovascular Reconstruction of the Aortic Bifurcation (CERAB), 850 kissing stent). Most studies were retrospective cohort studies with moderate methodological quality. Median follow-up was 20 months for primary patency, and 48 months for assisted and secondary patency. CERAB and kissing stent techniques showed similar primary patency (p=0.24). Primary-assisted patency was slightly lower for CERAB but not statistically significant (p=0.051). Secondary patency favored CERAB (p=0.045). At two years, CERAB had primary patency of 90%, primary-assisted patency of 87%, and secondary patency of 100%. Kissing stents showed primary patency of 91%, primary-assisted patency of 92%, and secondary patency of 96%. CONCLUSION: Both stent types yielded positive results, but current data does not favor one configuration. Current studies on this topic are low quality. At present, the method of endovascular intervention for AIOD could be left to clinical expertise, although hemodynamic studies may provide insights. Randomized trial data or post-market registries are needed to ascertain superiority of any stent configuration in this disease process.

METHODS: Studies reporting outcomes for endovascular reconstruction for AIOD, for TransAtlantic Inter-Society Consensus (TASC) C and D lesions were included in the review. Data for primary, primary-assisted and secondary patency were extracted (full-text articles or reconstructed from published Kaplan Meier curves).

title: Three working windows posterior midline approach for posterior column tibial plateau fractures.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Isolated posterior column tibial plateau fractures with combined posteromedial and posterolateral compression are challenging because conventional posterior approaches limit instrument trajectories and reduction vectors for distinct posterior fragments. METHODS: Ten patients with isolated posterior column tibial plateau fractures accompanied by combined posteromedial and posterolateral compression were treated using a posterior midline skin incision organized into three working windows. The central window served as the foundational posterior corridor, with medial and lateral windows developed as functional extensions to facilitate region-specific reduction and fixation. Relevant clinical data and outcomes were retrospectively analyzed. RESULTS: Postoperative radiographs of all 10 patients showed satisfactory joint reduction and alignment. Radiographic fracture union was achieved in all cases at a mean of 13.9 weeks, with a mean follow up of 11.8 months. At final follow up, mean knee flexion was 124.0°, and mean knee extension was -2.1°, and the mean Hospital for Special Surgery (HSS) knee score was 90.8 points. One patient developed a superficial wound infection that resolved with antibiotic treatment, and one patient experienced deep vein thrombosis that was successfully treated with anticoagulation therapy. No neurovascular injuries, deep infections, or fixation failures were observed during follow up. CONCLUSION: A posterior midline approach organized into three working windows may provide a feasible option for selected isolated posterior column tibial plateau fractures with combined posteromedial and posterolateral compression, allowing region-specific posterior fixation through a single posterior skin incision.

METHODS: Ten patients with isolated posterior column tibial plateau fractures accompanied by combined posteromedial and posterolateral compression were treated using a posterior midline skin incision organized into three working windows. The central window served as the foundational posterior corridor, with medial and lateral windows developed as functional extensions to facilitate region-specific reduction and fixation.

title: Fontan-associated liver disease: a Croatian national experience and current clinical practice.
abstract: AIM: To assess the characteristics of patients with Fontan-associated liver disease (FALD) and its clinical correlates within contemporary multidisciplinary practice at the national tertiary referral center in Croatia. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included all adult patients with Fontan circulation followed at University Hospital Centre Zagreb between 2023 and 2025. Data from the most recent comprehensive cardiology and hepatology evaluation were analyzed. Liver assessment included laboratory testing, transient elastography, and structured imaging surveillance with alternating ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging. Advanced FALD was defined as liver stiffness measurement (LSM)>22 kPa combined with indirect markers of portal hypertension. RESULTS: The study enrolled 37 adults (median age 24 years; 64.9% male), with a median of 21 years since Fontan completion. The median LSM was 18.5 kPa (interquartile range 14.6-23.1), and 27% of participants had LSM>22 kPa. Thrombocytopenia was present in 40.5% of patients. LSM was moderately negatively correlated with platelet count (Spearman's ρ=-0.490, P=0.0038). Conventional liver biochemistry was only mildly abnormal in most patients. One patient (2.7%) was diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma during surveillance and treated with locoregional therapy. CONCLUSION: FALD is common and clinically heterogeneous in adults with long-standing Fontan circulation, frequently affecting young patients decades after surgery. Conventional laboratory markers alone may underestimate disease severity. These findings support structured, multidisciplinary surveillance in this complex population. This first national experience from Croatia contributes region-specific data to the growing body of evidence on FALD.
englishSummary: AIM: To assess the characteristics of patients with Fontan-associated liver disease (FALD) and its clinical correlates within contemporary multidisciplinary practice at the national tertiary referral center in Croatia. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included all adult patients with Fontan circulation followed at University Hospital Centre Zagreb between 2023 and 2025. Data from the most recent comprehensive cardiology and hepatology evaluation were analyzed.

title: ChatGPT's and Claude's responses to patient questions on deep vein thrombosis.
abstract: AIM: To compare ChatGPT's and Claude's responses to frequently asked patient questions about deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in terms of expert-rated accuracy, comprehensibility, and unnecessary detail. METHODS: We compiled 33 Turkish questions about DVT from online sources and clinical experience. The questions were posed to ChatGPT and Claude in separate sessions, and the models' unedited responses were collected. Three blinded cardiovascular surgeons independently evaluated each answer on a 1-5 Likert scale across three domains: accuracy, comprehensibility, and unnecessary detail. We compared average answer lengths and domain scores using paired statistical tests. RESULTS: The mean lengths of the responses did not differ significantly between the models (139.7±49.4 words vs 145.67±25.41 words; P=0.490). ChatGPT had a higher median rater-averaged comprehensibility score (4.33 vs 4.00; raw P=0.002). In the principal rater-averaged analyses, the models did not significantly differ in accuracy (Holm-adjusted P=0.085), whereas ChatGPT received significantly higher scores for comprehensibility and unnecessary detail (Holm-adjusted P=0.006 for both). CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest potential differences in the presentation of patient-facing information rather than overall clinical superiority of any model. AI-generated medical information should continue to be reviewed by qualified health care professionals.

title: CDC48 protein regulates the turnover of peroxisomal catalase in tobacco.
abstract: In plant cells, protein homeostasis is tightly regulated to prevent imbalances between protein synthesis and degradation that can lead to proteotoxic stress. Protein turnover is largely maintained by the ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS), with the AAA+ ATPase CDC48 facilitating the extraction and processing of ubiquitinated substrates. Previous studies identified redox-related proteins as plant CDC48 partners. Here, using tobacco cell lines overexpressing CDC48, we identified the peroxisomal catalase CAT1 as a substrate of CDC48-dependent turnover. CDC48 overexpression markedly reduced CAT1 abundance and activity, indicating post-translational regulation. CAT1 undergoes extensive polyubiquitination, and was rapidly degraded in a CDC48-dependent manner. Inhibition of deubiquitinating enzymes or CDC48 ATPase activity both led to the accumulation of ubiquitinated CAT1. Finally, CDC48 overexpression, which leads to reduced CAT1 levels, correlated with impaired peroxisomal function. These findings reveal a role for CDC48 in regulating peroxisomal protein turnover in tobacco.

Previous studies identified redox-related proteins as plant CDC48 partners.

title: Bilateral Lateral Tarsal Artery Bypass and Free Flap Reconstruction of an Infected Gangrenous Heel in Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia: A Case Report of Three-Year Functional Limb Salvage.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Distal bypass for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) is technically demanding when the conventional pedal arteries are unavailable, and revascularization alone seldom heals an extensive heel defect. CASE PRESENTATION: A man in his 60s receiving maintenance hemodialysis presented with bilateral CLTI and gangrene of the left heel after failed endovascular therapy, and bilateral major amputations had been considered before referral. Both limbs were classified as Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection clinical stage 4. Diffuse calcification of the infrapopliteal and pedal arteries left the lateral tarsal artery (LTA) as the only suitable distal target, and bilateral superficial femoral artery-to-LTA bypasses were performed with in situ great saphenous vein grafts under nerve block anesthesia. Because repeated debridement left the calcaneus exposed, a free latissimus dorsi musculocutaneous flap anastomosed to the left bypass graft was transferred and covered with a split-thickness skin graft. The wounds healed after minor amputations, and the patient regained independent ambulation. An ulcer subsequently developed on the weight-bearing surface of the transferred flap and never healed despite pressure-relieving insoles and additional inflow angioplasty; nevertheless, the flap remained viable, both grafts remained patent, and ambulatory function was preserved until the patient died of an unrelated cause 3 years after revascularization. CONCLUSIONS: The LTA can serve as a distal bypass target when the conventional pedal arteries are unavailable, and, when combined with free flap reconstruction, it may achieve long-term functional limb salvage despite extensive heel gangrene. The reconstructed weight-bearing heel nevertheless remains prone to ulceration that may not heal, so preventive off-loading and long-term surveillance are essential.

title: Mechanical Thrombectomy of a Combined Persistent Primitive Trigeminal Artery and Basilar Artery Occlusion: A Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Persistent primitive trigeminal artery (PPTA) is a rare anastomosis between the internal carotid artery and the posterior circulation, most commonly with the basilar artery (BA). It has been associated with neurovascular diseases such as cerebral hemorrhage and ischemic stroke. Its occlusion in the case of ischemic stroke presents multiple challenges, both diagnostic and therapeutic, as the modified vascular anatomy may complicate the initial imaging diagnosis and endovascular treatment with mechanical thrombectomy (MT). CASE PRESENTATION: We report here the case of a 64-year-old woman presenting with an altered conscious status and bilateral mydriasis due to an occlusion of a PPTA and the distal part of the BA, which was treated with MT. Complete recanalization was obtained using combined contact aspiration and stent retriever thrombectomy through the PPTA. CONCLUSION: PPTA is a rare vascular anatomical variant whose knowledge is important in the setting of stroke. In this setting, MT appears to be a feasible, safe, and effective technique compared to other proximal sites of occlusion.

title: An In Vitro Study Simulating Prophylactic Anticoagulation in Haemophilia A and B.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Patients with haemophilia A (HA) and haemophilia B (HB) are at increased bleeding risk. A recent guidance document suggests considering pharmacological thromboprophylaxis on a case-by-case basis in these patients undergoing surgery at high-risk of venous thromboembolism. This study aimed to assess the effect of prophylactic doses of three anticoagulants (enoxaparin, rivaroxaban and unfractionated heparin [UFH]) on in vitro models of HA and HB. METHODS: FVIII- and FIX-deficient plasma were spiked with FVIII and FIX concentrates to mimic severe, moderate and mild HA (FVIII concentrations < 1%, 1.2% and 17.0%, respectively) and HB (FIX concentrations < 1%, 3.9% and 22.9%, respectively). Each pool was spiked with enoxaparin (concentration range 0.3-0.4 IU/mL), rivaroxaban (50-100 ng/mL) and UFH (0.2-0.3 IU/mL). The following assays were performed: prothrombin time (PT), activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) and thrombin generation (using the semi-automated fluorogenic calibrated automated thrombin generation assay [CAT]). RESULTS: The PT was not significantly affected by the anticoagulants. A significant prolongation of the APTT was observed; UFH showed the greatest increase, followed by rivaroxaban and enoxaparin. All anticoagulants impacted on the CAT curves. UFH showed the greatest reduction of the endogenous thrombin potential; rivaroxaban showed the greatest increase of lag time and time to peak. Peak thrombin and velocity index were similarly reduced by rivaroxaban and UFH, whereas enoxaparin was associated with smaller changes in all parameters. CONCLUSION: Trial Registration A significant effect of three prophylactic anticoagulants was observed in factor-deficient plasmas. This study provides further insight into this topic and supports the concept of an individualised approach to haemophilia patients.: The authors have confirmed clinical trial registration is not needed for this submission.

title: Impact of Balloon-Expandable Valve Asymmetry on Heart Failure Post Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Fluoroscopic assessment enables immediate evaluation of transcatheter heart valve expansion during transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Whether fluoroscopic asymmetric expansion of balloon-expandable valves is associated with post-TAVR heart failure (HF) remains uncertain. METHODS: Among 607 consecutive patients undergoing balloon-expandable valve-TAVR in a prospective registry, 589 were analyzed. Valve asymmetry was quantified using a fluoroscopic asymmetry index (%), defined as [(longest/shortest balloon-expandable valve height)-1]×100. The primary end point was 2-year HF hospitalization. RESULTS: P P P During follow-up, 99 patients (17%) experienced HF hospitalization. As a continuous variable, asymmetry index (%) was not independently associated with 2-year HF (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] per 1% increase, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.98-1.06]). Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated no significant linear or nonlinear association (overall=0.71;for nonlinearity=0.89), although the risk curve suggested increased HF risk beyond moderate valve asymmetry. Exploratory threshold analysis identified an asymmetry index cutoff of 7.48%. Patients above this threshold had a higher incidence of HF hospitalization than those below it (23.6% versus 15.8%; log-rank=0.043), despite comparable rates of impaired valve performance at discharge. Valve asymmetry >7.48% remained independently associated with late HF occurring beyond 30 days after TAVR (adjusted HR, 1.69 [95% CI, 1.10-2.60]). CONCLUSIONS: Fluoroscopic assessment of balloon-expandable valve expansion identified patients with marked valve asymmetry at increased risk of late HF after TAVR, despite preserved early valve performance. These findings support the potential value of intraprocedural valve geometry assessment for long-term risk stratification and warrant further investigation.

Whether fluoroscopic asymmetric expansion of balloon-expandable valves is associated with post-TAVR heart failure (HF) remains uncertain. title: Beyond Anatomy in Uncomplicated Type B Aortic Dissection: Hypoxia, Physiological Reserve, and the Next Generation of Intelligent Endovascular Devices.
abstract: Type B aortic dissection (TBAD) represents a heterogeneous disease process that cannot be fully understood through anatomy alone. Although the majority of patients initially meet current criteria for uncomplicated TBAD (uTBAD), a substantial proportion later progresses despite appearing stable during early assessment and surveillance. The mechanisms underlying this deterioration remain incompletely understood and extends beyond our current understanding of traditional anatomic high-risk criteria. This article examines impaired oxygenation and physiological reserve as potential dimensions of clinical vulnerability in uTBAD, while distinguishing their possible relevance to acute deterioration from their unproven value in predicting aortic progression or selecting patients for intervention. As such, TBAD is not simply a focal vascular event, but a disease with broader systemic and physiological implications. It also discusses how future intelligent endovascular technologies could support a more personalised approach to management by integrating embedded sensors, wireless physiological monitoring, and artificial intelligence-assisted haemodynamic analysis. Moreover, a conceptual framework is discussed in which the stent graft evolves from a purely mechanical device into an active therapeutic platform capable of physiological sensing and real-time feedback.

title: Haemodialysis in haemophilia B: a case report. Challenges and strategies from a nephrology perspective.
abstract: Haemophilia B, the result of factor IX deficiency, is a complex clinical condition that is particularly challenging when associated with kidney failure. This is primarily due to the high bleeding risk associated with kidney replacement therapies. The increase in life expectancy in haemophilia patients has resulted in a greater prevalence of age-related comorbidities, including chronic kidney disease. Nevertheless, a consensus has yet to be reached regarding the most suitable dialysis modality for this population. In this report, we present a case study of a 68-year-old male patient suffering from severe haemophilia B, who was administered prophylactic Idelvion® (albutrepenonacog alfa) and subsequently underwent arteriovenous fistula creation and haemodialysis initiation without encountering any bleeding complications. This narrative review, from the perspective of a nephrologist, addresses the epidemiology and main clinical considerations regarding dialysis in haemophilia B. These considerations include the choice between haemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis, vascular access planning, haemostasis management with factor IX replacement, and anticoagulation strategies aimed at minimising bleeding risk. A review of the extant literature and clinical reports published between 2020 and 2025 was conducted, integrating documented experiences and available guideline recommendations. In addition, we put forward a series of pragmatic recommendations that are -underpinned by a systematic decision-making framework. Through meticulous multidisciplinary planning incorporating the utilisation of factor IX concentrates, meticulous surgical techniques, and tailored anticoagulation protocols, patients with haemophilia B can be deemed eligible for chronic haemodialysis with a reasonable degree of safety.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of point-of-care ultrasound for proximal lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis in emergency settings: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of emergency clinician-performed ultrasound for proximal lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and explore variation by scan protocol and operator group.MethodsThis systematic review and meta-analysis included studies of adults with suspected DVT in emergency settings. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception to 8 April 2026, and a targeted literature update was conducted through 20 September 2026 during revision. A bivariate binomial random-effects model jointly estimated sensitivity and specificity. The primary analysis included one dataset per study to avoid duplicate weighting of paired cohorts. Risk of bias and applicability were assessed with QUADAS-2. Protocol and operator subgroup analyses were exploratory. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261361599).ResultsSixteen studies contributed quantitative data, providing 17 protocol datasets because one paired cohort was evaluated with both two-point and three-point protocols. Selecting the three-point result from that paired cohort for the primary overall model yielded 16 independent study datasets comprising 2,781 patient or limb/examination units. Pooled sensitivity was 0.91 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.85-0.95), and specificity was 0.95 (95% CI 0.91-0.97). Sensitivity estimates for two-point and three-point/extended protocols were 0.87 and 0.92, respectively. Source-data uncertainties, including a reconstructed diagnostic-analysis table in Jahanian 2019 and a provisional Crowhurst input, were examined in sensitivity analyses. Koylu 2026 was added during the revision-stage targeted literature update.ConclusionsEmergency clinician-performed ultrasound may support proximal DVT assessment within a defined diagnostic pathway. Negative limited examinations require interpretation alongside clinical probability and examination adequacy. Heterogeneity and unresolved source data limit confidence in the pooled estimates. Exploratory subgroup findings do not establish the superiority of any protocol or operator group.

title: T-cell states in aortic dissection: from molecular immune profiling toward causal and translational validation.
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Single-cell RNA sequencing and T-cell receptor profiling reveal substantial T-cell heterogeneity in aortic dissection (AD), but whether these responses contribute to vascular injury or reflect post-onset immune activation remains uncertain. This review evaluates human and experimental evidence by disease stage, tissue compartment, functional validation, T-cell specificity, and intervention timing, distinguishing descriptive profiling from evidence supporting causal and translational inference. DISCUSSION: + Human studies identify Th1/Th17-associated, CD8cytotoxicity-associated, and regulatory T-cell alterations, with stage-related differences in T-cell composition and clonality. Most evidence is cross-sectional and obtained after clinical onset. Antigen specificity, direct aortic-wall cytotoxicity, impaired Treg suppression, and T-cell-mediated aortic-wall injury remain unproven. Single-cell and TCR profiling identify candidate T-cell states and clonotypes for spatial and functional validation, not causal proof. Among candidate pathways, the IL-6-STAT3-IL-17 axis currently has the strongest AD-specific preclinical rationale, but existing interventions are largely non-T-cell-restricted and initiated before or during disease induction. Stronger causal attribution requires convergent human evidence, post-lesion T-cell-restricted perturbation, disease-progression endpoints, and rescue or target-engagement studies. The subacute phase after anatomical and haemodynamic stabilisation may offer a window to study persistent injury-amplifying T-cell responses, whereas early acute and perioperative immunomodulation remains unsupported. CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence supports altered T-cell states after AD onset but does not establish an initiating role. Near-term priorities should be prospective biomarker validation and post-lesion mechanistic studies rather than T-cell-directed immuno-modulation during the early acute and perioperative phases. Clinical translation should await reproducible associations linked to stage-specific causal mechanisms and acceptable safety.

title: Association between neuromuscular electrical stimulation and intermittent pneumatic compression for the prevention of deep venous thrombosis among neurosurgery patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) considerably affects the incidence and mortality rates in patients undergoing neurosurgery. Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) and intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) are frequently used as adjunct treatments to prevent DVT; however, their effects remain unclear. This study was conducted to compare the association of NMES and IPC as two mechanical prophylaxis strategies in neurosurgical patients who were ineligible for pharmacological prophylaxis. METHODS: Postoperative neurosurgical patients were retrospectively enrolled from a single centre between January 2020 and December 2021. These patients were assessed to have a high bleeding risk and received either NMES or IPC as mechanical prophylaxis. Univariable analysis was used to explore the risk factors for DVT, and multivariable logistic regression analysis was used to determine the independent associations between DVT and potential variables after adjusting for confounding factors. RESULTS: p p p p Among 232 patients who underwent neurosurgery, 131 received IPC and 101 received NMES, with no overlap between the two groups. DVT was diagnosed in 62 patients (11 received NMES and 51 received IPC). After controlling for sex, age, operation duration and length of hospital stay, NMES use was associated with a lower incidence of DVT (OR = 0.268, 95% CI = 0.125-0.576, = .001). Moreover, men were less likely to have DVT than women (OR = 0.469, 95% CI = 0.242-0.910, = .025), older age was associated with higher odds of DVT (OR = 3.419, 95% CI = 1.594-7.334, = .002), and a longer operation duration was associated with higher odds of DVT (OR = 2.180, 95% CI = 1.042-4.560, = .039). CONCLUSION: This study found an association between NMES and reduced odds of DVT compared with IPC in neurosurgery patients. Although NMES may be more widely adopted in neurosurgery to decrease the incidence of DVT, further evidence is required to determine its effectiveness in clinical practice.

title: Adipsic Hypernatremia Complicated by Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State and Extensive Venous Thromboembolism After Traumatic Brain Injury: A Case Report.
abstract: Adipsic hypernatremia is a rare disorder characterized by impaired thirst perception despite severe hyperosmolality, most commonly resulting from hypothalamic dysfunction. Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state (HHS) may further aggravate dehydration and electrolyte imbalance, increasing the risk of neurologic injury, acute kidney injury (AKI), and thromboembolic complications. Reports describing the coexistence of adipsic hypernatremia, HHS, and extensive venous thromboembolism are limited. A 42-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes and recent traumatic brain injury presented with neurologic decline, severe dehydration without thirst, severe hypernatremia, HHS, and transient renal dysfunction consistent with prerenal injury. Persistent severe hypernatremia despite improvement in hyperglycemia, together with preserved urinary concentrating ability, supported adipsic hypernatremia. Further evaluation revealed extensive deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and bilateral pulmonary embolism (PE), while brain imaging showed only mild diffuse cerebral atrophy. The patient was treated with controlled volume and free-water replacement, intravenous insulin therapy, anticoagulation, and close monitoring of serum sodium, glucose, renal function, and urine output. Gradual correction of hypernatremia resulted in significant improvement in neurologic manifestations, renal function, and metabolic abnormalities. Following stabilization, he was discharged on apixaban therapy with scheduled oral hydration instructions and outpatient follow-up. This case highlights a possible synergistic interaction between adipsic hypernatremia and HHS, which may have contributed to severe hyperosmolar stress and extensive thromboembolic complications. Adipsic hypernatremia should be considered in patients with severe hypernatremia and absent thirst sensation, particularly after traumatic brain injury, even when neuroimaging findings are unremarkable.

Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state (HHS) may further aggravate dehydration and electrolyte imbalance, increasing the risk of neurologic injury, acute kidney injury (AKI), and thromboembolic complications. Reports describing the coexistence of adipsic hypernatremia, HHS, and extensive venous thromboembolism are limited.

title: Sex-based differences in fibrosis markers in human abdominal aortic aneurysms.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA) are a complex degenerative vascular disease. The role of fibrosis in AAA progression is unclear. Our study evaluated the impact of fibroblast activation protein (FAP), collagen, and vimentin on AAA fibrosis and progression. We hypothesized that FAP may influence fibrosis and disease severity in AAA, with potential sex-specific differences. STUDY DESIGN: Multi-centered transcriptomic analysis of aortic samples from 15 human AAA and 5 non-AAA was performed to evaluate cell-specific fibrosis gene expression profiles. Histopathological and molecular analysis of 26 male and female AAA samples (mAAA and fAAA) and 29 male and female normal abdominal aortas (mNAA and fNAA) was performed to assess whole-tissue fibrosis markers and signaling. RESULTS: FAP COL1A1 Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis identified eight major cell clusters with distinct sex-based distributions. Although vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) and fibroblast clusters had reduced counts in both male and female AAAs, they more highly expressedandgenes, particularly in females. Whole-tissue analysis demonstrated elevated extracellular matrix deposits with markedly increased collagen type 1 in both mAAA and fAAA. Alpha-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA)-positive VSMCs were also reduced in mAAA and fAAA, but FAP was notably elevated, and robustly in fAAA. FAP-positive fibroblasts in fAAA exhibited increased expression of fibrosis markers, suggesting a unique pro-fibrotic phenotype. CONCLUSION: Our study reveals a sex-based difference in AAA tissue, with elevated fibrosis markers and increased FAP levels in females, suggesting its significant role in disease progression. These findings underscore the potential of FAP as a unique tissue biomarker for AAAs and warrants further investigation into novel targeted therapies that aim to stabilize AAAs, particularly in female patients.

title: Prognostic Value of the Frailty Index in Patients with Severe Aortic Regurgitation Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Frailty represents a multidimensional vulnerability that predicts poor outcomes in cardiovascular disease. Its prognostic value in patients with severe native aortic regurgitation (AR) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is not well defined. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether an abbreviated cumulative deficit frailty index predicts one-year all-cause mortality and to explore its interaction with N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide in this population. METHODS: In this post hoc analysis of the prospective China DVD2 multicenter cohort, 298 patients with isolated severe AR who underwent TAVR were included. Frailty was assessed preprocedurally using an abbreviated 8-9-item cumulative deficit frailty index (FI) encompassing functional, cognitive, nutritional, and clinical domains. The primary endpoint was one-year all-cause mortality. The cohort-derived FI threshold for mortality was derived using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis. Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, atrial fibrillation, and NT-proBNP were applied. Subgroup and interaction analyses were performed. RESULTS: The cohort-derived FI threshold was 0.407, classifying 32 patients as high frailty. High-FI patients exhibited greater symptom burden, higher prevalence of atrial fibrillation, larger left atrial diameter, and elevated NT-proBNP. One-year mortality was significantly higher in the high-FI group compared with low-FI patients (15.6% vs 3.4%, P = 0.010). High FI was associated with higher one-year mortality in Model 3 (HR 4.00, 95% CI 1.18-13.50; P = 0.026). No significant multiplicative or additive interaction with NT-proBNP was observed. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing TAVR for severe native aortic regurgitation, a high FI was associated with higher one-year mortality. These findings extend prior evidence on the prognostic implications of frailty to this understudied population.

Its prognostic value in patients with severe native aortic regurgitation (AR) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is not well defined. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether an abbreviated cumulative deficit frailty index predicts one-year all-cause mortality and to explore its interaction with N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide in this population.

title: Imaging in tarsal tunnel syndrome: A case series.
abstract: Tarsal tunnel syndrome is an under-recognized yet potentially debilitating entrapment neuropathy that is often misdiagnosed due to its non-specific clinical presentation. This case series presents four representative cases of space-occupying lesions within the tarsal tunnel - ganglion cysts, varicose veins, lipomas, and peripheral nerve sheath tumors - with emphasis on high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging and complementary radiographic and ultrasound findings. We demonstrate the characteristic imaging hallmarks of these lesions, including their mass effect on the tibial neurovascular bundle, signal intensities, and enhancement patterns, to aid clinicians and radiologists in timely recognition of this condition.

title: Clinical outcomes of total endovascular aortic arch repair by in situ microneedle fenestration using the triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique.
abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate the outcomes of total endovascular aortic arch repair (TEAAR) via in situ micro-needle fenestration (ISMNF) with the triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective study, the data of consecutive patients who underwent TEAAR via ISMNF with triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique between August 2022 and April 2025 were analyzed. Three 6-Fr, 90-cm sheaths were placed into ascending aorta without removing the dilator and super-stiff guidewires during main stent-graft deployment. This configuration creates a gutter between the stent-graft and aortic wall to maintain perfusion to supra-aortic branches. Operative details, technical success, 30-day and midterm outcomes, and adverse events were recorded. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to estimate freedom from all-cause death and reintervention. RESULTS: Overall, 36 patients were included. The technical success rate was 94.4% (34/36). Endovascular reconstruction of cervical branches was successfully performed in all cases. The 30-day mortality was 2.8%. The median follow-up period was 19 months (range, 1-32 months). The all-cause death rate was 11.1% (4/36), with no cases of any aorta-related death. The prevalence of endoleaks during follow-up was 13.9% (5/36). The overall stroke rate was 8.3% (3/36). The 1- and 2-year survival rates were 97.3% ± 2.7% and 85.8% ± 8.1%, respectively. The cumulative rate of freedom from reintervention at 1 and 2 years was 87.5% ± 5.9% and 83.2% ± 7.0%, respectively. CONCLUSION: TEAAR via ISMNF with the triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique was performed with a 94% technical success rate and stroke risk similar to open surgery.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective study, the data of consecutive patients who underwent TEAAR via ISMNF with triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique between August 2022 and April 2025 were analyzed. Three 6-Fr, 90-cm sheaths were placed into ascending aorta without removing the dilator and super-stiff guidewires during main stent-graft deployment.

title: Characteristics of treatment responses to physical exercise and diet in diabetic peripheral artery disease patients: a systematic review.
abstract: PURPOSE: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) affects walking performance and increases risk of amputation. Diabetes mellitus (DM) not only contributes to disease progression but may also affect treatment effects. Though physical exercise is crucial in PAD management and diet optimization may reduce risk of atherosclerosis, their effects and variations in diabetic PAD patients remain unclear. The present systematic review aims to summarize features of treatment response to physical exercise and diet management in diabetic PAD patients, and provide crucial information on optimization of PAD management of these patients in clinical practice. METHODS: A systematic review was performed on human studies investigating effects of physical exercise and diet on development and improvement of diabetic PAD patients by searching PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and CINAHL. The review was performed according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analysis (PRISMA). The certainty level of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE). RESULTS: A total of 18 studies were included, 15 of which evaluated effects of exercise on diabetic PAD, and three evaluated correlation between diet and diabetic PAD. Supervised exercise therapy (SET) and home-based exercise were able to improve ankle-brachial index (ABI) and blood flow velocity in diabetic PAD. In contrast, walking performance such as the six minute walk distance (6MWD), maximal walking time and distance, peak walking time (PWT) and claudication onset time (COT) were not significantly improved or presented conflicting results. Administration of multiple exercises or alternative interventions such as shock wave therapy or low-frequency pulsed electromagnetic field therapy (LFPMT) may enhance improvement of ABI. Adherence to Mediterranean diet was associated with blood flow and intermittent claudication, as well as risk of development of PAD. GRADE analysis revealed very low to moderate grade evidence for findings on ABI, flow velocity and functions, mainly due to study types, number of studies available, small sample size, moderate risk of bias and conflicting results. Similarly, low grade evidence was also revealed for effects and association of diet on risk of PAD due to study type and number of studies available. CONCLUSION: Diabetic PAD patients may present reduced treatment response to physical exercise in walking performance and other functions, which may be improved by combination of multiple physical exercises or alternative interventions with or without combination of exercise. Mediterranean diet may be associated with beneficial effects, which requires further investigations. These findings were of very low to moderate level of certainty, and therefore, further validation is warranted in the future.

Though physical exercise is crucial in PAD management and diet optimization may reduce risk of atherosclerosis, their effects and variations in diabetic PAD patients remain unclear.

title: Dissecting cell-type-specific genetic associations between colorectal cancer liability and thrombotic risk in peripheral blood immune cells.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major complication of colorectal cancer (CRC), but whether CRC-associated thrombotic susceptibility includes cell-specific inherited regulatory components in peripheral blood remains unclear. To investigate associations between CRC genetic liability and VTE-related outcomes within peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) regulatory contexts. We integrated CRC GWAS, FinnGen VTE-related outcomes, and TenK10K PBMC single-cell eQTL data across 28 immune cell types using cell-stratified Mendelian randomization (csMR). Prioritized signals were further examined in single-cell RNA-seq datasets and bulk transcriptomes. Conventional MR showed no clear evidence that CRC liability increased VTE, DVT, or PE risk, and LD Score regression detected no significant genome-wide genetic correlation. In contrast, csMR identified nominal, cell-context-dependent associations. B intermediate cells were prioritized across VTE (OR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.03-1.32), DVT (OR, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.08-1.57), and PE (OR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.07-1.49), while CD14 + monocytes and CD4 + central memory T cells received additional support from downstream single-cell analyses. Gene-level analyses prioritized LAMA5, LIMA1, and TRIM28 in these respective cell contexts. In bulk blood, RPS21 showed consistent disease-associated expression patterns and discriminated VTE patients from healthy controls in an external dataset (AUC, 0.865; 95% CI, 0.800-0.923). These findings suggest that genetic overlap between CRC liability and thrombotic phenotypes may be localized to selected PBMC regulatory contexts rather than broadly detectable genome-wide. Among the prioritized signals, B intermediate cells showed the most consistent csMR associations across VTE, DVT, and PE. The cell-gene pairs, together with RPS21, warrant independent genetic, functional, and prospective validation as candidates for studying peripheral immune regulation and blood-based markers of CRC-associated thrombosis.

We integrated CRC GWAS, FinnGen VTE-related outcomes, and TenK10K PBMC single-cell eQTL data across 28 immune cell types using cell-stratified Mendelian randomization (csMR).

title: L5 Corpectomy in a 12-Year-Old Owing to Rosai-Dorfman Disease: A Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Rosai-Dorfman disease (RDD) is a rare non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis typically presenting with massive, painless lymphadenopathy or subcutaneous masses. Extranodal involvement, particularly in the spine, is exceedingly rare and poses significant diagnostic and management challenges. Lumbar spinal RDD with vertebral collapse and neurological compromise is almost unheard of in the pediatric population, with no prior reports of surgical intervention requiring L5 corpectomy and circumferential fusion in an adolescent. CASE DESCRIPTION: We present a case of a 12-year-old girl with a 6-month history of worsening lower back pain unresponsive to conservative treatment. Imaging revealed collapse of the L5 vertebral body and a destructive, enhancing lesion encasing the neural elements, leading to severe canal and foraminal stenosis. Computed tomography-guided biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of RDD. A multidisciplinary surgical team implemented a 2-stage circumferential surgical plan. Stage 1 involved posterior decompression and posterior instrumentation from L3 to the pelvis using S2AI screws. A silastic barrier was placed to protect neural elements. Stage 2, performed via an anterior approach with vascular surgery assistance, involved complete corpectomy of L5 and reconstruction with an expandable cage spanning L4 to S1. Postoperative recovery was uneventful, and the patient remained neurologically intact. At 1-year follow-up, the patient demonstrated solid anterior and posterior fusion, maintained spinal alignment, and had returned to full activity. CONCLUSION: This is the first reported case of pediatric RDD requiring an L5 corpectomy with circumferential spinal fusion. The case underscores the importance of early tissue diagnosis, individualized surgical planning, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Recognition of RDD as a potential etiology for pediatric spinal lesions is critical, particularly when imaging mimics malignancy. Our successful outcome supports the use of staged, tailored surgical approaches in managing rare spinal pathologies in children.

title: Routine Chest CTA Reliably Quantifies Left Ventricular Myocardial Mass.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Routine chest computed tomography angiography (CTA) is the primary imaging modality for thoracic aortic disease, yet cardiac information within these examinations remains underutilized. We evaluated whether left ventricular myocardial mass (LVMM) can be reliably quantified from routine non-electrocardiographically (ECG)-gated chest CTA and its application in thoracic aortic pathology. METHODS: CTA scans were obtained from 257 patients without aortic disease and 181 patients with thoracic aortic aneurysm or dissection. LVMM was quantified using automated three-dimensional segmentation. In a separate 10-patient validation cohort, LVMM was compared across end-systolic, end-diastolic, and non-ECG-gated source reconstructions. CTA-derived LVMM was compared with published echocardiographic and cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) reference values using Cohen's d. RESULTS: d d d d p p LVMM remained stable across cardiac phases and non-ECG-gated images (mean coefficient of variation, 2.4%), whereas left ventricular volume varied substantially (36.9%). CTA-derived LVMM demonstrated small effect sizes with the Penn method (= 0.22) and moderate effect sizes with ASE linear (= 0.67), area-length (= 0.68), and CMR (= 0.63). LVMM increased through young adulthood, with minimal association with age beyond 30 years. LVMM was comparable between patients with thoracic aneurysms and normal adults (140 ± 43 g vs. 141 ± 40 g; adjusted= 1.0) but significantly greater in acute (199 ± 61 g) and chronic (191 ± 57 g) aortic dissection (both adjusted< 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Routine non-ECG-gated chest CTA enables reliable automated LVMM quantification without additional imaging or radiation and may facilitate large-scale investigations of ventricular remodeling in thoracic aortic disease.

We evaluated whether left ventricular myocardial mass (LVMM) can be reliably quantified from routine non-electrocardiographically (ECG)-gated chest CTA and its application in thoracic aortic pathology. METHODS: CTA scans were obtained from 257 patients without aortic disease and 181 patients with thoracic aortic aneurysm or dissection.

title: Maternal Mortality Across a Multi-Hospital Health System in Saudi Arabia: A Retrospective Study (2016-2024).
abstract: BACKGROUND: Maternal mortality remains a pressing global health challenge and is a vital indicator of healthcare quality. Despite improvements in Saudi Arabia, preventable maternal fatalities continue to occur, with insufficient research on regional disparities. OBJECTIVE: This study seeks to assess the maternal mortality ratio (MMR) and its causes across five hospitals within the Ministry of National Guard Health Affairs in Saudi Arabia and evaluate it is main causes,thereby addressing a gap in maternal mortality data in the Gulf region. METHODS: This retrospective, multicenter, descriptive study included all maternal deaths occurring during pregnancy or within 42 days postpartum between 2016 and 2024 across five National Guard hospitals in Riyadh, Jeddah, Madinah, Al-Ahsa, and Dammam. Data were extracted from hospital records and analyzed descriptively using SPSS version 28. RESULTS: Eighteen maternal deaths were identified over the nine-year period, yielding an overall MMR of 6.2 per 100,000 live births (mean age at death 29.8 ± 6.3 years). MMR varied considerably by year, from 0.00/100,000 in 2017 to 37.5/100,000 in 2020. Pregnancy-related complications accounted for 50% of deaths (9/18), most commonly venous thromboembolism (66.7%). Non-obstetric causes included COVID-19 (16.7%), unknown cause (16.7%), brain tumor (5.6%), and myocarditis (5.6%). Most deaths occurred in women with parity 1-3 (61.1%), split evenly between vaginal and caesarean delivery (50% each). Geographic variation was marked: Riyadh recorded deaths in most years with a peak in 2020; Dammam and Al-Ahsa each showed sporadic extreme spikes; Jeddah showed intermittent elevations; no deaths occurred in Madinah. CONCLUSION: The overall MMR at these hospitals is comparatively low to global figures, significant variations across different cities and years, alongside a notable number of deaths with unspecified causes, underscore the need for standardized mortality reviews, autopsy confirmations for suspected embolic deaths, and continuous targeted monitoring.

title: Comparison of Peripherally Inserted Central Catheters versus Central Venous Catheters in a Medical Intensive Care Unit: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients in medical intensive care units (MICUs) often require prolonged intravenous therapy, making optimal catheter selection critical. While central venous catheters (CVCs) remain common, peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs) are increasingly used. This single-centre retrospective study compared indwelling time, clinical utility, and complication profiles between PICCs and CVCs in MICU patients. METHODS: We analyzed 276 MICU patients with either a PICC or CVC, comparing catheter selection, length of stay, dwell time, and complication rates. Complication rates were also standardized per 1000 catheter-days. RESULTS: P P P P P P P P P P P P PICCs were used more frequently in patients with malignancy (< 0.001) or requiring chemotherapy (< 0.001), whereas CVCs were preferred in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (= 0.012), diabetes (= 0.012), COVID-19 (= 0.020), or vasopressor infusion (= 0.001). PICCs were associated with longer indwelling times (≥12 days,< 0.001). In the unstandardized analysis, PICCs had higher rates of catheter dislodgement (< 0.001) and occlusion (= 0.005), but lower rates of puncture-site complications (bleeding, hypersensitivity, fluid leakage; all< 0.05) and deep vein thrombosis incidence (= 0.038). After standardization per 1,000 catheter-days, dislodgement remained significantly more frequent with PICCs, whereas the difference in occlusion was no longer statistically significant. No bloodstream infections occurred with PICCs, versus 5.4% with CVCs (= 0.169). Because groups differed substantially in patient selection, clinical indication, dwell time, insertion site, and securement method, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than evidence of superiority. CONCLUSION: PICCs were associated with longer indwelling times and a higher rate of dislodgement, but lower rates of puncture-site complications and deep vein thrombosis; the difference in occlusion was no longer significant after standardization. Vascular access selection should be individualized according to patient characteristics, therapy requirements, anticipated duration, and device-related risks.

title: Age-adjusted and probability-adjusted D-dimer thresholds for the diagnosis of acute DVT: a narrative review.
abstract: In patients presenting to emergency departments with symptoms of lower-limb deep vein thrombosis (DVT), systematically ordering a compression ultrasonography (CUS) in all to rule out DVT contributes to crowding and low-yield testing. Contemporary diagnostic strategies aim at improving efficiency by avoiding the need for a CUS, while maintaining safety, as assessed by low short-term venous thromboembolism (VTE) rates among patients with a negative diagnostic work-up. This narrative review summarizes recent evidence, mainly from prospective management studies, supporting refined D-dimer-based pathways for first-episode DVT, and emerging data in patients with suspected recurrent DVT. In ADJUST-DVT, an age-adjusted D-dimer threshold (age×10 μg/L for ≥50 years) applied to outpatients with a non-high/unlikely pretest probability increased the proportion of patients ruled out without ultrasound by 7% overall as compared with the conventional 500 μg/L cutoff, with the largest gains in those ≥75 years. No failures were identified in patients with a D-dimer level 500 μg/L or greater but below the age-adjusted cutoff (0%, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0%-2.3%). In the 4D study, a clinical probability-adjusted D-dimer strategy (low Wells with D-dimer <1000 μg/L; moderate Wells with <500 μg/L) achieved a 0.6% 3-month VTE rate while reducing ultrasound use by 47%. In patients with a suspected recurrent ipsilateral DVT, D-dimer levels are often higher than in patients without previous DVT and are therefore less useful to exclude the disease. In this situation, a negative D-dimer test may also be associated with a higher failure rate. Indeed, in the PREDICTORS study, a higher-than-expected prevalence of recurrent VTE at presentation in patients with a non-high pretest probability and a negative D-dimer was reported. While CUS is also frequently non-diagnostic due to residual thrombi, the THEIA Study showed that magnetic resonance direct thrombus imaging (MRDTI) can safely guide management as a single test. Together, these studies support practical, outcome-validated approaches that improve diagnostic efficiency and may facilitate implementation in real-world workflows, while highlighting the need for accurate pretest assessment and continued prospective validation of simplified algorithms.

Contemporary diagnostic strategies aim at improving efficiency by avoiding the need for a CUS, while maintaining safety, as assessed by low short-term venous thromboembolism (VTE) rates among patients with a negative diagnostic work-up. This narrative review summarizes recent evidence, mainly from prospective management studies, supporting refined D-dimer-based pathways for first-episode DVT, and emerging data in patients with suspected recurrent DVT.

title: Endovascular management of acute and chronic arterial mesenteric ischaemia: A narrative review of evidence informing interventional radiology treatment.
abstract: Mesenteric ischaemia is a potentially life-threatening vascular disorder caused by impaired intestinal perfusion, with treatment selection requiring consideration of clinical presentation, bowel viability and lesion anatomy. This narrative review examines evidence informing interventional radiology decisions in arterial acute mesenteric ischaemia (AMI) and chronic mesenteric ischaemia (CMI). MEDLINE/PubMed was searched from inception to December 31, 2025, supplemented by reference-list screening and targeted guideline searches. Qualitative evidence synthesis considered patient selection, study design, adjunctive treatments, outcomes and follow-up. In AMI, endovascular techniques can restore perfusion, but predominantly retrospective evidence does not establish superiority over surgery in bowel preservation or survival. For CMI requiring revascularisation, European Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines recommend an initial endovascular approach, supported by Cardiovascular and Interventional Radiological Society of Europe consensus-based guidance. Observational comparisons associate endovascular treatment with lower perioperative morbidity, and surgery with less symptom recurrence. By linking individual treatment decisions to society guidance and supporting studies, this review complements existing comprehensive reviews and guidance documents. It distinguishes formal recommendations and consensus-based practice from technical feasibility and demonstrated comparative patient benefit, while identifying unresolved questions concerning AMI reperfusion strategies and device selection, in addition to antithrombotic therapy and restenosis management in CMI.
