title: Pseudodominant inheritance in paraplegin (SPG7)-associated CPEO-ataxia syndrome.
abstract: SPG7 encodes paraplegin, a mitochondrial AAA-metalloprotease critical for inner mitochondrial membrane protein quality control. Pathogenic variants most commonly cause autosomal recessive hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP) but its phenotypic spectrum includes cerebellar ataxia, progressive external ophthalmoplegia, myopathy and parkinsonism.We report a 47 year old man presenting with a progressive external ophthalmoplegia, ptosis, progressive gait disturbance, and spasticity. Ten-year follow-up of this individual showed slowly progressive spastic ataxia with ocular motor involvement and neurogenic bladder. His mother and maternal aunt both had marked spasticity, ataxia, ptosis and external ophthalmoplegia. Genetic testing demonstrated compound heterozygous pathogenic variants in paraplegin in this individual. Genetic testing in his mother and aunt revealed homozygous canonical splice-site variants (c.2182-2 A > G). Cascade testing of his asymptomatic father showed a common pathogenic missense variant p.(Ala510Val) in the same gene.This family demonstrates a pseudodominant inheritance pattern, instead of the expected autosomal recessive trait that applies to paraplegin. We highlight diagnostic pitfalls in relying on family history and assumed inheritance traits. We emphasise the importance of segregation analysis and comprehensive genomic testing. Recognition of pseudodominance inheritance has important implications for genetic counselling, family planning and cascade testing.

title: Development of a machine learning model to predict venous thromboembolism risk in women using combined oral contraceptives.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality, with combined oral contraceptives (COCPs) being a modifiable risk factor. Existing clinical tools have limited ability to capture complex predictor interactions. This study aimed to develop and evaluate machine learning (ML) models to predict VTE risk among COCP users. METHODS: This study was conducted using data from the Saudi Real-World Evidence Network (2016–2023). The primary outcome was the first VTE event within 2 years of COCP initiation. Following data partitioning, feature selection was performed on the training set. Elastic-net logistic regression, random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), one-class support vector machine and Isolation-Forest were trained on original and resampled datasets. Performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and F1 score. RESULTS: The cohort included 24 518 treatment episodes (n=17 512, VTE events=52). After handling class imbalance, RF and XGBoost were the best-performing models (F1: 84.3% and 81.6%; AUROC: 59.6% and 69.2%, respectively), compared with other models (F1: 2.6%–55.3%, AUROC: 54.2%–68.4%). Key predictors included age, glucocorticoid use and rheumatic, renal and thyroid diseases. DISCUSSION: ML shows potential for VTE risk detection despite low event rate and class imbalance. However, findings suggest synthetic sample overfitting, and external validation is warranted before clinical deployment. Identified predictors reinforce the role of metabolic and inflammatory factors in VTE susceptibility among COCP users. CONCLUSION: ML models, particularly XGBoost and RF, demonstrated moderate predictive ability for VTE among COCP users, supporting their use in individualised risk assessments, though external validation is warranted.

title: Association of circumferential dissection on computed tomography angiography with preoperative rupture in type A aortic dissection.
abstract: BACKGROUND: To investigate the association between circumferential dissection on computed tomography angiography (CTA) and preoperative rupture in patients with type A aortic dissection (TAAD). METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 597 consecutive patients diagnosed with TAAD at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024. Patients were classified into circumferential dissection (n = 130) and non-circumferential dissection (n = 467) groups based on preoperative CTA. Clinical, laboratory, and imaging characteristics were compared between groups. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to examine factors independently associated with preoperative rupture, and between-group differences in preoperative rupture were compared. RESULTS: Circumferential dissection was strongly associated with DeBakey type I dissection, supra-aortic branch involvement, and greater false-lumen expansion with true-lumen compression. Preoperative rupture occurred more frequently in patients with circumferential dissection than in those without (33.8% vs 7.1%, P < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression demonstrated that circumferential dissection was independently associated with preoperative rupture ascertained by bedside echocardiography following the admission CTA after adjustment for demographic, laboratory, and imaging factors (OR = 5.24, 95% CI: 1.86-14.76, P = 0.002). CONCLUSION: Circumferential dissection on CTA is independently associated with preoperative rupture and may support timely surgical decision-making in TAAD.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 597 consecutive patients diagnosed with TAAD at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024. Patients were classified into circumferential dissection (n = 130) and non-circumferential dissection (n = 467) groups based on preoperative CTA.

title: Machine learning models for predicting futile recanalisation after endovascular treatment in patients with large core infarction.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Predicting futile recanalisation following endovascular treatment (EVT) in patients with large core infarctions is crucial for guiding clinical decisions, optimising perioperative management and improving healthcare resource allocation. This study aimed to compare four machine learning (ML) algorithms and identify the most effective model for preinterventional prediction of futile recanalisation. METHODS: Patients achieving successful reperfusion (expanded Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction Score≥2b) from the EVT in Acute Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusive Patients With a Large Infarct Core trial were stratified into two groups: no-futile recanalisation (90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) 0–3) and futile recanalisation (mRS 4–6). The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression method was used for feature selection, and four ML algorithms, including logistic regression, support vector machine (SVM), decision tree and random forest, were applied. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration plots and decision curve analysis. Feature importance was ranked using SHapley Additive exPlanation (SHAP) values. RESULTS: Among 146 patients, 74 experienced futile recanalisation. Eight predictors were identified and ranked by SHAP analysis from highest to lowest importance: sex, age, National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale, glucose, systolic blood pressure, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, fibrinogen and occlusion site. Among the four models, the SVM model achieved the highest area under the curve of 0.891 (95% CI 0.837 to 0.945), along with good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow test, p=0.103) and clinical utility. CONCLUSION: The SVM model emerges as the optimal predictive tool for futile recanalisation following EVT in patients with large core infarction. Nevertheless, external validation is required to confirm its performance before clinical application. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT04551664.

title: Factors associated with infarct volume growth after mechanical thrombectomy in large core infarction: ANGEL-ASPECT insights.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Infarct volume growth (IVG) correlates with outcomes and may represent a prognostic imaging biomarker in acute ischaemic stroke due to anterior circulation large vessel occlusion (LVO). This study aims to identify factors associated with IVG after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in patients with large core infarction. METHODS: This is a post hoc analysis of the Endovascular Therapy in Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusion with a Large Infarct randomised trial. IVG was calculated as final infarct volume minus baseline infarct volume (BIV). The optimal IVG threshold for predicting 90-day favourable outcomes (modified Rankin Scale score 0–3) was determined using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, maximising both sensitivity and specificity. Factors associated with IVG were identified using multivariate logistic regression analyses. RESULTS: Among 228 included patients, ROC analysis identified an optimal IVG threshold of 105 mL for predicting favourable 90-day outcomes (area under the curve=0.71; specificity=0.85, sensitivity=0.53). Patients were stratified into mild (IVG <105 mL, n=150) and severe (IVG ≥105 mL, n=78) groups. Multivariate logistic regression identified BIV (OR 1.02, 95% CI 1.00 to 1.03; p<0.01), admission blood glucose (OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.04 to 1.37; p=0.01), time from puncture to recanalisation (OR 1.01, 95% CI 1.00 to 1.02; p=0.049) and recanalisation at 36 hours (±12 hours) (OR 0.19, 95% CI 0.05 to 0.72; p=0.01) as independent factors associated with IVG. CONCLUSION: IVG after MT significantly correlates with clinical outcomes. Identification of modifiable IVG determinants after MT may inform periprocedural management strategies in patients with large infarct due to LVO. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT04551664.

METHODS: This is a post hoc analysis of the Endovascular Therapy in Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusion with a Large Infarct randomised trial.

title: Early Staged STABILISE Technique Achieves Favorable Aortic Remodeling after Central Repair for Acute Type A Aortic Dissection.
abstract: Residual distal aortic dissection often persists after repair of acute type A aortic dissection, and may cause progressive aortic enlargement requiring secondary intervention. We describe a 43-year-old male who underwent an early staged stent-assisted balloon-induced intimal disruption and relamination in aortic dissection repair (STABILISE)-thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) procedure after central repair for an acute type A aortic dissection. Early postoperative computed tomography angiography demonstrated persistent false lumen perfusion, progressive false lumen enlargement, and marked true lumen compression. Thirty-eight days postoperatively, staged STABILISE-TEVAR was performed. Early staged STABILISE-TEVAR was technically feasible and achieved favorable aortic remodeling at 12 months in this patient.

title: Personalised approach to venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in heavier critically ill patients (PROSPER): A randomised, parallel-group, electronic medical record (EMR)-embedded feasibility trial.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Data are limited regarding optimal low molecular weight heparin dosing for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in heavier critically ill patients. This trial evaluated the feasibility of a weight-based dynamic dosing algorithm. DESIGN SETTING PARTICIPANTS: Open-label, electronic medical record-embedded randomised feasibility trial. Patients, weighing ≥100 kg who required thromboprophylaxis were eligible. Enoxaparin was commenced with weight-based dosing and anti-Xa level-guided adjustment (target peak anti-Xa level 0.2-0.4 IU/mL) or usual care (40 mg twice daily). MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was peak anti-Xa level at 'steady state' (after ≥3 enoxaparin doses). The feasibility threshold was set at 95% of steady state anti-Xa levels in the intervention group being less than the threshold for therapeutic anticoagulant effect (≤0.6 IU/mL). RESULTS: Fifty participants (intervention n = 17, control n = 33) received 331 doses of enoxaparin (median of 4 [interquartile range {IQR}: 3-7] doses per participant, and a dose of 50 [IQR: 50-60] mg (intervention) and 40 [IQR: 40-40] mg (control)). Thirty-two 'steady state' peak anti-Xa measurements were recorded from 24 patients (12 intervention and 12 control). The proportion of peak anti-Xa levels that were ≤0.6 IU/mL was: 15 of 17 (88%) vs. 15 of 15 (100%). There were fewer peak anti-Xa measurements below the prophylactic range (<0.2 IU/mL) in the intervention group compared with the control group (2 of 17 [12%] vs. 5 of 15 [33%]). Six patients developed venous thrombosis or pulmonary embolism (2 of 17 [12%] vs. 4 of 33 [12%]). Major bleeding occurred in one patient in the intervention group. CONCLUSIONS: A weight-based dynamic thromboprophylaxis algorithm was implemented via the electronic medical record but did not meet the predefined feasibility threshold.

This trial evaluated the feasibility of a weight-based dynamic dosing algorithm. DESIGN SETTING PARTICIPANTS: Open-label, electronic medical record-embedded randomised feasibility trial.

title: Tumor necrosis factor inhibitors and cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis is associated with persistent systemic inflammation and increased cardiovascular risk. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between anti-TNF therapy and clinical cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. METHODS: The authors conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and prospectively registered the protocol in PROSPERO (CRD420251270784). Randomized controlled trials and comparative observational studies evaluating anti-TNF therapy versus placebo, no anti-TNF exposure, topical therapy and/or phototherapy, or non-biologic systemic therapy were eligible. Outcomes of interest were Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE), myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular death, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism, and all-cause mortality. RESULTS: Fourteen studies were included. In randomized evidence, anti-TNF therapy was not associated with significant differences in the risk of MACE, myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure. In observational analyses stratified by comparator, anti-TNF therapy was associated with a lower pooled risk of reported cardiovascular events versus topical therapy, but not versus oral therapy or phototherapy. STUDY LIMITATIONS: The available evidence was limited by short follow-up in randomized trials, low cardiovascular event counts, wide confidence intervals, and indirect assessment of cardiovascular outcomes, as most trials were designed primarily for dermatologic efficacy and general safety rather than cardiovascular endpoints. CONCLUSIONS: Anti-TNF agents were not associated with a clear increase in major cardiovascular risk and appear to have an acceptable short-term cardiovascular safety profile. However, current evidence does not establish a conclusive cardioprotective effect, and larger prospective studies with longer follow-up are needed.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between anti-TNF therapy and clinical cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. METHODS: The authors conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and prospectively registered the protocol in PROSPERO (CRD420251270784).

title: Efficacy and safety of topical versus intravenous tranexamic acid in primary total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) often leads to substantial perioperative blood loss and postoperative hemoglobin decline, frequently requiring allogeneic transfusions. Tranexamic acid (TXA) effectively reduces bleeding, but debate persists regarding whether topical or intravenous (IV) administration provides superior clinical outcomes.This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of topical versus IV TXA in primary TKA using pooled data from randomized controlled trials (RCTs). METHODS: PubMed was searched for parallel-group RCTs comparing topical and IV TXA. Random-effects models analyzed continuous outcomes via standardized mean differences (SMDs) and dichotomous outcomes via relative risks (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: Eleven RCTs were included. Pooled analysis demonstrated no statistically significant differences between topical and IV TXA across all metrics. Postoperative hemoglobin drop (9 studies, 815 patients; SMD = -0.292, 95% CI: -0.748 to 0.163, P = 0.208), total blood loss (5 studies, 418 patients; SMD = 0.356, 95% CI: -0.297 to 1.009, P = 0.284), drainage volume (5 studies, 357 patients; SMD = 0.721, 95% CI: -0.394 to 1.836, P = 0.204), and transfusion rate (10 studies, 914 patients; RR = 0.644, 95% CI: 0.343 to 1.209, P = 0.171). Safety data were limited, as usable deep vein thrombosis (DVT) data were reported in only seven studies (with four studies not reporting or not stating thromboembolic/adverse event), and only a single DVT event was reported in the IV group. CONCLUSIONS: In primary TKA, no clear difference was detected between topical and IV TXA for blood conservation, drainage volumes, and transfusion rates, with substantial uncertainty, especially for safety and thromboembolic outcomes.

title: Anatomical Risk Factors for Technical Failure of the Perclose Vascular Closure Device: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Percutaneous large-bore femoral closure with the Perclose device is widely used, but technical failure remains clinically important. We identified anatomical risk factors for technical failure. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed endovascular aortic repair and endovascular therapy procedures using the Perclose device at the common femoral artery (CFA) between April 2020 and March 2025. Preoperative computed tomography (CT) measured CFA diameter, puncture depth, and a calcification score (0-4). Technical failure was defined as failure to achieve hemostasis with the intended deployment. Independent predictors were identified using patient-clustered generalized estimating equations. RESULTS: Among 300 patients (485 limbs), technical failure occurred in 52 limbs (10.7%), of which 75.0% required surgical repair. Independent predictors were a higher calcification score (odds ratio [OR] 2.13 per 1-point increase; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.37-3.31), an emergency procedure (OR 3.77; 1.55-9.14), a smaller CFA diameter (OR 1.16 per 1-mm decrease; 1.01-1.32), and a shallower puncture depth (OR 1.22 per 5-mm decrease; 1.01-1.47); the area under the curve was 0.72. CONCLUSIONS: Technical failure was driven by unfavorable CFA anatomy-heavy calcification, a small diameter, and a shallow puncture depth-and by emergency procedures. Preprocedural imaging assessment is essential; alternative closure or surgical cutdown should be considered in unfavorable or emergent cases.

We identified anatomical risk factors for technical failure. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed endovascular aortic repair and endovascular therapy procedures using the Perclose device at the common femoral artery (CFA) between April 2020 and March 2025.

title: Computational Fluid Dynamics Analysis of Contrast Agent Distribution in Acute Large Artery Occlusive Stroke: A Preliminary Proof-of-Concept Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) resulting from carotid artery occlusion (CAO) represents a significant clinical challenge because conventional imaging modalities often lead to inaccuracies in occlusion length assessment, potentially compromising therapeutic decision-making. We aimed to analyze the distribution patterns of contrast agents using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations in AIS caused by CAO and to mitigate errors in estimating occlusion length. METHODS: Data from four patients with AIS caused by CAO were analyzed. CFD simulations were conducted using postoperative computed tomography angiography (CTA) data to model contrast agent flow, and the results were compared with those of preoperative CTA and intraoperative digital subtraction angiography (DSA). RESULTS: CTA/DSA demonstrated a flame sign at the ICA origin in Patients 1-3. Patients 1 and 2 had carotid dissection, whereas Patient 3 had a C4-segment embolic occlusion. In Patient 3, DSA showed C1-origin vortices, a horizontal contrast-blood interface, and no distal C1 opacification, features distinct from those in Patients 1 and 2. CFD simulations using the post-recanalization CTA model replicated this contrast distribution, including the vortices and interface; proximal C1 vortex ranges, velocities, pressures, and wall shear stress were comparable, but the mass-weighted average velocity varied over time. CONCLUSIONS: CFD simulations recreated contrast agent distribution during C4 segment occlusion, revealing a high-pressure dead space in the distal C1 segment. This study generated preliminary evidence for understanding contrast agent distribution in CAOs, offering valuable insights for clinical imaging assessments.

We aimed to analyze the distribution patterns of contrast agents using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations in AIS caused by CAO and to mitigate errors in estimating occlusion length. METHODS: Data from four patients with AIS caused by CAO were analyzed.

title: Nurse-Led Longitudinal Screening and Care Transitions for Post-Traumatic Stress Symptoms After Acute Type A Aortic Dissection: A 12-Month Retrospective Longitudinal Cohort Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To identify longitudinal trajectories of post-traumatic stress symptoms (PTSS) after acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) and to examine baseline and time-varying psychological factors associated with subsequent symptom burden in a nurse-led follow-up cohort. METHODS: This single-center retrospective longitudinal cohort study included 278 ATAAD survivors discharged from Henan Provincial Chest Hospital between 1 August 2023 and 30 July 2024. Clinical and nurse-led follow-up records through 1 August 2025 were reviewed for assessments at discharge and at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. The primary trajectory analysis used PCL-5 scores from 1 to 12 months among participants with at least two valid assessments. One- through four-class latent class mixed models were compared according to convergence, Bayesian information criterion, classification quality, and minimum class size. Baseline correlates were examined with multinomial regression. Lagged models separated between-person means from within-person changes in illness threat, insomnia, and repetitive negative thinking; social support was examined across the 3-to-6-month interval. RESULTS: A three-class solution was selected: low-decreasing (n=153, 55.0%), recovering (n=77, 27.7%), and persistent-high (n=48, 17.3%). Within-person increases in illness threat, insomnia, and repetitive negative thinking were associated with higher subsequent PCL-5 scores, whereas higher social support was associated with a lower subsequent score. Baseline associations were attenuated after multiplicity correction. CONCLUSION: The model identified three PTSS trajectories during the first year after ATAAD discharge. Repeated nurse-led assessment may help identify survivors with a persistent symptom burden, and changes in illness threat, insomnia, repetitive negative thinking, and social support may inform the timing and focus of transitional care. The effectiveness of screening or targeted care was not tested.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective longitudinal cohort study included 278 ATAAD survivors discharged from Henan Provincial Chest Hospital between 1 August 2023 and 30 July 2024. title: Timeless therapeutics: cardiac indications for vitamin K antagonists in clinical practice.
abstract: Anticoagulation is a critical component in the treatment of cardiovascular diseases. Large randomised controlled trials have demonstrated that direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are effective and safe for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and treatment or prevention of venous thromboembolism. Nevertheless, for specific cardiac indications and patient characteristics, vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) rather than DOACs are either preferred, or the benefit of DOACs in comparison to VKAs remains uncertain. These include, among others, mechanical heart valves, AF associated with moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis, left ventricular or atrial thrombus, and older patients with frailty. As VKAs will continue to play a vital role in the management of patients with cardiovascular diseases in the foreseeable future, this review discusses cardiac indications and patient characteristics that necessitate the use of VKAs and general management principles of VKA therapy.

title: Predictors of in-hospital venous thromboembolism in patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty.
abstract: PURPOSE: This study evaluated the national inpatient incidence, patient characteristics, and independent predictors of VTE following primary THA. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed using the National Inpatient Sample from 2016 to 2022. Adult patients undergoing primary THA were identified using ICD-10 procedure codes. The primary outcome was in-hospital VTE, defined as deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism during the index admission. Survey-weighted analyses were used to generate national estimates, compare baseline characteristics, and identify independent predictors of VTE using multivariable logistic regression. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05. RESULTS: Among 855,645 weighted inpatient primary THA admissions, 1660 patients developed in-hospital VTE, corresponding to an incidence of 0.19%. Patients with VTE were older (P < 0.001) and more frequently covered by Medicare (P < 0.001), treated at large hospitals (P = 0.009), and treated at urban teaching hospitals (P = 0.013). They also had a greater prevalence of comorbidities, including autoimmune disease, coagulopathy, congestive heart failure, deficiency anemia, peripheral vascular disease, pulmonary circulation disorders, and moderate renal failure (all P < 0.001), as well as chronic pulmonary disease (P = 0.001) and obesity (P = 0.003). On adjusted analysis, the strongest predictors of VTE were paralysis (OR 9.79, P < 0.001), lymphoma (OR 4.35, P = 0.001), other neurologic disorders (OR 4.30, P < 0.001), and pulmonary circulation disorders (OR 3.50, P < 0.001). Additional independent predictors included peripheral vascular disease (OR 2.19, P < 0.001), autoimmune disease (OR 2.01, P < 0.001), congestive heart failure (OR 1.83, P = 0.022), coagulopathy (OR 1.80, P = 0.035), deficiency anemia (OR 1.65, P = 0.002), hypothyroidism (OR 1.45, P = 0.007), and obesity (OR 1.35, P = 0.018). CONCLUSION: In-hospital VTE following primary THA was uncommon but concentrated among medically complex patients. Improved risk stratification may guide perioperative counseling, surveillance, and individualized thromboprophylaxis for higher-risk patients.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed using the National Inpatient Sample from 2016 to 2022. Adult patients undergoing primary THA were identified using ICD-10 procedure codes.

title: Integration of computed tomography and endoscopic findings in identifying pseudoaneurysm rupture associated with duodenal penetration by pancreatic head cancer: A case report.
abstract: Pancreatic head cancer may cause life-threatening upper gastrointestinal bleeding through duodenal invasion and tumor-related arterial involvement. In such patients, differentiating between benign peptic ulcer disease and tumor invasion or penetration is clinically important because this distinction may influence whether endoscopic management or angiography with possible endovascular treatment is pursued. We report a 66-year-old man receiving chemotherapy for unresectable pancreatic head adenocarcinoma who presented with melena. Compared with pre-chemotherapy computed tomography, contrast-enhanced computed tomography on admission showed tumor shrinkage; however, air and a gas-containing low-attenuation area involving the residual pancreatic head lesion and adjacent peripancreatic region suggested tumor necrosis and/or communication with the gastrointestinal lumen. A focal aneurysmal lesion was also identified within the residual pancreatic head tumor. Endoscopy revealed a deep duodenal bulb ulcer without active bleeding. Together, these findings suggested duodenal penetration with tumor-related arterial involvement. The patient subsequently developed hemorrhagic shock, and emergency angiography demonstrated pseudoaneurysm rupture corresponding to the aneurysmal lesion seen on computed tomography. Transcatheter arterial embolization achieved hemostasis, and follow-up endoscopy showed coil exposure at the ulcer base. This case highlights that careful integration of computed tomography and endoscopic findings may help identify duodenal penetration with tumor-related pseudoaneurysm rupture, even when endoscopy shows no active bleeding.

In such patients, differentiating between benign peptic ulcer disease and tumor invasion or penetration is clinically important because this distinction may influence whether endoscopic management or angiography with possible endovascular treatment is pursued. We report a 66-year-old man receiving chemotherapy for unresectable pancreatic head adenocarcinoma who presented with melena.

title: Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyzes reveal hepatic regulatory mechanisms of residual feed intake during the late growth stage of slow-growing yellow-feathered broilers.
abstract: This study aimed to characterize hepatic molecular features associated with residual feed intake (RFI) during the late growth stage of slow-growing yellow-feathered broilers through integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyzes. RFI was measured in 478 individually caged male Langya chickens from 96 to 133 days of age. After the feeding trial, the chickens were ranked in ascending order of RFI and classified into low-RFI (LRFI) and high-RFI (HRFI) subpopulations using the population mean RFI as the cutoff. Eight healthy chickens were then randomly selected from each subpopulation to form the LRFI and HRFI groups (n = 8 per group). Following slaughter and tissue collection at 133 days of age, hepatic transcriptomic and LC-MS-based untargeted metabolomic analyzes were conducted. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and differentially abundant metabolites (DAMs) were subsequently subjected to enrichment and correlation analyzes. Compared with HRFI chickens, LRFI chickens had lower feed intake (FI) and higher eviscerated carcass yield and breast muscle yield. They also had lower abdominal fat percentage and muscle fat width, whereas BWG and metabolic body weight were similar between groups. Liver profiling identified 850 DEGs and 282 DAMs. Integrated KEGG analysis identified 15 pathways significantly enriched in both datasets. The amino acid metabolism-related pathways among these shared pathways collectively pointed to aromatic amino acid (AAA)-related metabolism, including biosynthesis of amino acids, phenylalanine metabolism, phenylalanine, tyrosine and tryptophan biosynthesis, and tryptophan metabolism. A total of 16 DEGs and 29 DAMs were mapped to these pathways and showed widespread significant correlations. Among them, IL4I1, AFMID, ASS1, PHGDH, MAOB, IDO2, HAAO, and PAH were identified as candidate genes associated with RFI. These results characterized hepatic molecular features associated with RFI during the late growth stage of slow-growing yellow-feathered broilers. These findings indicate that hepatic AAA-related metabolism may play a potential role in RFI divergence during the late growth stage in slow-growing yellow-feathered broilers. The identified AAA metabolism-related pathways provide a focused set of candidate genes, metabolites, and pathways for further investigation of their roles in RFI and feed efficiency, and provide a theoretical basis for molecular breeding and breed conservation of slow-growing broilers.

title: PASCAL Precision System Outcomes by Implant Location and Lesion Location in Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation Patients From the STS/ACC TVT Registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair can be more challenging in noncentral regions of the valve and in anterior or bileaflet lesions. We assess effect of implant location and leaflet lesion location on safety and effectiveness of PASCAL Precision system in degenerative mitral regurgitation (MR). METHODS: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair outcomes in patients with degenerative MR treated with PASCAL Precision system (September 2022-October 2024), from the US STS/ACC TVT (Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy) Registry, were analyzed by implant location (A2P2/non-A2P2) and leaflet lesion location (anterior/posterior/bileaflet). Procedural, clinical, and echocardiographic outcomes to 30 days were assessed. RESULTS: P P P P P P P P At 30 days, both A2P2 (n=1526) and non-A2P2 (n=299) groups had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 1.1% versus 1.0%, mitral valve reintervention: 0.4% versus 0.0% and single leaflet device attachment: 0.5% versus 0.3%; all>0.05) and demonstrated significant MR reduction (<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference between groups (=0.750) (MR ≤2+: 93.4% versus 95.4%; MR ≤1+: 72.0% versus 73.3%). Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores improved significantly in both groups (∆19.3, ∆17.7 points;=0.741). The anterior (n=250), posterior (n=902), and bileaflet (n=192) disease groups also had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 0.4%, 1.1%, 0.0%; mitral valve reintervention: 0.8%, 0.1%, 0.5%; and single leaflet device attachment: 0.8%, 0.2%, 0.5%; all>0.05), and demonstrated significant MR reduction (<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference across groups (=0.459) (MR ≤2+: 94.1%, 93.1%, and 94.5%; MR ≤1+: 79.0%, 69.2%, and 72.4%). All groups experienced significant improvement in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores (∆21.4, ∆18.8, ∆12.0 points;=0.087). CONCLUSION: In real-world patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation, treatment with the PASCAL Precision system was associated with favorable safety and effectiveness at 30 days, regardless of implant location or leaflet lesion location.

title: Renal pseudoaneurysm and arterial-pelvicalyceal fistula after partial nephrectomy managed with staged angioembolization: A case report.
abstract: Delayed haemorrhage after partial nephrectomy is usually attributed to a single vascular lesion and controlled by transarterial embolization. A 62-year-old man developed massive haematuria one week after left partial nephrectomy. CT angiography showed a segmental renal pseudoaneurysm, which was embolised superselectively. Bleeding recurred within 24 hours; repeat angiography revealed a separate arterial-pelvicalyceal fistula, treated by a second embolization with durable haemostasis. Recurrence after apparently successful embolization may therefore reflect a second, unrecognised lesion rather than treatment failure. A low threshold for repeat angiography and staged, lesion-specific embolization can achieve definitive control while preserving renal parenchyma.

title: Percutaneous device closure of a massive pseudoaneurysm of the descending aorta in a paediatric patient with Takayasu arteritis.
abstract: TM Takayasu arteritis (TA) is commonly known as a disease of young women, highly prevalent in Asia and Central America, and associated with multiple vascular complications. Although it is well described in the paediatric population, severe complications are rarely seen. A 6-year-old girl was referred to our institution with features suggestive of a tuberculosis infection, along with a suspected intrathoracic mass on preliminary imaging. Further investigations confirmed the mass to be a massive pseudoaneurysm originating from the descending aorta and extending into the left hemithorax. A multidisciplinary discussion concluded that this pseudoaneurysm carried a high mortality risk with a direct surgical approach. This case report describes the use of an Amplatzerseptal occluder as a bridge to surgical excision of the massive pseudoaneurysm in a paediatric patient with confirmed TA.

title: Ascending and hemi arch replacement during bilateral orthotopic lung transplant: a case report.
abstract: Lung transplant candidates increasingly have concomitant cardiac disease. Prior studies have demonstrated the safety of lung transplant with concurrent cardiac surgery in small case series. Here, we describe a case of ascending aorta replacement at the same time as bilateral lung transplant utilizing a clamshell incision. The patient recovered well. With this case report, we aim to contribute to the growing literature showing the safety of concomitant heart and aortic surgery during lung transplant.

title: Post-Transcriptional Silencing of PHD2 by CRISPR-Cas13d Enhances Pro-Angiogenic Signaling in Human Endothelial Cells.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) reduces tissue perfusion and causes ischemia, conditions in which hypoxia-responsive pathways have an important adaptive role. Hypoxia- inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF-1α), a central regulator of this response, is tightly controlled by prolyl hydroxylase domain protein 2 (PHD2), encoded by EGLN1. Here, we used an RNA-targeting CRISPR-Cas13d system to downregulate EGLN1 in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) under normoxia and hypoxia. METHODS: A PHD2-knockdown (PHD2-KD) HUVEC line was generated by lentiviral delivery of an EGLN1-targeting RNA guide, alongside non-transduced (CTRL) and non-targeting gRNA (NTG) control lines. Molecular and functional assays assessed hypoxia-related signaling, metabolic activity, migration, and sprouting responses under normoxia and hypoxia. RESULTS: Western blotting confirmed a marked reduction in PHD2 protein abundance in PHD2-KD cells relative to both CTRL and NTG cells. PHD2-KD HUVECs exhibited increased VEGFA transcript levels (6.5-fold under normoxia and 5.3-fold under hypoxia) and secreted VEGF concentrations (6.6-fold and 9.4-fold, respectively), together with early increases in HIF1A transcript and HIF-1α protein levels and lower TNF-α concentrations. Functional assays showed higher metabolic activity, faster wound closure (2.0-fold under normoxia and 2.2-fold under hypoxia), and enhanced sprouting, with up to 7.2-fold more sprouts per bead and sprouts up to 2.7-fold longer than those formed by CTRL. DISCUSSION: CRISPR-Cas13d-mediated EGLN1 targeting reduced PHD2 protein abundance and was associated with higher endothelial metabolic activity, faster wound closure, enhanced sprouting behavior, and lower TNF-α secretion. CONCLUSION: CRISPR-Cas13d-mediated downregulation of EGLN1/PHD2 was associated with increased pro-angiogenic signaling and improved angiogenesis-related endothelial responses in vitro, supporting RNA-targeting strategies to modulate hypoxia-responsive pathways.

Hypoxia- inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF-1α), a central regulator of this response, is tightly controlled by prolyl hydroxylase domain protein 2 (PHD2), encoded by EGLN1. Here, we used an RNA-targeting CRISPR-Cas13d system to downregulate EGLN1 in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) under normoxia and hypoxia.

title: Factors associated with failures and outcomes of Peripherally Inserted Central Catheters in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: to analyze factors associated with catheter progression failure and outcomes of Peripherally Inserted Central Catheters inserted by nurses in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. METHOD: observational cohort study was conducted with hospitalized COVID-19 patients, following the STROBE guidelines. Categorical variables were described as absolute and relative frequencies; quantitative variables were expressed as median and interquartile range. Non-parametric tests were applied due to non-normal distribution. Associations were analyzed using Pearson's chi-squared or Fisher's exact tests. Logistic regression was performed for variables associated with outcomes. RESULTS: a total of 1061 Peripherally Inserted Central Catheters were analyzed. The main indications were for antibiotic therapy, and most catheters were removed after treatment completion. First-attempt failure and clinical patient profile were associated with catheter progression failure. Subcutaneous heparin was a protective factor. Among Peripherally Inserted Central Catheters successfully inserted, tip confirmation via chest X-ray and catheter-to-vessel ratio between 31%-40% were associated with thrombosis, whereas Sherlock™ confirmation was protective. CONCLUSION: catheter progression failure was associated with clinical conditions and first-attempt failure. Adverse outcomes were associated with X-ray tip confirmation and catheter-to-vessel ratio, whereas Sherlock™ use and subcutaneous heparin were protective factors.

title: Evaluation of morphometric characteristics and positional variations of the carotid sinus using computed tomography angiography.
abstract: PURPOSE: The aim of this study was to determine the morphometric characteristics and spatial variations of the carotid sinus (CS) using computed tomography angiography (CTA) images. METHODS: In the study, cervical CTA images of a total of 100 individuals (200 sides) comprising 55 men and 45 women were examined. The diameters of the proximal and distal segments of the common carotid artery (CCA) and the internal carotid artery (ICA), as well as the proximal diameter of the external carotid artery (ECA), were measured. In addition, measurements of the maximum transverse diameter and length of the CS were taken; the resulting data were compared according to the variables of age, gender and side. RESULTS: All artery diameters, CS length (mean 8.78 ± 1.33 mm), and maximum CS diameter (mean 8.27 ± 1.10 mm) were found to be significantly higher in men than in women (p < 0.001). It was determined that the diameters of the CCA and ICA on the left side were statistically significantly wider than those on the right side (p < 0.001). It was found that CS localization was asymmetric in 29% of cases and most commonly occurred in the proximal ICA (Type I) in 74.5% of cases. In addition, a positive and statistically significant correlation (r = 0.554; p < 0.001) was found between age and CS length. CONCLUSION: Understanding the morphological variations of the CS is of critical importance in preventing unintended CS stimulation and related complications during surgical procedures in this region, particularly carotid endarterectomy.

title: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Endovascular and Open Surgical Repair for Infective Native Aortic Aneurysms.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Infective native aortic aneurysms (mycotic) are rare but highly lethal, and the optimal treatment strategy between endovascular repair and open surgical repair (OSR) remains debated because of a persistent trade-off between early survival and durable infection control. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing early and long-term outcomes of endovascular repair and OSR, complemented by a single-arm meta-analysis characterizing outcomes after endovascular repair. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to June 16, 2026. Comparative studies were pooled using inverse-variance random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation of between-study variance (odds ratios [ORs]); single-arm proportions were pooled using logit-transformed, inverse-variance-weighted random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed with Risk of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions-I. Outcomes included 30-day and 1-year all-cause mortality, reinfection (a new or persistent infection requiring antimicrobial therapy or source control), sepsis recurrence (a new episode meeting sepsis criteria after initial clinical resolution), reintervention, and acute kidney injury (AKI). RESULTS: Thirty-five retrospective studies were included: 18 comparative studies (2,853 enrolled patients; 1,305 endovascular repair and 1,548 OSR; 17 of which, comprising 2,836 patients, reported 30-day mortality) and 17 single-arm studies (444 endovascular repair patients; 16 of which reported 30-day mortality). Endovascular repair was associated with significantly lower 30-day mortality than OSR (OR 0.72, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.55-0.93) but not with 1-year mortality (eight studies, 1,630 patients; OR 1.23, 95% CI 0.66-2.29), and with a higher risk of reinfection (14 studies, 1,448 patients; OR 2.56, 95% CI 1.71-3.82). No significant differences were found for sepsis recurrence, reintervention, or AKI, though these comparisons were imprecise and compatible with both clinically meaningful benefit and harm, and should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence between strategies. In the single-arm analysis, pooled 30-day mortality after endovascular repair was 6.5%, 1-year mortality was 22.4%, and reinfection was 14.7%. CONCLUSION: In pooled analysis, endovascular repair was associated with lower early mortality compared with open surgical repair, although this finding was sensitive to the inclusion of a single large registry-based study and should be interpreted with caution. No significant difference in 1-year mortality was observed, but this comparison was imprecise and based on few studies and should not be interpreted as evidence that a survival advantage is absent. Endovascular repair carries a higher risk of reinfection. Careful patient selection, prolonged antimicrobial therapy, and structured postoperative surveillance remain essential regardless of the repair strategy chosen. Certainty of evidence for all comparative outcomes was very low (GRADE), reflecting the observational design, serious risk of confounding by indication, and imprecision of the pooled estimates.

title: Lesion Water Content on CT Predicts 12-Month Outcome and Modifies Thrombectomy Effect in Large-Core Stroke-A Secondary Analysis of the TENSION Trial.
abstract: In large-core ischemic stroke, outcomes after thrombectomy remain heterogeneous, and imaging markers that capture treatment-modifiable injury beyond lesion extent are needed. We investigated whether lesion water content on noncontrast CT, quantified as net water uptake (NWU), predicts 12-month functional outcome and modifies the effect of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). This secondary analysis of the randomized TENSION trial included 198 patients with admission CT suitable for NWU quantification and available 12-month modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores; 168 had paired 24-h CT for follow-up NWU (NWUFU) assessment. The primary outcome was ordinal 12-month mRS. Multivariable ordinal and logistic regression tested associations and the NWU × EVT interaction, with discrimination assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Median baseline NWU was 16.4% and NWUFU 28.9%. At 12 months, 45 patients (23%) had mRS 0-3 and 111 (56%) had died. Higher baseline NWU independently predicted worse 12-month mRS (adjusted common odds ratio [acOR], 1.10 per percentage-point; 95% CI, 1.05-1.16; P < 0.001) and modified the EVT effect (interaction acOR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.06-1.30; P = 0.002), with greater discrimination than ASPECTS. NWUFU was the strongest single imaging predictor (acOR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.06-1.14; P < 0.001; AUC, 0.78 for mRS 0-3) and superseded baseline NWU when co-modeled. Among 97 90-day survivors, higher NWUFU independently predicted late mortality (adjusted odds ratio, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.02-1.18; P = 0.019). Lesion water content may therefore provide a clinically accessible CT biomarker linking treatment-modifiable injury at baseline with realized post-treatment injury and long-term outcome.

We investigated whether lesion water content on noncontrast CT, quantified as net water uptake (NWU), predicts 12-month functional outcome and modifies the effect of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). This secondary analysis of the randomized TENSION trial included 198 patients with admission CT suitable for NWU quantification and available 12-month modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores; 168 had paired 24-h CT for follow-up NWU (NWUFU) assessment.

title: AI-enhanced intraoperative decision-making in robotic surgery: from augmented reality navigation to foundation models.
abstract: Robotic surgical platforms have improved instrument dexterity, tremor filtration, and ergonomic control, yet intraoperative decisions still depend on a surgeon interpreting a moving, partially observed field under time pressure. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to close parts of this loop by recognizing anatomy, tracking instruments, anticipating events, and-experimentally-planning or executing selected actions. This review maps the computational technologies that support intraoperative decision-making in robotic surgery and appraises the clinical evidence for them.Because the direct robotic evidence base is still uneven, we explicitly distinguish three kinds of material: (i) studies conducted on robotic systems during surgery; (ii) non-robotic surgical evidence from laparoscopic and thoracoscopic procedures that use the same vision and workflow methods; and (iii) preclinical, preoperative, and perioperative work that is conceptually relevant but not intraoperative. Robotic and non-robotic settings are labeled throughout the tables and text. We further separate non-AI image guidance-indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence and registered overlays-from AI-based inference, and we include image-guided endovascular robotics as a complementary setting in which fluoroscopic perception, vascular-topology reasoning, and closed-loop instrument control are particularly advanced.We organize the field into four computational layers: perception, anatomical and procedural reasoning, action planning, and control and execution. Augmented-reality and fluorescence navigation can improve orientation and selected intermediate outcomes, and several randomized trials now exist. Computer-vision systems can recognize anatomy, phases, instruments, and adverse events, and in endovascular work they can track guidewires and reason over vascular topology. Foundation models broaden language and multimodal capabilities but remain, in surgery, largely preclinical. Autonomous subtasks have shown promise in phantoms, animals, and a small number of carefully bounded tissue tasks; no system has demonstrated safe, accountable patient-level autonomous decision-making.Navigation and AI-assisted systems have improved orientation, reduced ischemia, and accelerated recognition of critical events in some studies. Whether these intermediate gains improve patient outcomes, generalize across institutions, or justify their cost remains unknown. The question is not whether AI can interpret surgical scenes, but which decisions can be delegated, with what evidence, uncertainty limits, oversight, and outcome measures.

title: From hypoxia to thrombosis: a hypothesis-driven framework for pulmonary embolism risk in deep underground environments.
abstract: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is one of the most severe manifestations of venous thromboembolism, yet current diagnostic and preventive frameworks have largely been developed in ground-based clinical settings. Deep underground environments represent complex occupational exposure systems characterized by relative hypoxia or oxygen fluctuation, normobaric to mildly hyperbaric pressure, high humidity and heat, airborne particulates, radon accumulation, restricted ventilation, limited mobility, circadian disruption, and enclosed psychosocial stress. These factors may interact dynamically with oxygen sensing, cardiopulmonary compensation, venous return, endothelial function, and coagulation-inflammation pathways. However, the relationship between deep underground exposure, thrombogenesis, PE recognition, and prevention remains insufficiently conceptualized. Direct epidemiological evidence linking deep-underground occupational exposure to incident venous thromboembolism or PE remains scarce, and existing PE prediction tools have not been specifically validated in deep-underground occupational populations. Therefore, this review does not assume that underground exposure independently increases PE incidence or that established clinical tools are inadequate. Instead, we develop a hypothesis-driven framework to examine whether exposure-related factors-including oxygen fluctuation, heat and dehydration, restricted mobility, altered hemodynamics, and inflammatory stress-could modify thrombotic susceptibility, symptom interpretation, or the operational performance of conventional PE pathways. We summarize the environmental and physiological stressors relevant to PE, examine how they may amplify Virchow's triad, and discuss research questions concerning symptom recognition, anticoagulation, reperfusion decision-making, preventive interventions, and the staged development of dynamic risk warning models. This review aims to provide a conceptual foundation for future surveillance, prevention, and clinical research on PE in deep underground occupational populations.

title: Anticoagulation management in a pediatric patient with protein S deficiency and acute pulmonary embolism undergoing ECMO-supported intervention: a case report.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Protein S deficiency is a predominant form of hereditary thrombophilia in Asian populations. Pediatric venous thromboembolism (VTE) is exceedingly rare, with an incidence of only 0.2%-0.6%, and acute massive pulmonary embolism (PE) requiring extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) support in children with thrombophilia presents exceptional clinical challenges. The core therapeutic dilemma lies in reconciling the hypercoagulable state inherent to protein S deficiency with the high bleeding risk following thrombolytic therapy, compounded by the obligatory anticoagulation requirement during ECMO. This case report describes the nursing management of a pediatric patient with protein S deficiency and acute PE who successfully underwent ECMO-supported interventional treatment under high bleeding risk. OUTCOME: The patient was successfully weaned from ECMO after 98 h of support, extubated on day 6, and discharged in stable condition after 30 days of hospitalization. At 6-month follow-up, no thrombus recurrence was observed, and the patient had fully resumed normal life and academic activities. CONCLUSION: This case demonstrates that an individualized low-dose heparin anticoagulation strategy, guided by the PEACE consensus and supported by meticulous monitoring, can effectively balance the competing risks of thrombosis and hemorrhage in pediatric ECMO patients with underlying thrombophilia and recent thrombolysis. Notably, as a single case report, this finding cannot be broadly generalized to all pediatric ECMO patients with thrombophilia. Instead, this case provides a potential framework for individualized anticoagulation and nursing management that requires further validation in larger pediatric cohorts. The nursing experience provides a practical reference for managing similar complex cases in pediatric critical care.

title: Dietary aromatic amino acids, their food sources, and incident hypertension in Chinese adults: a prospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Prospective evidence linking dietary aromatic amino acids (AAAs), including phenylalanine (Phe), tyrosine (Tyr), and tryptophan (Trp), to incident hypertension currently remains limited, particularly regarding their individual components and food sources. Herein, we examined the association between dietary AAAs, their food sources, and incident hypertension among Chinese adults. METHODS: Using the China Health and Nutrition Survey database, this prospective cohort study collected data from 10,087 adults without hypertension at baseline. Baseline dietary intake was assessed using three consecutive 24-h dietary recalls, combined with household food weighing; the energy-adjusted AAA intake was expressed in g/1,000 kcal. Incident hypertension was defined as measured blood pressure, physician diagnosis, or use of antihypertensive medication. Mixed-effects Cox proportional hazards models with household identifiers as random intercepts were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Dose-response, food-source-specific, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses were performed. RESULTS: During the 95,153 person-years of follow-up, 3,531 participants developed hypertension. In fully adjusted models, the highest quartile of total AAA intake was associated with a modestly higher risk of incident hypertension compared with the lowest quartile (HR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.03-1.31; P for trend = 0.006). Positive associations were more consistent for Phe (HR for Q4 vs. Q1, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.11-1.44) and Trp (HR, 1.29; 95% CI, 1.14-1.46) individually, while Tyr intake showed no significant association with hypertension. Dose-response analyses indicated approximately linear positive associations for total AAA, Phe, and Trp. The association for total AAA was attenuated following additional adjustment for baseline province (HR for Q4 vs. Q1, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.97-1.24), while the positive associations for Phe and Trp persisted. Cereals were the predominant contributors to AAA intake, and plant-derived Phe and Trp were positively associated with the risk of hypertension. CONCLUSION: Higher dietary intakes of Phe and Trp showed consistent positive associations with incident hypertension, while Tyr showed no clear association. The modest association for total AAA was attenuated after adjusting for baseline province and should therefore be interpreted cautiously in relation to potential regional confounding factors. These findings support the component-specific interpretation of dietary AAAs and consideration of their regional and food source contexts.

title: Artificial intelligence for vascular minimally invasive surgery: techniques, clinical integration, and challenges.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Minimally invasive surgery (MIS), including endovascular and robot-assisted procedures, is widely used for vascular pathologies but remains limited by technical complexity, cognitive workload, and postoperative complications. Artificial Intelligence (AI) may help address these challenges through predictive analysis, decision support, image analysis, and automation. METHODS: A structured Google Scholar search was conducted from February 21, 2025, to January 1, 2026, and updated through September 2026. Peer-reviewed studies applying AI to vascular MIS were included, with additional targeted searches addressing clinical translation, deployment, regulation, and ethical considerations. RESULTS: Thirty primary studies were analyzed, including eight on machine learning, nine on deep learning, four on natural language processing, and nine on robotics or reinforcement learning. Machine learning supported risk stratification and outcome prediction, deep learning enabled imaging and segmentation applications, natural language processing facilitated clinical information extraction, and robotic systems supported navigation and procedural assistance. DISCUSSION: AI demonstrates substantial potential across the vascular MIS pathway, but broader clinical adoption requires stronger validation, prospective multicenter studies, standardized reporting, health-economic evaluation, and careful consideration of regulatory, liability, and accessibility challenges.

title: From revascularization to multimodal integrated therapy for peripheral arterial disease: immunomodulation, metabolic correction, and tissue engineering.
abstract: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD), a critical manifestation of systemic atherosclerosis (AS), poses substantial therapeutic challenges. Despite pharmacological interventions and revascularization, efficacy remains constrained by high restenosis rates and suboptimal functional recovery. These limitations underscore a necessary transition from localized structural revascularization toward integrated systemic repair, with a particular focus on the underlying immunopathology. The progression of PAD is driven by a dysregulated immune response, characterized by an imbalance in macrophage polarization (M1/M2), overactivation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, and a vicious cycle of immune-metabolic coupling. Current research trajectories emphasize the synergistic orchestration of the vascular microenvironment through immunomodulation. Beyond modulating localized inflammatory responses, emerging strategies target metabolic homeostasis and advanced tissue engineering, including spatiotemporal growth factor delivery, extracellular vesicle-based therapies, and bioengineered scaffolding systems. These interdisciplinary developments point toward a multimodal integrated therapeutic strategy for PAD. Such a strategy would build on conventional revascularization and may address its limitations, including restenosis, through targeted immunomodulation and local tissue regeneration. Whether this approach can improve long-term outcomes compared with revascularization alone remains to be tested. If validated, it could shift the clinical standard beyond vessel patency toward comprehensive, long-term vascular health.

title: Staphylococcus aureus -associated infected subclavian artery pseudoaneurysm treated with dual bare-metal stent implantation: a case report.
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus Infected subclavian artery aneurysms are exceedingly rare, life-threatening vascular lesions associated with high risks of rupture and mortality. We report a 70-year-old male presenting with intermittent hemoptysis, who was diagnosed with a pseudoaneurysm of the left subclavian artery adjacent to the dominant vertebral artery. Blood cultures confirmed methicillin-sensitiveinfection. The patient underwent endovascular repair with dual bare-metal stents to preserve vertebral artery perfusion. Hemoptysis completely resolved post-intervention. Complete thrombosis and occlusion of the aneurysm sac were achieved at the 3-month follow-up, with remarkable sac shrinkage observed at 6 months. This case suggests that dual bare-metal stents may represent a feasible potential treatment alternative for highly selected patients with infected subclavian artery aneurysms. Long-term safety and efficacy remain to be further verified. Long-term antimicrobial therapy and close surveillance remain mandatory.

title: Stage 1 Registered Report: sex differences in anticoagulation and stroke outcomes among patients with atrial fibrillation: a registry-based cohort study.
abstract: Women with atrial fibrillation have a higher risk of ischaemic stroke and worse functional outcomes than men but may be less likely to receive adequate anticoagulation. Preliminary single-centre findings in patients treated with endovascular thrombectomy for large vessel occlusion suggest that women may be under-anticoagulated prior to stroke onset. This Stage 1 Registered Report outlines a prespecified analysis plan to test sex-based differences in anticoagulation, stroke characteristics, treatment and outcomes in a prespecified confirmatory population and to explore whether similar patterns are observed at the national level. Using a retrospective cohort design, we will analyse local data from Stavanger University Hospital (2009-22) and national data from the Norwegian Stroke Registry. Confirmatory analyses will include patients with atrial fibrillation and large vessel occlusion treated with endovascular thrombectomy. Sex differences in anticoagulation, stroke severity, treatments and outcomes will be examined using chi-square tests and prespecified regression models; equivalence testing will be applied where appropriate. Exploratory analyses will assess age, comorbidity and healthcare delivery as potential mediators and moderators. No confirmatory analyses have been conducted.

title: ® ® Comparative cost analysis of Eluvia™ versus ZilverPTXin treating femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease utilizing real-world data.
abstract: Aim: Materials & methods: Results: Conclusion: ® ® To compare the hospital-based costs among patients with femoropopliteal artery (FPA) disease treated with Eluvia™ versus ZilverPTXdrug-eluting stents using a large real-world USA hospital database.This retrospective study included adults in the Premier Healthcare Database who underwent lower extremity FPA endovascular revascularization with Eluvia or Zilver PTX between 1 April 2019 and 31 March 2022. Total hospital-based costs during the index procedure and cumulative 1- and 2-year post-discharge follow-up were compared using multivariable generalized linear models adjusted for age, sex, race and baseline chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) status. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted by care setting (hospital inpatient and hospital outpatient) and among patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and CLTI.A total of 7208 patients were included, comprising 4218 treated with Eluvia and 2990 treated with Zilver PTX. Patients treated with Eluvia had a higher prevalence of several comorbidities, including congestive heart failure and CKD. Unadjusted mean hospital-based index procedure costs were similar between groups (Eluvia, $28,631 vs Zilver PTX, $28,359; difference, -$272; p = 0.7233). After adjustment, mean index procedure hospital-based costs did not differ significantly between treatment groups ($30,031, p = 0.8491). However, Eluvia was associated with lower adjusted cumulative hospital-based costs at the 1-year (difference, $4,017; p = 0.0066) and 2-year (difference, $6250; p = 0.0021) follow-up. Similar associations were observed in the hospital inpatient and CKD subgroups, whereas no statistically significant differences were observed in the CLTI subgroup.Across patients undergoing femoropopliteal endovascular revascularization, Eluvia was associated with significantly lower post-discharge cumulative hospital-based follow-up costs than Zilver PTX while index procedure costs were comparable. These findings reflect hospital-based costs captured within participating hospitals and do not include medication costs or costs of care received outside the Premier Healthcare Database; therefore, they should not be interpreted as total healthcare costs.

title: Quality and reliability of short videos about type A aortic dissection on Bilibili and TikTok: a cross-sectional study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Type A aortic dissection (TAAD) is a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency. Short-video platforms such as TikTok and Bilibili have become important channels for health information dissemination, but the quality and reliability of TAAD-related videos remain unclear. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the quality and reliability of TAAD-related short videos on TikTok and Bilibili, with particular attention to platform differences and uploader characteristics. METHODS: The top 250 videos ranked by comprehensive ranking on each platform were screened using the Chinese keyword "A." A total of 391 eligible videos were included. Uploaders were classified as medical practitioners, individual users, or institutions. Video quality and reliability were assessed using the Global Quality Score (GQS), modified DISCERN (mDISCERN), JAMA benchmarks, and Video Information Quality Instrument (VIQI). Multivariable regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with video quality. RESULTS: TikTok videos showed higher engagement, whereas Bilibili videos were longer and provided broader coverage of epidemiology, etiology, and clinical presentation-related content. TikTok remained independently associated with higher VIQI scores after adjustment. Medical practitioners and institutions generally achieved higher VIQI and JAMA scores than individual users, and content coverage score was independently associated with higher video quality. However, mDISCERN scores did not differ significantly among uploader types. CONCLUSION: TAAD-related short videos demonstrated moderate overall quality but limited reliability. Platform characteristics, uploader type, and content coverage were associated with assessed information quality. Professional participation may improve some aspects of health communication, but uploader identity alone does not ensure higher reliability or transparency.

Short-video platforms such as TikTok and Bilibili have become important channels for health information dissemination, but the quality and reliability of TAAD-related videos remain unclear. title: Yeast Mitochondrial Escape 1-Like as a Mitochondrial Gatekeeper in Aging-Related Cardiovascular Disease.
abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is a hallmark of aging and is closely linked to the progression of cardiovascular disease. Yeast mitochondrial escape 1-like (YME1L) is an adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-dependent i-AAA (intermembrane space AAA, AAA=ATPase associated with diverse cellular activities) protease embedded in the mitochondrial inner membrane that maintains mitochondrial homeostasis by regulating proteostasis, cristae architecture, and metabolic adaptation. Notably, YME1L influences mitochondrial fusion-fission dynamics, respiratory chain supercomplex organization, and oxidative phosphorylation efficiency through the regulated processing of optic atrophy protein 1 (OPA1). Accumulating evidence suggests that age-associated impairment of YME1L function contributes to mitochondrial fragmentation, energetic insufficiency, and reduced stress tolerance, particularly in long-lived, high-energy demand tissues. In the cardiovascular system, experimental models indicate that YME1L deficiency disrupts cristae organization, promotes maladaptive metabolic remodeling, and promotes heart failure-like phenotypes. Conversely, preservation of YME1L activity supports mitochondrial integrity and enhances cardiac resilience under hemodynamic stress. In addition to cardiomyocytes, YME1L also supports endothelial mitochondrial homeostasis, thereby linking mitochondrial proteostasis to vascular aging and diastolic dysfunction. Although YME1L has been extensively studied in cancer biology, its relevance to aging-related cardiovascular vulnerability is increasingly recognized, especially in cardio-oncology, where therapy-induced mitochondrial stress may be exacerbated by age-dependent decline in mitochondrial quality control. This review integrates current evidence supporting YME1L as a context-dependent regulator of mitochondrial stress adaptation, with particular emphasis on the roles of YME1L in cardiovascular aging, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), and stress tolerance. Rather than positioning YME1L as a universal therapeutic target, we discuss how modulating YME1L-associated pathways may help preserve mitochondrial resilience and mitigate age-related cardiovascular dysfunction.

title: Trends, outcomes and patient- and hospital-level factors associated with sepsis following cesarean delivery: a propensity-matched nationwide inpatient analysis (2016-2022).
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sepsis is a major global health concern and a serious complication of cesarean delivery. However, contemporary nationwide data describing both the temporal trend in post-cesarean sepsis and its downstream clinical and economic burden-particularly in propensity-matched comparisons-remain limited. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, propensity-matched analysis of all adult inpatients undergoing cesarean delivery recorded in the U.S. Nationwide Inpatient Sample (NIS, 2016-2022). Sepsis and cesarean delivery were defined using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes. After 1:5 propensity-score matching on demographics, comorbidity burden and hospital characteristics, we compared in-hospital mortality, length of stay (LOS), total hospitalization costs, and the incidence of perioperative complications between septic and non-septic patients. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify patient- and hospital-level factors independently associated with sepsis. RESULTS: n P P P Of 1,619,187 hospitalizations for cesarean delivery, 1,589,186 adults met the inclusion criteria. Annual sepsis prevalence rose from 0.058% in 2016 to 0.136% in 2022. In the 1:5 propensity-matched cohort ( = 10,050), septic patients had markedly higher in-hospital mortality (2.4% vs. 0.0%, < 0.001), longer median LOS (6 vs. 3 days, < 0.001), and approximately 2.6-fold higher median total hospitalization costs (USD 71,466 vs. USD 27,063, < 0.001). Non-elective admission, treatment in teaching hospitals, a higher comorbidity burden, Asian/Pacific Islander race, and hospital region were independently associated with sepsis. After propensity matching, septic patients also showed substantially elevated adjusted odds of pulmonary embolism (OR 61.7), postoperative shock (OR 28.7), deep-vein thrombosis (OR 24.6), urinary tract infection (OR 25.5), and chronic respiratory diseases (OR 13.2). CONCLUSIONS: In this large U.S. study, sepsis after cesarean section was linked to much higher death rates, twice the hospital stay, about 2.6 times higher costs, and more severe problems like blood clots, shock, infections, and heavy bleeding. These results show that post-cesarean section sepsis is a growing concern, remind us to spot at-risk mothers early, and offer a benchmark against which prevention and cost-effective care can be evaluated.

title: Endothelial glycocalyx dysfunction in the setting of mechanical thrombectomy: a conceptual link between cardiometabolic vulnerability and microvascular reperfusion failure.
abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) has made macrovessel reopening achievable in acute ischemic stroke, but angiographic success does not ensure effective tissue-level reperfusion or microvascular oxygen delivery. This narrative review examines endothelial glycocalyx dysfunction as a plausible blood-facing interface that may connect pre-existing cardiometabolic vulnerability with post-thrombectomy microvascular dysfunction. Targeted English-language literature from PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Embase, and Google Scholar through 30 April 2026 was synthesized, with emphasis on MT, impaired microvascular reperfusion (IMR), no-reflow, blood-brain barrier (BBB) and neurovascular-unit (NVU) biology, glycocalyx-related biomarkers, cardiometabolic risk, perfusion imaging, and microcirculatory rescue. The evidence base is heterogeneous and is explicitly separated into direct human MT/LVO evidence, indirect human biomarker or imaging evidence, experimental cerebral evidence, non-cerebral/cross-disease vascular evidence, and hypothesis-generating mechanistic inference. Ischemic priming, abrupt reperfusion, oxidative and inflammatory stress, complement activation, metabolic stress, distal embolization, device-endothelial trauma, and host vulnerability may converge on the luminal endothelial surface. Glycocalyx dysfunction may amplify leukocyte adhesion and capillary plugging, platelet adhesion and microthrombosis, impaired mechanosensing and nitric-oxide signaling, BBB destabilization, and heterogeneous capillary flow; however, direct causal proof in human MT is lacking. Circulating syndecan-1, heparan sulfate, and hyaluronan are therefore best interpreted as time- and compartment-dependent systemic signals rather than direct readouts of the cerebral glycocalyx. Post-EVT microcirculatory rescue trials show that downstream perfusion may remain therapeutically actionable, but they do not demonstrate glycocalyx repair as the operative mechanism. A practical translational strategy is to combine serial, compartment-annotated biomarkers with prespecified early perfusion/barrier imaging and tissue endpoints, while explicitly modeling cardiometabolic vulnerability and competing microvascular mechanisms. The glycocalyx framework should therefore be considered a testable network hypothesis rather than an established primary cause of post-thrombectomy no-reflow or futile recanalization.

title: Perforated marginal ulcer after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass: a national analysis of operative approaches, outcomes, and practice variations, 2018-2022.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Perforated marginal (gastrojejunal) ulcer is an uncommon but life-threatening complication after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass. Evidence is limited to single-center series and one 2022 systematic review of approximately 600 patients; contemporary national International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10)-era data are lacking. METHODS: We queried the National Inpatient Sample (2018-2022) for adults with a perforated gastrojejunal ulcer and a code indicating prior bariatric surgery. Operative approach was classified as laparoscopic patch, open patch, revisional gastrojejunostomy/reversal, or non-operative management. Survey-weighted statistics, negative-binomial (length of stay), gamma (total charges), and logistic (predictors of operative repair) models were estimated with hospital cluster-robust standard errors. RESULTS: The cohort included 1,669 unweighted admissions (8,345 weighted). Operative repair was performed in 28.9% (laparoscopic patch 12.6%, open patch 7.2%, revisional/reversal 9.2%); 71.1% were managed non-operatively. Crude in-hospital mortality was 1.1% overall. Non-operative management rose from 64.1% (2018) to 72.0% (2022), while laparoscopic patch declined from 18.1% to 12.1%. Open patch was associated with longer length of stay than laparoscopic patch [incidence-rate ratio 1.41, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.13-1.77] and higher complication rates after correction for multiple comparisons of sepsis, acute kidney injury, respiratory failure, and venous thromboembolism. Elective admission strongly predicted operative repair (adjusted odds ratio 2.58, 95% CI 1.74-3.83), elective admissions were concentrated in the revisional group, but the reason for elective admission could not be determined from administrative data. Operative rates declined modestly each year (adjusted odds ratio 0.91, 95% CI 0.84-0.98). Case mix differed between laparoscopic-first and open-first centers. CONCLUSIONS: In the largest contemporary national cohort to date, non-operative management dominated and increased during 2018-2022. Among operatively managed patients, laparoscopic patch repair was associated with shorter length of stay and a more favorable complication profile than open repair. Because operative approach was not randomized and patients selected for open repair may have carried greater physiologic severity or technical complexity, these associations support-but do not establish-a laparoscopic-first approach where anatomy and physiology permit. Prospective evidence is needed to refine operative vs. non-operative triage.

Evidence is limited to single-center series and one 2022 systematic review of approximately 600 patients; contemporary national International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10)-era data are lacking. METHODS: We queried the National Inpatient Sample (2018-2022) for adults with a perforated gastrojejunal ulcer and a code indicating prior bariatric surgery.
