title: Aortic Dissection Incidentally Detected on PET/CT During Evaluation for Suspected Multiple Myeloma.
abstract: The identification and diagnosis of aortic dissection on PET/CT remain challenging without the use of contrast agents. Such cases are prone to misdiagnosis or being overlooked, particularly when the examination is focused on an unrelated primary clinical objective. We present a case of thoracic aortic dissection that was incidentally detected on initial PET/CT during the further evaluation of suspected multiple myeloma. The FDG-avid lesion was initially mistaken for an esophageal mass, with differential diagnoses including extramedullary plasmacytoma associated with multiple myeloma and primary esophageal neoplasm.

title: Analysis of risk factors for venous thromboembolism in hospitalized patients with acute herpetic neuralgia and construction of a predictive nomogram model.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To explore the risk factors for venous thromboembolism (VTE) in hospitalized patients with acute herpetic neuralgia (AHN) and to construct a VTE prediction model based on clinical indicators to help clinicians better identify high-risk patients and develop prevention and treatment strategies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study retrospectively included 327 patients diagnosed with AHN who were hospitalized in the Pain Department of Hengshui People's Hospital between December 2020 and December 2023, of whom 26 developed VTE during hospitalization. The basic clinical data of the patients were collected, and the independent risk factors for VTE were screened by LASSO regression and multifactorial Logistic regression analysis, and the VTE prediction model was constructed. Model performance was evaluated by ROC curves, calibration curves, and decision curves, and internal validation was performed using ten-fold cross-validation and bootstrap resampling. RESULTS: P P P P The incidence of VTE in AHN patients was 7.95%. LASSO regression screened for 10 relevant variables, and final multifactor logistic regression analysis identified FIB (fibrinogen), FDP (fibrin degradation products), NRS (Numerical Rating Scale) score, and thrombotic risk score as independent predictors. Among them, FIB was a protective factor for VTE (OR = 0.477,= 0.006), while FDP (OR = 1.48,< 0.001), NRS score (OR = 1.584,= 0.039), and thrombotic risk score (OR = 2.05,< 0.001) were risk factors. The AUC of the prediction model was 0.853 (95% CI: 0.764-0.941), and the bootstrap optimism-corrected C-index was 0.834. At the optimal cutoff, the sensitivity and specificity were 0.731 and 0.877, respectively, with good calibration and clinical applicability. CONCLUSIONS: In this study, a VTE prediction model was constructed for patients with AHN. The model can accurately predict the risk of VTE in patients with AHN and provide a reference for clinical prevention and intervention; however, external validation in larger, multicenter cohorts is warranted before clinical implementation.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven imaging-based prediction models for hemorrhagic transformation after mechanical thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Hemorrhagic transformation (HT) is a major complication after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in acute ischemic stroke (AIS). Although artificial intelligence (AI)-driven imaging-based prediction models have shown promise for predicting HT, their overall predictive performance remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated their predictive performance. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, and CBM/SinoMed were searched from inception to July 2, 2026. Studies developing or validating AI-driven imaging-based prediction models for predicting HT after MT in AIS, including both pre- and post-procedural imaging predictors, were included. A random-effects model was used to pool the area under the curve (AUC), while a bivariate random-effects model was used to jointly estimate pooled sensitivity and specificity and construct the SROC curve. Subgroup analyses explored potential sources of heterogeneity. RESULTS: N I p 2 Eleven studies (total = 3,541) were included, 10 studies contributed eligible AUC estimates, with evaluation cohorts ranging from 18 to 261 participants. The pooled AUC was 0.891 (95% CI: 0.853-0.928), with low between-study heterogeneity ( = 29.0%, = 0.238). The bivariate random-effects model yielded a pooled sensitivity of 0.666 (95% CI: 0.578-0.744) and a pooled specificity of 0.919 (95% CI: 0.842-0.960). Exploratory subgroup analyses did not provide robust evidence supporting the superiority of any specific subgroup, and their interpretation was limited by small subgroup sizes and methodological heterogeneity. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited number of studies within individual subgroups. CONCLUSION: AI-driven imaging-based prediction models showed generally favorable discrimination in predicting HT after MT in AIS. However, current evidence does not establish the superiority of any specific model type. The predominance of retrospective studies, limited external validation, and methodological heterogeneity limit the generalizability of current findings. Large, multicenter prospective studies with rigorous external validation are needed before clinical implementation. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: The systematic review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261441463).

Although artificial intelligence (AI)-driven imaging-based prediction models have shown promise for predicting HT, their overall predictive performance remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated their predictive performance.

title: Hierarchies of vascular risk: gendered perceptions of arterial and venous disease.
abstract: This study explores how patients interpret vascular risk through the intersecting lenses of disease type and gender. Drawing on qualitative interviews with 28 patients in Italy diagnosed with peripheral arterial disease (PAD) or chronic venous disease (CVD), the analysis examines how individuals construct meanings around symptoms, risk, and care. Findings reveal a hierarchy of vascular risk in which arterial disease is perceived as life-threatening and generates vigilance, anxiety, and intensive self-monitoring, whereas venous disease is often normalized and trivialized within everyday life. Gender further shapes these perceptions: men tend to minimize symptoms and delay care, while women demonstrate greater bodily attentiveness and concern. Theoretically, the study advances the concept of a socially constructed hierarchy of vascular risk, showing how culturally differentiated meanings of disease severity intersect with gendered embodiment to shape risk perception, symptom interpretation, and healthcare engagement. By integrating sociological theories of risk, biographical disruption, and gendered embodiment within the study of vascular disease, the analysis extends risk scholarship to an underexplored clinical domain and demonstrates how biomedical risk is translated into socially differentiated lived experience.

title: Inflammatory bowel disease and the heart: how trained immunity shapes cardiovascular outcomes.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), comprising Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, is a chronic relapsing intestinal inflammatory disorder. Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a leading cause of death in patients with IBD, with elevated risks of myocardial infarction, heart failure, stroke, and venous thromboembolism that are independent of traditional risk factors. Disease activity and histological inflammation independently predict major adverse cardiovascular events, and Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis differ in cardiovascular risk profiles. This residual risk points to immune mechanisms that remain unclear. Trained immunity (TI), an innate immune memory induced by epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming, may link chronic intestinal inflammation to cardiovascular injury. This review integrates epidemiological and mechanistic evidence, outlines cardiovascular risk features in IBD, examines the molecular basis of TI and its roles in atherosclerosis, myocardial injury, and heart failure, and evaluates candidate biomarkers and targeted therapeutic strategies. We also discuss current limitations and challenges in clinical translation and propose future research directions, to inform mechanistic studies and clinical interventions for IBD-associated CVD.

title: Novel techniques in the prophylaxis and treatment of type II endoleaks: a narrative review.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Type II endoleaks (T2ELs) are a frequent complication after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR), posing a risk of aneurysm expansion. This review evaluates modern techniques for T2ELs management, moving beyond traditional embolization methods. METHODS: Recent controlled trials and observational studies were analyzed to trace evidence on conventional and novel techniques employed in managing T2ELs. RESULTS: Novel techniques, such as transcaval embolization (TCE) and laser-assisted transgraft embolization (LATE), have demonstrated encouraging early technical and clinical outcomes, although the available evidence remains limited. In addition, shape memory polymer (SMP) embolization resulted in significant sac shrinkage in >85% of patients and prevented clinically significant T2ELs. CONCLUSIONS: TCE, LATE, and prophylactic SMP embolization are promising alternatives to conventional methods, offering high technical success and the potential to reduce reinterventions. Larger studies are needed to confirm long-term outcomes and define optimal use.

title: Tissue-specific moderate DNA methylation alterations featuring hypomethylation in microRNA regulatory regions associated with advanced carotid atherosclerosis.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: DNA methylation is an important epigenetic mechanism involved in the regulation of gene expression, but its contribution to the regulation of microRNA genes in atherosclerosis remains poorly understood. METHODS: MIR10B, MIR21, MIR100, MIR127, and MIR143 We profiled DNA methylation of regulatory elements and gene bodies of five microRNA genes () in vascular tissues and paired peripheral blood leukocytes from 92 patients with advanced carotid atherosclerosis along with peripheral blood leukocytes of 32 subclinical atherosclerosis controls, using targeted bisulfite sequencing. RESULTS: MIR10B, MIR127 MIR100 MIR100 MIR127 MIR100 MIR10B, MIR21 MIR127 MIR10B, MIR21 MIR100 MIR10B MIR143 MIR21 MIR10B MIR143HG CARMN We identified distinct tissue-specific DNA methylation patterns for all studied regions of microRNA genes. The regulatory regions of, andwere moderately hypomethylated in carotid atherosclerotic plaques compared with intact vascular tissues. We further integrated our findings with lab-internal and publicly available epigenome-wide methylation datasets and evaluated the contribution of vascular and blood cell composition using computational deconvolution. After adjustment for estimated vascular cell proportions, methylation at CpG sites within theandregions remained associated with atherosclerosis. Increased DNA methylation at a single CpG site (chr11:122025143, GRCh37/hg19) located in theE-box region was associated with metabolic syndrome, while DNA methylation levels of, andin atherosclerotic plaques were linked with indicators of histological instability and a history of acute cerebrovascular events. In peripheral blood cells, we observed moderate hypomethylation, predominantly at individual CpG sites within the regulatory regions of, and theE-box region in patients compared with controls. However, MIR10B methylation showed weak associations with estimated blood cell composition. In blood,andmethylation correlated with lipid metabolism and carotid stenosis, while theCpG island showed strong correspondence between blood and plaque methylation. Using miRNA-seq to analyze microRNA expression in vascular samples, we identified miR-143-3p, miR-21-5p, miR-100-5p, miR-145-5p, miR-145-3p, and miR-10b-5p as the most highly expressed microRNAs. Methylation of CpG sites withinand() promoters was inversely associated with the expression of the corresponding microRNAs. DISCUSSION: Advanced carotid atherosclerosis is characterized by specific moderate tissue-associated DNA methylation patterns of microRNA genes, predominantly involving hypomethylation of regulatory regions. These epigenetic shifts, driven both by changes in vascular cell composition and the functional state of the vessel wall, enable highly coordinated regulation of microRNA expression profiles. These findings highlight promising candidate loci and biomarkers for predicting the complicated course of atherosclerosis, which warrants further validation in larger independent cohorts.

title: De-escalated rivaroxaban in postoperative isolated distal deep vein thrombosis: a propensity score-matched study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In postoperative isolated distal deep vein thrombosis (IDDVT), anticoagulation intensity is frequently constrained by bleeding risk, which may compromise treatment continuity and clinical effectiveness. OBJECTIVES: To compare the effectiveness and safety of a de-escalated (rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily) versus standard-maintenance rivaroxaban regimen for postoperative IDDVT in a real-world surgical cohort. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients diagnosed with IDDVT following urological surgery between 2013 and 2025. Patients received rivaroxaban at either a low maintenance dose (10 mg once daily) or a standard maintenance dose (20 mg once daily) according to routine clinical practice. Propensity score matching (1:1) was applied to balance baseline characteristics, incorporating surgical approach (endoscopic vs. major structural procedures) as a surrogate for surgical trauma and bleeding risk. The primary outcome was thrombus progression to proximal deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism. Secondary outcomes included IDDVT resolution and clinically relevant non-major bleeding (CRNMB). Competing-risk analyses were performed. RESULTS: P P P After matching, 152 patients were included (76 per group). Thrombus progression did not differ significantly between groups (subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR] 1.29; 95% CI 0.48-3.46; = 0.613). No statistically significant difference in IDDVT resolution was detected between the two groups (SHR 0.93; 95% CI, 0.64-1.36; = 0.721). The low-dose regimen was associated with a significantly lower risk of CRNMB (HR 0.31; 95% CI, 0.11-0.85; = 0.023) and fewer early bleeding-related treatment interruptions. Early postoperative hematuria was more frequent in the standard-dose group. CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center retrospective cohort of patients with isolated distal deep vein thrombosis after urological surgery, low-dose rivaroxaban (10 mg once daily) was associated with a lower incidence of clinically relevant non-major bleeding than 20 mg once daily. No statistically significant differences were detected between regimens in thrombus progression or complete thrombus resolution. However, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalent antithrombotic efficacy, given nonrandomized treatment allocation, residual confounding, limited sample size, and wide confidence intervals for thrombotic outcomes. The results are hypothesis-generating and support studies-preferably randomized non-inferiority trials-to determine whether dose de-escalation can provide an acceptable balance between thrombotic protection and bleeding risk in postoperative patients.

OBJECTIVES: To compare the effectiveness and safety of a de-escalated (rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily) versus standard-maintenance rivaroxaban regimen for postoperative IDDVT in a real-world surgical cohort. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients diagnosed with IDDVT following urological surgery between 2013 and 2025.

title: Perioperative prothrombin time activity trajectories and subsequent mortality after surgical repair of acute type A aortic dissection.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Perioperative prothrombin time activity (PTA) changes rapidly during surgical repair of acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD), but single measurements do not capture heterogeneous longitudinal patterns. We sought to identify recurring perioperative PTA trajectories, characterize their clinical context, and examine their association with subsequent all-cause mortality. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 284 adults who underwent ATAAD repair from 2021 through 2023. Group-based trajectory modeling used the last preoperative and observed postoperative day (POD) 1-7 PTA measurements. Patients required at least three observed PTA measurements for trajectory modeling. Mortality analyses began immediately after POD7. The primary Cox model adjusted for age and sex; Firth regression addressed sparse events. Incremental information beyond last preoperative PTA was evaluated by a prespecified likelihood-ratio comparison. RESULTS: P P P P P The trajectory cohort comprised 268 patients with 1,895 observations and 27 deaths after POD7. Four perioperative PTA trajectory groups were identified: moderate-stable [87 (32.5%)], low-declining [50 (18.7%)], preserved-rapidly-declining [61 (22.8%)], and high-preserved [70 (26.1%)]. Cumulative mortality differed globally (log-rank = 0.00210), and trajectory group remained associated with subsequent mortality in the age- and sex-adjusted Cox model (global = 0.0322) and Firth sensitivity analysis (global = 0.0481). The prespecified direct low-declining-versus-preserved-rapidly-declining comparison did not demonstrate a clear difference. Adding trajectory group to age, sex, and last preoperative PTA did not show clear incremental information (likelihood-ratio = 0.304; Firth = 0.380). After exclusion of mechanical-valve recipients, the principal trajectory structure was largely preserved, although this sensitivity analysis did not exclude treatment-related effects on PTA. CONCLUSION: Four reproducible perioperative PTA trajectories characterized distinct longitudinal patterns and were associated with mortality after the POD7 landmark. These trajectories should be interpreted as composite perioperative patterns reflecting both disease and treatment context rather than as intrinsic coagulation states. They were not ordered mortality-risk tiers and did not show clear incremental prognostic information beyond last preoperative PTA. External validation is required.

We sought to identify recurring perioperative PTA trajectories, characterize their clinical context, and examine their association with subsequent all-cause mortality. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 284 adults who underwent ATAAD repair from 2021 through 2023.

title: Comparison of ultrasound-guided oblique-axis versus short-axis approaches for right internal jugular vein cannulation in the left decubitus position: a prospective, randomized, single-center trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Central venous cannulation in the left decubitus position is more difficult than in the supine position and may be required when patients cannot safely return to supine. Whether the oblique-axis (OA) approach improves the success and safety of right internal jugular vein (RIJV) cannulation compared with the short-axis (SA) approach remains unknown. METHODS: Seventy-four patients (ASA I-III) scheduled for elective surgery in the left decubitus position under general anesthesia requiring RIJV cannulation were randomly assigned 1:1 to the OA or SA group (n = 37 each). Under real-time ultrasound guidance and a 20° Trendelenburg tilt, cannulation was performed by one of three experienced attending anesthesiologists, each with more than 15 years of experience in ultrasound-guided central venous cannulation. Venipuncture attempts and total procedure time were recorded by a separate investigator; patients were blinded by general anesthesia. The primary outcome was first-time puncture success; secondary outcomes were overall cannulation success, procedure time, venipuncture attempts, and mechanical complications. RESULTS: All 74 randomized patients completed the trial and were analyzed. The first-time puncture success rate was higher in the OA group (27/37 [73.0%] vs. 18/37 [48.6%]; risk difference 24.3%, 95% CI 2.8% to 45.9%; P = 0.032, Pearson chi-square test; Fisher exact test P = 0.056). Venipuncture attempts were fewer in the OA group (median 1 vs. 2; IQR 1-2; P = 0.037). Total procedure time did not differ significantly between groups (median 2.79 [IQR 2.46-3.19] vs. 3.01 [2.72-3.45] min; P = 0.060). Mechanical complications occurred in 6 of 37 patients (16.2%) in the SA group (one arterial puncture and five posterior wall penetrations) and in none in the OA group (P = 0.025); overall cannulation success was 100% in both groups. CONCLUSIONS: For RIJV cannulation in the left decubitus position, the oblique-axis approach was associated with a higher first-time puncture success rate than the short-axis approach and with fewer mechanical complications detected during or immediately after the procedure; however, the primary-endpoint evidence was borderline and the complication estimates were imprecise. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400091385; registered 28 October 2024).

title: Safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System in acute intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism: the SPIRARE II pivotal trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Percutaneous aspiration thrombectomy can rapidly reduce afterload in acute pulmonary embolism (PE), but catheter stiffness and instability may limit access and prevent effective right ventricle (RV) unloading. The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System with Transforming Fixation (TFX) technology is designed to address current limitations of existing catheter-based systems by separating the flexibility necessary for safe navigation from the support that is essential for procedural control. AIMS: We aimed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System for mechanical aspiration thrombectomy in acute intermediate-risk PE. METHODS: SPIRARE II was a prospective, single-arm, multicentre pivotal investigation conducted at 19 sites in the United States and Europe. Eligible patients had acute PE (≤14 days), a computed tomography angiography-assessed RV to left ventricle (RV/LV) ratio>0.9, and haemodynamic stability (systolic blood pressure ≥90 mmHg). Co-primary endpoints were composite major adverse events (MAE) within 48 hours and core laboratory-assessed RV/LV change from baseline to 48 hours. Prespecified secondary endpoints were collected immediately pre- and post-procedure in all patients including mean pulmonary artery pressure, total pulmonary vascular resistance, and cardiac index. RESULTS: In 123 patients, the 48-hour composite MAE rate was 2.4% (3/123), meeting the prespecified performance goal (one-sided p<0.0001). The mean RV/LV diameter ratio decreased from 1.44±0.33 at baseline to 1.05±0.21 at 48 hours, a mean reduction of 0.39±0.33, exceeding the prespecified performance goal (p<0.0001). CONCLUSIONS: The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System met its prespecified safety and effectiveness endpoints in acute intermediate-risk PE. TFX delivered precise, stable control with reliable vessel access, enabling consistent right ventricular unloading. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06576427).

title: Noninvasive hemodynamics of nonthrombotic iliac vein lesions are disturbed in patients with a history of deep vein thrombosis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Nonthrombotic iliac vein lesions (NIVLs) are thought to be associated with deep vein thrombosis (DVT), yet most individuals with NIVL never develop thrombotic complications. This study assessed whether ultrasound-derived hemodynamic measurements differ between NIVL patients with and without a history of DVT, and whether these hemodynamic measurements better discriminate DVT history than percent stenosis alone. METHODS: We performed a retrospective case control study of patients evaluated at a tertiary academic referral center between 2022 and 2025 who underwent pelvic venous duplex ultrasound imaging. Patients with left common iliac vein (LCIV) stenoses greater than 20% were included and categorized by history of left lower-extremity DVT. Exclusion criteria included concurrent DVT or previous venous stenting. Ultrasound images were digitized to obtain vessel diameters and spectral Doppler velocities in the iliac veins. Mean velocity, peak velocity, flow rate, shear rate, and ipsilateral and contralateral ratios were calculated. Continuous variables were compared using Welch t-tests, with statistical significance defined as P < .05. RESULTS: 2 2 2 2 Forty-five patients were included, comprising nine patients with previous DVT and 36 without. Among all metrics, velocity-based metrics at the compressed LCIV showed the strongest associations with a history of previous DVT, including ipsilateral velocity ratio [logfold change (FC), -1.539; P = .007], peak velocity (logFC, -0.999; P = .002), and mean velocity (logFC, -0.989; P = .002). Differences in percent stenosis were statistically significant but less discriminative than velocity-based metrics (logFC, 0.363; P = .033). Composite metrics such as flow rate and shear rate demonstrated weaker discrimination. Dimensionality reduction analysis revealed distinct clustering based on multivariate hemodynamic features between patients with and without a history of DVT. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with NIVL, decreased velocity through the LCIV at the compression point was the strongest predictor of previous DVT, whereas percent stenosis was less discriminative. This study suggests that ultrasound-derived hemodynamic assessment can potentially provide a functional framework for risk stratification in patients with NIVL, but further prospective studies are needed to validate its clinical utility.

title: A pilot study of the InVera Infusion Device: Twelve-month outcomes in the treatment of incompetent saphenous veins.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The InVera Infusion Device (IVID; InVera Medical) is a novel catheter designed for the delivery of sclerosant agents during nonthermal, nontumescent ablation of incompetent superficial truncal veins of the lower extremity. This device pilot study aimed to evaluate the technical success, safety, and 12-month clinical outcome. METHODS: A single-center, prospective pilot study enrolled 10 patients with primary symptomatic axial reflux who underwent chemical ablation procedures with sclerosant delivery using the IVID. Primary outcomes assessed were technical procedural success, adverse events, revised Venous Clinical Severity Score (rVCSS), patient-reported outcomes based on a Heaviness, Achiness, Swelling, Throbbing, and Itching (HASTI) symptom questionnaire, and anatomical success rates from duplex ultrasound examination at baseline, 1 and 8 weeks, 3, 6, and 12 months postprocedure. Baseline and 12-month postprocedures were compared for both the rVCSS and the HASTI results using a paired t-test and a Wilcoxon signed-rank test respectively. RESULTS: Technical procedural success was 100%. There were no device-related adverse events or serious adverse events including no deep vein thrombosis recorded throughout the follow-up period. Clinician assessed rVCSS and patient reported HASTI scores both showed statistically significant reductions from baseline to 12 months (adjusted P = .03 for both). Ultrasound-based anatomical assessment at 12 months demonstrated elimination of abnormal reflux and complete or partial occlusion in 90% of patients. CONCLUSIONS: The IVID provides a safe and effective technique for the delivery of sclerosant agents as part of the management of incompetent saphenous veins, demonstrating favorable 12-month anatomical, clinical and patient-reported outcomes in this pilot cohort.

title: Systematic review of devices, designs, and trials for the treatment of deep venous reflux.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Chronic venous insufficiency is driven primarily by venous reflux and affects nearly one-third of adults. Although superficial reflux is effectively treated with ablation, therapeutic options for deep venous reflux (DVR) remain limited. Despite decades of innovation, no prosthetic or bioprosthetic venous valve has achieved U.S. regulatory approval. We systematically reviewed device strategies, clinical and hemodynamic outcomes, complications, and barriers to translation for devices designed to treat DVR. METHODS: We conducted an International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420251101761) of six databases from inception through February 2026, including in vivo animal and human studies evaluating prosthetic or bioprosthetic devices for DVR. Studies of native valve repair or autotransplantation were excluded. The primary outcome for human studies was clinical improvement, and secondary outcomes included patency, procedural complications, valvular function, and thrombosis. RESULTS: Of 516 records identified, 15 met inclusion criteria: eight human and seven animal studies. Two principal strategies were identified: intraluminal valve restoration and external compression, with approximately 40% of devices delivered percutaneously or endovenously. In human studies, technical success ranged from 87.7% to 100%, patency from 67% to 100%, and perioperative complication rates from 0% to 44%, consisting primarily of bleeding, wound infection, and valve thrombosis. Valve occlusion occurred in up to 28% of animal implants and 18% to 22% of select human cohorts. Two perioperative deaths occurred in animal studies; none were reported in human studies. Among human studies, valve competency assessment methods varied substantially. Reported competency ranged from 0% to 92%, reflecting heterogeneity in imaging modalities and definitions. Discordance between anatomic patency, duplex-derived reflux reduction, and clinical improvement was frequently observed. In contemporary multicenter trial data, fewer than half of patients met predefined reflux-reduction end points despite high device patency and substantial clinical improvement, highlighting discordance between anatomic, hemodynamic, and patient-centered outcomes. By 1 year, pain had improved in 75% to 97% of patients; revised Venous Clinical Severity Scores decreased by 37% to 81%, with clinically meaningful (≥3-point) improvement in up to 84.6%; and ulcer healing ranged from 67% to 100%. Longer follow-up extended to 2 years in animal studies and up to 11 years in human series with various outcomes reported. CONCLUSIONS: Several devices developed for DVR have demonstrated technical feasibility and symptom improvement. However, the risk of thrombosis, the marginal impact on valvular function, and the lack of standardization and selection of adequate end points in the measurement of results remain major barriers to regulatory approval. Standardized composite end points integrating objective hemodynamic measures with patient-centered outcomes are essential to advance durable DVR device development and clinical translation.

title: Impact of prolonged balloon inflation on valve expansion and early clinical outcomes following contemporary balloon-expandable transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Incomplete expansion of balloon-expandable (BE) transcatheter heart valves (THVs) after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) may affect valve performance and durability. Routine THV post-dilatation (the "double-tap" technique) has been proposed to optimise device expansion; however, it may increase procedural complexity. AIMS: We sought to evaluate the impact of a prolonged balloon inflation implantation strategy on BE THV expansion, haemodynamic performance, and early clinical outcomes. METHODS: This single-centre study analysed consecutive TAVI patients treated for native tricuspid aortic stenosis with the SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA THV using a prolonged balloon inflation strategy (8 seconds). Valve expansion was assessed by fluoroscopy at multiple frame levels and compared with three validated reference standards. Results were also descriptively compared with previously published data on the double-tap technique. Clinical and haemodynamic outcomes at 30 days were adjudicated according to Valve Academic Research Consortium 3 criteria. RESULTS: A total of 84 patients (mean age 78.8 years, 58% male, median Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score 3.9%) were included. Prolonged inflation resulted in complete THV expansion at the inflow and outflow levels, with only mild underexpansion (98.5±1.3%) detected at the midframe level when manufacturer-defined nominal values were used as the reference. When compared with previously published data on the double-tap technique, expansion values for the 23, 26, and 29 mm valves were consistently similar or higher, whereas lower expansion was observed for the 20 mm size. Device success was achieved in all cases, with no stroke at 30 days. Permanent pacemaker implantation occurred in 6% of patients. Haemodynamic performance was favourable (mean gradient 9.2 [interquartile range 7.0-10.3] mmHg at 30 days), with no patients having moderate or severe paravalvular leak. CONCLUSIONS: Prolonged balloon inflation during BE THV deployment is associated with favourable valve expansion, haemodynamic results, and a favourable safety profile, consistent with values reported in double-tap series. If confirmed in larger studies, this strategy may represent a simple alternative to routine double-tap in selected patients.

title: Magnetic resonance imaging vs computed tomography for baseline imaging evaluation in acute basilar artery occlusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The optimal imaging modality, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT), for identifying good treatment candidates among patients with acute basilar-artery occlusion (BAO) remains unclear. METHODS: This was a post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION trial. Patients were categorized into MRI or CT groups according to the baseline imaging modality. The primary outcome was mRS 0-3 at 90 days. The secondary outcomes included mRS score shift on an ordinal scale, early neurological deterioration, time from stroke onset to arterial puncture, and time from onset to randomization. The safety outcome was mortality within 90 days. Clinical outcomes and workflow times were compared between the two groups. RESULTS: Among 340 patients (CT: n = 277; MRI: n = 63), baseline imaging was not significantly associated with 90-day mRS 0-3 in the overall cohort (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.50-1.95; P = 0.976). It remained highly consistent across both the endovascular treatment and best medical management subgroups. Baseline MRI assessment was not associated with significant workflow delays compared with CT, including time from stroke onset to randomization (mean difference [MD] 5.23 min; P = 0.843) and time to puncture (MD 13.16 min; P = 0.701). Furthermore, the association between imaging modality and outcomes was consistent across different time windows. DISCUSSION: In patients with acute BAO, we did not observe evidence supporting the preferential use of MRI over CT as the primary imaging strategy for patient selection. Conventional imaging appears sufficient as a first-line tool for selecting patients in clinical practice.

title: Unintended shifts in high-priority adult heart transplant listings after the OPTN's September 2025 policy change.
abstract: The Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network amended Status 2 heart allocation criteria in September 2025, requiring documented failure of high-dose inotropes before candidates could qualify via intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) or percutaneous endovascular ventricular assist device (PEVAD) support. Using OPTN data, we compared seasonally matched pre-policy (September 2024 to June 2025, n=4206) and post-policy (September 2025 to June 2026, n=4231) adult candidates. While standard Status 3 high-dose inotrope listings increased 2.0% to 4.1% and standard Status 2 IABP/PEVAD listings decreased 18.2% to 11.0%, Status 1 listings and Status 2 exceptions increased 7.7% to 10.6% and 17.5% to 21.5%, respectively (all p<0.001). Consequently, combined initial Status 1/2 listings were unchanged (44.5% vs 44.0%, p=0.71). Furthermore, overall transplant volume remained similar, but status at transplant shifted from standard Status 2 toward Status 2 exceptions and Status 1. Tightening standard Status 2 eligibility was associated with redistribution across high-priority pathways rather than reduced high-priority listings.

title: Plasma neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin levels and risk of future incident venous thromboembolism.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although neutrophils are suggested to play a role in the pathogenesis of venous thromboembolism (VTE), no study has investigated whether neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL), a marker of neutrophil activation, is associated with future VTE risk in the general population. OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between plasma NGAL levels and the risk of future VTE. METHODS: Plasma NGAL levels were measured in 416 VTE cases and 848 age- and sex-matched controls in a nested case-control study derived from the Tromsø study cohort (1994-2007). Logistic regression models were used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) with 95% CIs for VTE according to quartiles of plasma NGAL, adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, arterial cardiovascular disease, cancer, and C-reactive protein. Separate analyses with follow-up restricted to the first 2 and 5 years after cohort inclusion were conducted to investigate potential short-term associations. RESULTS: We found no association between NGAL levels and risk of future VTE when analyzing the entire study period (OR for highest vs lowest quartile of NGAL: 1.02, 95% CI, 0.70-1.51). However, when follow-up was restricted to 2 years, higher NGAL levels were associated with increased risk of future VTE (OR, 3.87; 95% CI, 1.15-13.03). The association was attenuated when follow-up was extended to 5 years (OR, 1.51; 95% CI, 0.82-2.80). CONCLUSION: Higher plasma NGAL levels were associated with a transiently increased risk of future VTE.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between plasma NGAL levels and the risk of future VTE. METHODS: Plasma NGAL levels were measured in 416 VTE cases and 848 age- and sex-matched controls in a nested case-control study derived from the Tromsø study cohort (1994-2007).

title: SGLT2 Inhibitors and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients With Moderate-to-Severe Psoriasis Receiving Biologic Therapy: A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis have an increased risk of cardiovascular disease. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors provide cardiovascular benefits, but their association with cardiovascular outcomes in patients with psoriasis remains insufficiently studied. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the global TriNetX research network. Patients older than 40 years with plaque psoriasis receiving biologic therapy were categorized according to SGLT2 inhibitor use. Propensity score matching was performed to balance demographic characteristics, cardiovascular risk factors, kidney disease, and concomitant antidiabetic medications. RESULTS: After matching, 2016 patients were included in each cohort. SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with a significantly lower incidence of acute myocardial infarction (HR, 0.601; 95%CI, 0.426-0.849), stroke (HR, 0.553; 95%CI, 0.381-0.804), heart failure (HR, 0.751; 95%CI, 0.581-0.970), peripheral artery disease (HR, 0.648; 95%CI, 0.470-0.894), and angina pectoris (HR, 0.601; 95%CI, 0.404-0.894). No significant association was observed for transient ischemic attack. CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with favorable cardiovascular outcomes in patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis receiving biologic therapy. These findings support further prospective investigation of SGLT2 inhibitors as a potential strategy for cardiovascular risk reduction in this population.

title: Asymptomatic Versus Symptomatic Carotid Revascularization: A Single Institution Retrospective Review.
abstract: BACKGROUND: While carotid revascularization reduces stroke risk in both asymptomatic (AD) and symptomatic (SD) carotid diseases, its role continues to evolve with advances in medical therapy, surgical techniques, and cost considerations. METHODS: This retrospective study reviews outcomes of patients undergoing revascularization at a level 1 stroke center between 2019 and 2024. Primary endpoints were ipsilateral stroke, myocardial infarction (MI), and death at 30 days, 90 days, and 1 year. Secondary endpoints include restenosis rates. RESULTS: A total of 113 patients underwent 127 carotid endarterectomies. Sixty-four percent presented with SD, with a median time to intervention of 9 days (interquartile range 6-11). Patients with SD had a longer median length of stay (2 vs. 1 day, P = 0.076. Follow-up rates were higher in AD at 1 year (65% vs. 36%, P = 0.003). MI rates were 0% at 30 days and 90 days and 0.9% at 1 year. Stroke rates were 0.9%, 0.9%, and 1.8% at 30 days, 90 days, and 1 year, with no difference between AD versus SD. One-year mortality rates were 0.9% and 5.3% at 90 days and 1 year, without a difference by AD versus SD. Restenosis occurred in 4% of patients, with no difference between groups. CONCLUSION: Carotid endarterectomy was associated with low perioperative rates of ipsilateral stroke, MI, and death. Despite a longer length of stay, patients with SD did not have significantly different outcomes or restenosis rates. While males had improved follow-up rates, there was no significant difference in outcomes by gender or race. These findings support favorable outcomes following CEA in both AD and SD.

title: Vein of Galen malformation in newborns and children: contemporary advances and future directions.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Vein of Galen malformation is a rare and complex cerebrovascular disorder associated with significant morbidity and mortality from the fetal period through childhood. Advances in perinatal care, neuroimaging, endovascular therapy, and multidisciplinary management have improved survival and expanded therapeutic options, while generating new challenges in clinical strategies and long-term outcomes. OBJECTIVE: This review integrates evidence and expert perspectives presented during the II International Meeting on Vein of Galen Malformation in Newborns and Children, held in Camogli, Italy, in October 2025 and summarizes current advances, emerging developments, and priorities for research and clinical innovation. RECENT ADVANCES: Current developments include improved fetal and neonatal imaging, emerging prognostic biomarkers, fetal intervention, advances in endovascular treatment, and increasing understanding of underlying genetic and molecular mechanisms. Contemporary management increasingly integrates cardiovascular and neurological assessment, advanced neuroimaging, individualized endovascular strategies, and structured long-term neurodevelopmental follow-up. The development of a disease-specific registry reflects the growing impact of international collaboration. FUTURE DIRECTIONS: Major priorities include validation of risk-stratification tools, development of standardized imaging and neurodevelopmental biomarkers, refinement of fetal and neonatal interventions, improved understanding of disease biology, and multicenter data sharing. Family-centered care and standardized long-term outcome assessment should remain integral components of future VOGM research and clinical practice. CONCLUSIONS: VOGM management is rapidly evolving from survival-focused treatment toward individualized, multidisciplinary care extending from fetal diagnosis through childhood and adulthood. This review provides a comprehensive overview of current knowledge and emerging developments in this field, while defining a multidisciplinary, internationally informed roadmap for future research.

Advances in perinatal care, neuroimaging, endovascular therapy, and multidisciplinary management have improved survival and expanded therapeutic options, while generating new challenges in clinical strategies and long-term outcomes. title: Development and internal validation of a parsimonious model for neurological deterioration at 48 h after endovascular thrombectomy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The incremental value of routine admission measurements for predicting early neurological deterioration after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) remains unclear. METHODS: This retrospective single-center reanalysis used a 2020-2022 registry. END48 was defined as an increase of at least 4 National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) points from admission to the fixed 48-h postoperative assessment. The conservative primary cohort excluded an unresolved longitudinal data segment. A revision-stage locked five-predictor logistic regression model included admission NIHSS scores, age, glucose levels, white blood cell count, and ln triglyceride value, with the NIHSS-only model serving as the comparator. Internal validation used 1,000 bootstrap samples and paired nested intervals of 1,000 outer × 100 inner samples. RESULTS: Post-hoc Of the 253 records representing 251 unique patients, 214 adults entered the primary cohort; 51 (23.8%) had END48. The primary model had an apparent area under the curve (AUC) of 0.651 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.601 (0.511 to 0.723). The corrected AUC difference vs. the NIHSS-only model was 0.038 (-0.025 to 0.171). The corrected Brier score was 0.180, compared to a prevalence-only reference of 0.182, resulting in a Brier skill score of 0.9%. The corrected primary calibration slope was 0.731 (0.519 to 0.892). Incremental net benefit was -0.015, 0.036, and 0.013 at 10%, 20%, and 30% thresholds, respectively; all corresponding 95% confidence intervals crossed zero.Riley assessments across plausible model-fit assumptions indicated that the available cohort was below the sample size desirable for model development. The reconstructed cohort sensitivity analysis did not change the overall interpretation. CONCLUSION: Discrimination was limited, improvement in probability accuracy was marginal, and incremental discrimination and net benefit were uncertain. The model should be regarded as exploratory rather than clinically implementable; independent validation and improved outcome ascertainment are required.

title: The snake-head sign on MRI in craniocervical junction dural arteriovenous fistulas: a novel imaging feature and a hypothesis of venous remodeling and congestion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Craniocervical junction (CCJ)-region dural arteriovenous fistulas (dAVFs) are rare but potentially reversible causes of venous congestive myelopathy, often difficult to recognize due to non-specific presentation. We observed a characteristic pattern of intramedullary T2 hyperintensity on sagittal MRI, involving the medulla and upper cervical cord with a rostral end divided into ventral and dorsal limbs, which we termed the "snake-head sign." This study aimed to characterize the prevalence of this feature among reported CCJ-region dAVF cases and explore its clinical and anatomical correlates. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed published cases of CCJ-region or adjacent dAVFs reported between 1996 and 2026 that included retrievable sagittal T2-weighted or FLAIR images. The presence of the snake-head sign was assessed, and clinical, angiographic, and treatment-related variables were extracted, including fistula location, feeding artery, draining vein direction, treatment modality, and outcome. Associations with the sign were evaluated using univariate analyses. Given the retrospective, literature-based design and limited sample size, findings were considered hypothesis-generating. RESULTS: Among 64 reported cases, the snake-head sign was identified in 31 (48.4%). No significant associations were found between the sign and age, sex, symptom duration, feeding artery, treatment modality, or outcome. However, a non-significant trend was observed for venous drainage configuration: cases with cranial convergence of the draining vein toward the CCJ more frequently demonstrated the sign, whereas purely caudal drainage patterns showed it less often. Fistulas at lower cervical nerve-root sleeves, requiring a longer cranial venous course, also showed higher sign frequency. These findings suggest the sign may reflect venous outflow geometry rather than arterial source or fistula location. CONCLUSION: The snake-head sign is a recognizable MRI feature present in roughly half of reported CCJ-region dAVF cases. Its identification may raise clinical suspicion for CCJ-related dAVF, particularly in unexplained venous congestive myelopathy. The trend toward a higher frequency of the sign in cases with cranially convergent venous drainage raises the hypothesis that it reflects concentrated venous congestion at this anatomical transition zone. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized imaging review and angiographic correlation are needed to confirm its diagnostic value and clarify the underlying mechanism.

title: Comparative outcomes of arteriovenous accesses with and without tunneled hemodialysis catheters: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: This study compared patency rates of arteriovenous accesses with and without concurrent tunneled hemodialysis catheter (THC) use, addressing limited research on combined outcomes. A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted on patients undergoing arteriovenous access creation at a single hospital between January 2021 and December 2022. Primary outcomes were the 6-month primary patency rate and functional dialysis success. Secondary outcomes were the factors associated with each of these endpoints. Statistical analyses employed t tests, chi-square tests, logistic regression, and Kaplan-Meier survival curves. A total of 319 vascular accesses were included. The 6-month patency rate was significantly higher in the access-only group than in the access + THC group (87.04% vs 78.20%, P = .04). THC usage (odds ratio [OR] = 0.49, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.25-0.95, P = .03), graft usage (OR = 0.38, 95% CI: 0.18-0.82, P = .01), and higher hemoglobin levels (OR = 0.80, 95% CI: 0.65-0.96, P = .02) were associated with reduced patency rates. Functional dialysis success at 6 months did not differ significantly between groups (87.96% vs 83.89%, P = .21). However, older age (OR = 0.96, 95% CI: 0.93-0.99, P = .01), use of a cubital artery to an autologous vein (OR = 0.39, 95% CI: 0.19-0.82, P = .01) or graft (OR = 0.40, 95% CI: 0.17-0.97, P = .04), and higher hemoglobin levels (OR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.66-0.99, P = .03) were associated with a lower likelihood of functional dialysis success. Concurrent THC use was independently associated with reduced 6-month primary patency without a corresponding reduction in the short-term delivery of dialysis, suggesting an increased need for interventions to maintain the access. Judicious use of THCs and careful consideration of the vascular access type are important to optimize vascular access outcomes in patients undergoing hemodialysis.

A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted on patients undergoing arteriovenous access creation at a single hospital between January 2021 and December 2022. Primary outcomes were the 6-month primary patency rate and functional dialysis success.

title: The emerging molecular landscape of abdominal aortic aneurysms: non-coding RNAs as diagnostic and therapeutic targets.
abstract: An abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a progressive, often asymptomatic condition whose rupture is associated with a high mortality rate. Ultrasonography and computed tomography are established diagnostic methods, while molecular biomarkers may provide additional information about disease activity. This review discusses the potential role of non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) as diagnostic and therapeutic tools in AAAs. These molecules, including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) and circular RNAs (circRNAs), are strongly involved in the regulation of gene expression. Through binding to their target mRNAs, miRNAs primarily suppress translation or promote mRNA degradation. Some lncRNAs and circRNAs act as miRNA sponges, affecting their availability. Here, these mechanisms are discussed by pathological function, distinguishing human tissue and circulating studies from animal, cellular and computational findings. Particular attention is given to miR-21, H19, GAS5, circCdyl and miR-26b-3p, which have functional experimental evidence or human biomarker data beyond expression profiling. Abnormal expression can be detected in peripheral blood or aortic tissue, but these findings do not necessarily predict aneurysm growth or rupture. Integration of ncRNA profiling with imaging and clinical parameters may improve the assessment of AAAs. However, prospective validation and further studies of delivery and safety are needed before these molecules can be used in clinical practice.

title: Apparent Diffusion Coefficient Composition and Tissue Heterogeneity as Predictors of Functional Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy in Patients With Large Ischemic Core.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Recent trials established endovascular thrombectomy efficacy in large ischemic cores, yet outcomes remain heterogeneous despite similar infarct volumes, suggesting that current volumetric assessments may not fully capture tissue viability. We examined whether tissue composition quantified by apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) distribution and tissue heterogeneity within baseline diffusion-weighted imaging lesions are associated with functional outcomes in large-core patients after successful endovascular thrombectomy. METHODS: -6 2 We retrospectively analyzed patients with large vessel occlusion with large ischemic cores (diffusion-weighted imaging candidate volume ≥50 mL) achieving successful reperfusion after endovascular thrombectomy. We quantified ADC tissue composition as proportions within 3 ADC ranges relative to total diffusion-weighted imaging lesion volume: low (<540), mid (540-700), and high (>700 × 10mm/s). Separately, tissue heterogeneity was assessed using Shannon entropy, a metric quantifying ADC distribution heterogeneity. The primary outcome was 3-month good functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score of 0-3), analyzed via adjusted logistic regression. RESULTS: P P Among 126 patients (age, 70.8±12.4 years; 60.3% men; diffusion-weighted imaging candidate volume, 93.7±41.2 mL), 39.7% achieved a good functional outcome. Both tissue heterogeneity (adjusted odds ratio, 1.45 per 0.1-unit increase, 1.09-1.93,=0.011, area under the curve, 0.671) and mid-ADC fraction (adjusted odds ratio, 1.78 per 5% increase, 1.20-2.63,=0.004, area under the curve, 0.688) were associated with good functional outcomes. Neither low-ADC nor high-ADC fractions showed significant associations with functional outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: -6 2 Higher mid-ADC (540-700 × 10mm/s) fraction and greater tissue heterogeneity predicted favorable outcomes in patients with large ischemic core, indicating that tissue composition within the ischemic core, beyond its volume, is associated with functional outcome after reperfusion. Among large-core patients who achieved successful reperfusion, ADC-based tissue characterization may help predict functional outcome.

title: Homocysteine as a risk factor for thrombosis and when to ask for testing.
abstract: Homocysteine (Hcy) is a sulfur-containing amino acid that is produced from methionine through the removal of a methyl group. It can be recycled into methionine, an essential amino acid found in food, through two primary pathways: remethylation and transsulfuration. The remethylation process involves vitamins B6, B9, and B12, as well as 5-methyltetrahydrofolate, while transsulfuration converts Hcy into cysteine; this is facilitated by pyridoxal-5'-phosphate (vitamin B6) and the enzyme cystathionine β-synthase. Hcy has long been regarded as a risk factor for both venous and arterial thrombosis. However, clinical trials using folate have not demonstrated a significant effect in reducing the recurrence of venous thromboembolism or cardiovascular disease, except for a slight reduction in the incidence of ischemic stroke. We aimed to clarify the best course of action for managing hyperhomocysteinemia (HHcy) levels over 15 μmol/L. Moreover, we focused on severe HHcy, which may lead to a misdiagnosis of either homocystinuria or a remethylation defect. This condition is associated with a heightened risk of both venous and arterial thrombosis. In fact, a thrombotic episode can often be the first clinical manifestation of the disease, as well as a serious complication during its progression. Finally, we discuss the opportunity for including Hcy testing in thrombophilia screening. We conclude that this is not an appropriate approach to adopt, but Hcy testing should be requested for a young or adolescent patient with an unproven, unexplained thrombotic event.

title: Cardiovascular complications as a consequence of coronavirus infection in pregnant women managed in ambulatory settings.
abstract: BACKGROUND: SARS-CoV-2 has been linked to cardiovascular complications in the general population. However, data regarding cardiovascular outcomes among pregnant women remain limited, particularly in community-based ambulatory populations, as most previous studies focused primarily on hospitalized or critically ill patients. In this retrospective population-based matched cohort study, we evaluated whether COVID-19 infection during pregnancy is associated with an increased incidence of cardiovascular complications among pregnant women managed predominantly in outpatient settings. METHODS: p We conducted a retrospective population-based matched cohort study using electronic health record data from pregnant women between 2020 and 2025. Women with COVID-19 during pregnancy were matched 1:1 to women without documented COVID-19 during pregnancy according to demographic, obstetric, and clinical characteristics. The final analytical cohort included 4,068 women in each group. Cardiovascular outcomes during pregnancy and within a year since last menstrual period were assessed. Baseline demographic and obstetric characteristics were comparable between the COVID-19 and control groups. No significant differences were observed between the groups in the incidence of major cardiovascular complications, either when analyzed individually or as a composite endpoint (0.15% vs. 0.15%; OR 1.00, 95% CI 0.27-3.74). Specifically, there were no significant differences in the occurrence of atrial fibrillation/flutter, congestive heart failure, cardiomyopathy, myocarditis, pulmonary embolism, or deep venous thrombosis. In contrast, cough and backache were significantly more frequent among women with COVID-19 than among matched controls (6.88% vs. 4.87%; OR 1.45, 95% CI 1.19-1.75; 13.8% vs. 11.8%; OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.05-1.37; = 0.007 respectively). CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that among pregnant women in ambulatory community settings, COVID-19 infection is not associated with an increased risk of major cardiovascular complications.

However, data regarding cardiovascular outcomes among pregnant women remain limited, particularly in community-based ambulatory populations, as most previous studies focused primarily on hospitalized or critically ill patients. title: Anxiety in patients with lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis: a patient-centred sequential explanatory mixed-methods study of prevalence, associated factors, and patient experiences.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Lower extremity deep vein thrombosis (LEDVT) is associated with substantial psychological burden. Anxiety after DVT may reflect not only an emotional consequence of thrombosis, but also a signal of unmet informational, functional, and supportive care needs. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence and factors associated with anxiety among LEDVT patients and to explore their lived experiences, perceived triggers, and support needs using a mixed-methods design. METHODS: A sequential explanatory mixed-methods study was conducted. In the quantitative phase, 175 LEDVT patients completed the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7), Brief Illness Perception Questionnaire (B-IPQ), and Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support (MSPSS). Clinical and care-process variables were collected, including the perceived adequacy of structured counselling at diagnosis using an 8-item checklist. Clinically significant anxiety was defined as GAD-7 score ≥10. Multivariable logistic regression was performed according to a prespecified conceptual framework. In the qualitative phase, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 15 purposively selected participants; data were analyzed using thematic analysis. RESULTS: P P P P The prevalence of clinically significant anxiety was 41.1% (72/175; 95% CI: 33.9%-48.6%). Younger age (OR = 0.95, 95% CI: 0.92-0.98, = 0.002), higher B-IPQ score (OR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.11-1.26, < 0.001), lower MSPSS score (OR = 0.94, 95% CI: 0.90-0.98, = 0.005), and adequate counselling at diagnosis (OR = 0.42, 95% CI: 0.20-0.88, = 0.022) were independently associated with anxiety. Qualitative analysis generated five major themes: fear of complications, treatment-related anxiety, role and functional impairment, information delivery and illness meaning-making, and insufficient emotional and social support. CONCLUSION: Anxiety affects approximately two in five LEDVT patients in this single-centre cross-sectional cohort. Anxiety was associated not only with younger age, negative illness perception, and low social support, but also with symptom burden and perceived inadequacy of counselling at diagnosis; qualitative findings additionally highlighted symptom burden and functional limitations as key experiential drivers of anxiety. Integrated DVT care should address anticoagulation management, structured education, risk communication, cognitive reframing, functional recovery, and psychosocial support.

title: Risk factors of major bleeding associated with direct oral anticoagulant treatment in patients with venous thromboembolism: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are commonly prescribed for venous thromboembolism (VTE), but major bleeding (MB) remains an important complication of treatment. Despite their widespread use, systematic evaluations of prognostic factors associated with major bleeding during DOAC treatment remain scarce. To address this gap, we conducted a systematic review to identify prognostic factors associated with major bleeding during DOAC treatment in patients with VTE. This study seeks to enhance the safety and efficacy of anticoagulation therapy for VTE patients. METHOD AND RESULTS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted to search the PubMed and Web of Science databases for studies published before September 18, 2026. The review adhered to predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria to identify studies that investigated risk factors for major bleeding associated with DOAC treatment in patients diagnosed with VTE. Among the evaluated prognostic factors, quantitative pooling was possible only for age, which was reported in two studies; the remaining factors were summarized individually. Low-certainty evidence from a single study suggested a possible association between non-recommended dosing regimens and major bleeding. Evidence regarding declining adherence was also limited and of very low certainty. For age, very low-certainty evidence from the pooled analysis of two studies did not demonstrate a statistically significant association with major bleeding. CONCLUSION: The available evidence suggests possible associations between several prognostic factors and major bleeding in patients with VTE treated with DOACs; however, most findings are supported by low- or very low-certainty evidence and frequently by single studies. These findings should therefore be interpreted cautiously and require validation in larger, high-quality prospective studies.

To address this gap, we conducted a systematic review to identify prognostic factors associated with major bleeding during DOAC treatment in patients with VTE.

title: Case Report: Brucella-associated complications following thoracic endovascular aortic repair: a case series of three patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Brucellosis is a rare but potentially fatal cause of vascular graft infection. Evidence regarding Brucella-associated complications after thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) remains limited. Case presentation: We report three elderly male patients who developed severe aortic complications following TEVAR, including pseudoaneurysm formation and aorto-esophageal fistula. All patients had a history of epidemiological exposure to Brucella and were diagnosed with active infection through serological testing (Rose Bengal test, serum agglutination test, Brucella IgG and IgM antibodies). Endovascular re-intervention combined with targeted anti-brucellosis therapy was performed in all cases. RESULTS: One patient achieved sustained clinical remission after repeat endovascular repair and prolonged antimicrobial therapy. Two patients developed catastrophic infectious complications, including mediastinal abscess and aorto-esophageal fistula, resulting in death despite aggressive management. CONCLUSIONS: Brucella infection should be considered in patients presenting with unexplained symptoms after TEVAR, especially in endemic regions. Endovascular repair plays a critical role in acute stabilization; however, long-term outcomes remain highly dependent on effective infection control.

Evidence regarding Brucella-associated complications after thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) remains limited. title: Microsurgical Clipping of a Tumor-Like Bilobulated Ophthalmic Aneurysm: A 2-Dimensional Operative Video.
abstract: 1-3 4-6 2,4,7 8 Ophthalmic artery aneurysms are technically challenging lesions because of their complex paraclinoid anatomy and intimate relationship with the optic apparatus, internal carotid artery (ICA), and ophthalmic artery.Visual dysfunction is an important clinical presentation, particularly in large aneurysms causing optic nerve compression, and visual outcomes remain a major consideration when selecting among microsurgical and endovascular treatment strategies.Microsurgical clipping remains an important option in selected complex aneurysms because it provides definitive exclusion while allowing direct optic nerve decompression and parent vessel reconstruction.We present the operative video of a 59-year-old woman with progressive right-predominant visual deterioration over approximately 30 days. Imaging demonstrated a large, irregular, bilobulated ophthalmic artery aneurysm measuring 18 × 11 mm, with an 8-mm neck and postcontrast wall enhancement. Given the progressive visual deficit and optic nerve compression, microsurgical treatment was selected. Following proximal cervical ICA control and a pterional-transsylvian approach,the optic nerve was decompressed and the aneurysm exposed. Its broad neck and complex bilobulated morphology required tandem clip reconstruction of the ICA while preserving ophthalmic artery flow. Motor-evoked potentials and indocyanine green videoangiography guided clip adjustment. Atherosclerotic plaque at ophthalmic artery origin further influenced final clip positioning. Postoperative computed tomography angiography confirmed parent vessel patency, and visual field testing demonstrated improvement at 2 weeks. This video demonstrates optic nerve decompression, reconstructive clipping, and flow-preserving microsurgical strategies for a complex ophthalmic artery aneurysm.

title: Optimizing Vessel Preparation in Femoropopliteal Lesions: Does the Chocolate Balloon Deliver on Its Clinical Promise?
abstract: The "leave nothing behind" paradigm using drug-coated balloons (DCBs) has reshaped femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease treatment, though clinical success remains heavily contingent upon optimal vessel preparation. In a recent issue of The American Journal of Cardiology, Li and colleagues address the limitations of conventional plain old balloon angioplasty (POBA) through a propensity score-matched analysis of 508 patients from the multicenter PROMISING registry, comparing specialized vessel preparation using the nitinol-constrained Chocolate balloon against POBA before DCB angioplasty. The Chocolate balloon significantly reduced the primary endpoint of bailout stenting (20.47% vs 29.92%) and facilitated larger final DCB diameters, though these acute mechanical advantages did not translate into statistically significant differences in clinical outcomes at 12 months. This commentary examines this striking "procedural-to-clinical paradox," highlighting how the potent antiproliferative effect of DCBs and the acute compensatory function of bailout stents may temporarily mask early clinical divergence. Given that cumulative mechanical failures of permanent metallic implants typically emerge beyond one year in hostile biomechanical environments, longer-term observation remains essential to capture the true clinical dividend of a stent-free strategy.

title: The Moderating Effects of Race and Ethnicity on a Motivational Interviewing Intervention for Improving Physical Health Among Patients With Peripheral Artery Disease: Secondary Analysis of a Pilot Randomized Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In a pilot randomized trial, face-to-face or telephone motivational interviewing (MI) was more efficacious than a smartphone app after 3 months for increasing 6-minute walk distance (primary outcome) and reducing body weight (secondary outcome) in patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD). Little is known about intervention heterogeneity related to social determinants of health (SDOH). OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore whether SDOH are associated with the MI intervention effects on walking distance and weight loss and generate intervention heterogeneity hypotheses. METHODS: Community dwellers in Wichita, Kansas, were recruited through community outlets and screened for PAD. Consented participants were randomly assigned to MI (n=16) or an app (n=13). Survey instruments were used to measure SDOH, demographics, and adverse childhood experiences, which were assessed for their associations with 6-minute walk distance change and weight loss. Difference-in-differences (DiD) comparisons of median changes between SDOH strata were conducted using Wilcoxon and Kruskal-Wallis nonparametric tests. RESULTS: For 6-minute walk distance, pretest-posttest changes were significantly greater among participants of "other" race and ethnicity than among non-Hispanic White participants (DiD=44.0 m, 95% CI 19.2-164.2; P=.004), and no DiDs for other SDOH were significant. Significant median pretest-posttest increases in walking distance were observed in those with a college or higher educational attainment (48.8 m, 95% CI 28.0-61.4), unmarried individuals (40.4 m, 95% CI 0.5-56.0), those living with family (55.7 m, 95% CI 30.5-199.5), those who talked to and saw family or friends 3 or more times a week (46.4 m, 95% CI 17.2-69.4), and those without unmet daily needs (46.5 m, 95% CI 7.6-67.1). For weight loss, we did not observe significant DiDs with any SDOH. However, a significant median weight loss was observed in every SDOH stratum where we observed a significant increase in 6-minute walk distance. Significant weight loss was also observed in 5 additional SDOH strata: male individuals, household income below US $30,000, never served in military, employed status, and no stress. The improvements in weight loss and walking distance were highly consistent in both direction and size across SDOH strata. CONCLUSIONS: This pilot study was the first to explore potential SDOH-related intervention effect modification and heterogeneity. The significant association between walking distance and race and ethnicity suggested a potential effect modification. Significant pretest-posttest improvements in both outcomes were found in the same SDOH strata. The highly consistent evidence across both outcomes and all SDOH strata provided confidence in potential intervention efficacy and heterogeneity despite the small sample size. Our findings were consistent with established associations between SDOH and general functions in patients with PAD, suggesting likely mediation pathways through health literacy and social support. Future interventions should consider heterogeneity to target socially disadvantaged patients with PAD to bridge disparities and maximize benefits. title: Outcomes of hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation (HEPATIC): an international, multicentre, retrospective registry study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation is a severe complication that can lead to acute graft failure, often requiring urgent re-transplantation. We aimed to assess the 1-year incidence of graft loss and mortality and to evaluate outcomes according to the timing of hepatic artery thrombosis and the treatment approaches in patients with hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation. METHODS: In this international, multicentre, retrospective study, the HEPATIC registry, which had 33 centres across 21 countries as of December, 2025, was used to identify patients who developed hepatic artery thrombosis at age younger than 18 years after paediatric liver transplantation between Jan 1, 2002, and Dec 31, 2021, and who either received a diagnosis of or received an intervention for hepatic artery thrombosis before Jan 1, 2023. Donor-related, recipient-related, and transplantation-related characteristics collected from local medical records were entered retrospectively into electronic case reports by participating centres, with centralised data quality control. Primary outcomes were 1-year graft loss and mortality after hepatic artery thrombosis diagnosis. The outcomes were examined based on when hepatic artery thrombosis occurred after paediatric liver transplantation (early [≤7 days] vs late [>7 days]), primary management strategy (conservative management, surgical revascularisation, endovascular therapy, or immediate listing for re-transplantation), and transplantation era (in 5-year intervals). The registry was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05818644. FINDINGS: Hepatic artery thrombosis occurred in 415 patients, of whom 216 (52%) were female and 199 (48%) were male, and median age was 1·7 years (IQR 0·8-6·5). Median follow-up was 50·9 months (IQR 17·0-112·6). Graft loss occurred in 180 patients by 1 month (cumulative incidence 43% [95% CI 38-48]) and 222 by 1 year (54% [49-58]); 51 patients died by 1 month (12% [9-15]) and 77 by 1 year (19% [15-22]). Surgical revascularisation was the first-line treatment approach in 195 (47%) patients. Other strategies included listing for re-transplantation in 99 (24%), conservative management in 79 (19%), and endovascular therapy in 42 (10%). Treatment approaches changed over time, with increased use of conservative management and endovascular therapy and reduced listing for re-transplantation (p<0·0001), with no accompanying change in 1-year mortality across eras (p=0·14). Early (≤7 days) hepatic artery thrombosis occurred in 282 (68%) patients and was associated with higher 1-year graft loss than late (>7 days) hepatic artery thrombosis (cumulative incidence 57% [95% CI 51-63] vs 47% [37-55], log-rank p=0·010). Surgical revascularisation was used in 167 (59%) patients and listing for re-transplantation in 66 (23%) patients with early hepatic artery thrombosis, whereas conservative management was used in 51 (38%) patients and endovascular therapy in 21 (16%) patients with late hepatic artery thrombosis; however, 1-year mortality did not differ between treatment strategies among patients with early versus late hepatic artery thrombosis. INTERPRETATION: Hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation is associated with notably high 1-year graft loss and mortality, particularly if hepatic artery thrombosis occurs within 7 days after the procedure. The management strategies for hepatic artery thrombosis differ according to the post-transplantation timing of hepatic artery thrombosis occurrence. Despite changes in management over the past 20 years, outcomes have remained poor, underscoring the need to improve therapeutic strategies for this complication. FUNDING: None.

title: Long-term graft and patient survival of patients with portal vein stenosis after pediatric liver transplantation: Results from the multicenter multinational PORTAL registry.
abstract: Pediatric liver transplantation (pLT) has become a standard treatment, but it is still burdened by complications such as portal vein stenosis (PVS). PVS can result in compromised graft function and portal hypertension if left untreated. We aimed to assess long-term patient and graft survival after PVS diagnosis following pLT. Our study analyzed data from the Portal Vein Obstruction Revascularisation Therapy After Liver Transplantation (PORTAL) registry, which contains retrospective data from 21 centers across 18 countries, over a 20-year period. Graft and patient survival rates were determined after PVS diagnosis. This study included 239 patients (53% female; median age at pLT 1.1   y) diagnosed with PVS. The median age at diagnosis was 2.7 years. The overall 10-year graft survival was 90%, and the 10-year patient survival was 96%. One-year graft and patient survival were lowest in patients with PVS diagnosed ≤7 days after pLT (80% and 92%, respectively). Initial treatment strategies comprised mostly endovascular procedures (87%), followed by conservative (11%) and surgical treatment (3%). Patient outcomes did not differ between these treatment groups. Within the endovascular group, graft survival in patients treated with stent (n=26) was significantly lower compared with those with percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (n=181) (88% vs. 98%, respectively, p =0.01). Our findings indicate excellent graft and patient survival after PVS diagnosis and its treatment. Further research is needed to determine the safety and efficacy of optimal management strategies, especially in early-onset PVS.

PVS can result in compromised graft function and portal hypertension if left untreated. We aimed to assess long-term patient and graft survival after PVS diagnosis following pLT.
