title: "Not so Minor" - Digital Amputation as a Precursor to Major Amputation and Mortality in an Irish Tertiary Vascular Center.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Minor (toe) amputations are a common consequence of peripheral arterial disease and/or diabetes. They can herald further forefoot and major amputations and are a poor prognostic indicator for 5-year survival. This study aimed to identify prognostic indicators for progression from minor amputation to major amputation and all-cause mortality. METHODS: Index digital amputations performed by vascular surgeons in a tertiary referral hospital between 2017 and 2022 were identified from Hospital In-Patient Enquiry data. Electronic records for each limb were followed up to October 2025 for further ipsilateral minor and major amputations and mortality. RESULTS: A total of 224 limbs in 209 patients underwent at least 1 minor amputation. The cohort was predominantly male (86%) with a mean age of 66.3 years (±12.7). 70% had peripheral arterial disease and 80% had diabetes. In total, 34% (n = 73/215) required further ipsilateral amputation, 78.3% of which occurred within 12 months of index surgery. Minor and major reamputation rates were 25.6% and 11%, respectively. Predictors of further amputation at any level included ischemic heart disease (IHD) (odds ratio [OR] 2.796, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.54-5.06), diabetes (OR 2.31, 95% CI 1.04-5.136), and dialysis (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.021-4.915). Index hallux amputation, IHD, and revascularization at index admission were risk factors for further major ipsilateral amputation. All-cause mortality was 11.4%, 24.8%, and 48% at 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively. CONCLUSION: Consistent with international data, minor amputations are poor prognostic factor for limb loss and death. In this cohort, patients with IHD and dialysis were most at risk for further amputation.

title: The Clinical Profile of Rupture: A 19-Year Case-Control Study of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysms.
abstract: BACKGROUND: To identify factors associated with ruptured infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) presentation and quantify ruptures below current sex-specific elective repair thresholds. METHODS: This retrospective case-control study compared patients presenting with ruptured infrarenal AAA with a contemporaneous comparison group undergoing elective infrarenal AAA repair. Multivariable logistic regression assessed associations with ruptured presentation. The primary model included maximum aneurysm diameter, age, female sex, and calendar year; the extended model additionally included hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and dyslipidemia. Discrimination was evaluated using optimism-corrected area under the curve. RESULTS: Among 394 patients with infrarenal AAA, 194 presented with rupture and 200 underwent elective repair. The median diameter was 80.0 versus 53.0 mm (P < 0.001), and women comprised 10.9% versus 3.0% (P = 0.002), respectively. Diameter per 10-mm increase (odds ratio, 2.19; 95% confidence interval, 1.84-2.61) and female sex (odds ratio, 4.72; 95% confidence interval, 1.49-14.94) were independently associated with ruptured presentation. Optimism-corrected area under the curves were 0.836 for diameter alone, 0.832 for the primary model (diameter, age, female sex, and calendar year), and 0.840 for the extended model (primary model plus hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and dyslipidemia). Sixteen of 160 ruptures (10.0%) occurred below sex-specific thresholds. CONCLUSION: Diameter was the dominant factor associated with ruptured presentation, but female sex remained independently associated. These findings support diameter-based practice while highlighting the need for prospective, sex-aware, multiparametric risk assessment.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: To identify factors associated with ruptured infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) presentation and quantify ruptures below current sex-specific elective repair thresholds. METHODS: This retrospective case-control study compared patients presenting with ruptured infrarenal AAA with a contemporaneous comparison group undergoing elective infrarenal AAA repair. Multivariable logistic regression assessed associations with ruptured presentation.

title: Comparative Outcomes of Endovascular and Open Surgical Repair for Extracranial Carotid Artery Aneurysms: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Extracranial carotid artery aneurysms (ECAAs) are rare lesions managed by open surgical repair (OpR) or endovascular repair (ER). We compared the perioperative and long-term outcomes of both strategies. METHODS: A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA)-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis, registered in International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO), was performed. Comparative studies were pooled using random-effects models, and separate single-arm meta-analyses were conducted for OpR and ER. RESULTS: Twenty-six retrospective studies involving 707 patients and 725 procedures were included (574 OpR and 151 ER). Six comparative studies (228 procedures) showed no significant differences between ER and OpR in 30-day mortality (odds ratio [OR], 2.58; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.53-12.52), 30-day stroke (OR, 1.08; 95% CI, 0.30-3.91), late stroke, reintervention, or primary patency. In the single-arm analyses, pooled 30-day mortality and stroke rates after OpR were 1.18% and 4.29%, respectively. No 30-day deaths and one stroke were reported after ER, yielding a pooled stroke rate of 1.25% (95% CI, 0.18-8.34). Primary patency was high after both OpR (98.44%) and ER (94.50%). CONCLUSION: Observational evidence suggests similar perioperative outcomes and similar observed late event rates for ER and OpR in ECAAs, although heterogeneous follow up and the absence of time-to-event analyses limit formal comparison of long-term durability. Both approaches were associated with low mortality, stroke, reintervention rates, and excellent primary patency. Open repair remains supported by a larger body of evidence and longer follow up, whereas evidence for ER remains comparatively limited. Because treatment allocation in the available studies was influenced by patient characteristics, anatomical complexity, and surgical risk, the observed similarity in outcomes should not be interpreted as evidence of therapeutic equivalence. Given the observational design and the predominantly moderate-to-serious risk of bias of the included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution.

We compared the perioperative and long-term outcomes of both strategies. METHODS: A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA)-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis, registered in International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO), was performed.

title: Endovascular Iliac Stenting Versus Open Aortobifemoral Bypass for Aortoiliac Occlusive Disease: A Retrospective Multicentre Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aortoiliac occlusive disease (AIOD) causing chronic or critical limb-threatening ischemia can be treated by open aortobifemoral bypass (ABF) or endovascular reconstruction. Comparative effectiveness data adjusted for treatment selection bias remain limited. This multicenter study compared mid-term outcomes of endovascular versus open reconstruction for AIOD. METHODS: Retrospective, nonrandomized cohort study of 171 patients with AIOD (Rutherford 3-6) treated at three centers (UK, Ireland, and Egypt) between January 2023 and February 2026. Outcomes were primary patency, freedom from reintervention (FFR), amputation-free survival (AFS), overall survival, and perioperative complications. Cox regression and inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting (IPTW) were used to adjust for confounding. RESULTS: 125 patients (73.1%) underwent endovascular treatment and 46 (26.9%) open bypass. Endovascular patients were older (66.8 vs 60.8 years, P < 0.001) and had a lower burden of TransAtlantic Inter-Society Consensus II (TASC II) C-D disease (53.6% vs 93.5%, P < 0.001). Primary patency at 24 months was 62.7% versus 91.8% (log-rank P < 0.001; IPTW-adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 5.67, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.75-18.37). FFR at 24 months was 63.1% versus 93.3% (P < 0.001). AFS (85.0% vs 87.4%, P = 0.992) and overall survival (93.3% vs 90.0%, P = 0.335) were comparable between groups. Wound infection was less frequent after endovascular treatment (0.8% vs 10.9%, P = 0.006). Major amputation was independently predicted by critical limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) presentation (odds ratio [OR] 4.0) and age, not treatment group. Progressive infrainguinal disease, rather than failure of proximal revascularization, accounted for most amputations in both groups. CONCLUSION: Open bypass confers a substantial mid-term patency and reintervention-free survival advantage over endovascular reconstruction for AIOD, most pronounced in TASC D and CLTI subgroups, without a corresponding difference in limb salvage or survival. These findings support risk-stratified rather than uniformly endovascular-first treatment selection, pending confirmation from the ongoing Endovascular Versus Open revascularisation in severe oCClusive aorto-iliac disease (EVOCC) randomized trial.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Aortoiliac occlusive disease (AIOD) causing chronic or critical limb-threatening ischemia can be treated by open aortobifemoral bypass (ABF) or endovascular reconstruction. Comparative effectiveness data adjusted for treatment selection bias remain limited. This multicenter study compared mid-term outcomes of endovascular versus open reconstruction for AIOD.

title: Distinct Temporal Patterns of Limb Loss and Mortality after Transcatheter Arterialization of the Deep Veins for No-Option CLTI.
abstract: BACKGROUND: No-option chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) represents the most advanced stage of peripheral arterial disease, characterized by exhausted revascularization options and substantial systemic comorbidity. Contemporary registry data have reported amputation-free survival (AFS) as low as approximately 37% at 1 year with standard care alone. Deep venous arterialization has emerged as a limb-salvage strategy for these patients by arterializing the venous circulation to restore perfusion to the distal extremity. Although early trial data have been encouraging, the durability of transcatheter arterialization of the deep veins (TADV) in routine clinical practice beyond the trial setting remains incompletely defined. We evaluated 2-year technical and clinical outcomes following TADV in a single-center cohort. METHODS: We performed a retrospective, single-center cohort study of 29 consecutive patients with no-option CLTI who underwent TADV, with follow-up extending up to 2 years. Outcomes assessed included technical success, 30-day circuit patency, major amputation, limb salvage, all-cause mortality, and AFS. Kaplan-Meier methods were used to estimate time-to-event outcomes, and univariable Cox regression was used to identify baseline factors associated with AFS and mortality. RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in all 29 patients (100%). During the follow-up, limb salvage was maintained in 22 of 29 patients (75.9%). The Kaplan-Meier limb-salvage curve plateaued after approximately 7 months, with no major amputations observed among patients who remained amputation-free beyond this point. All-cause mortality was 41.4% (12 of 29 patients) and increased throughout follow-up (Table 2). Older age was significantly associated with mortality (median, 77 vs. 71 years; P = 0.047), and congestive heart failure showed a nonsignificant trend toward increased mortality risk (83.3% vs. 47.1%; P = 0.064). CONCLUSION: In this cohort of patients with no-option CLTI, TADV achieved durable limb preservation in approximately three-quarters of patients through 2 years of follow-up, with amputation occurring almost exclusively within the first several months after the procedure. All-cause mortality remained substantial throughout follow-up, consistent with the comorbidity burden of this population. These findings support TADV as a limb-salvage option for patients with no-option CLTI who would otherwise face major amputation, although larger multicenter studies are needed to confirm long-term durability.

Contemporary registry data have reported amputation-free survival (AFS) as low as approximately 37% at 1 year with standard care alone. Deep venous arterialization has emerged as a limb-salvage strategy for these patients by arterializing the venous circulation to restore perfusion to the distal extremity.

title: Severity-Dependent Patterns of Hemodynamic Change in Symptomatic Carotid Stenosis during the Waiting Period Before Endarterectomy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: To determine whether the rate of hemodynamic change after a symptomatic carotid event differs between moderate and severe stenosis. METHODS: Serial duplex examinations in symptomatic patients awaiting carotid endarterectomy were analyzed with a linear mixed-effects model, using an extended, prospectively maintained database. Maximum internal carotid artery peak systolic velocity (ICA PSV) was modeled as a linear function of time from the index event interacting with baseline severity (moderate 125-229, severe ≥230 cm/s), with a random intercept per patient. The rate of change (cm/s per day) and the moderate-severe difference were the principal outcomes. Categorical interval comparisons and paired within-patient changes, including distal common carotid artery (CCA) PSV, were secondary analyses. RESULTS: The time course of maximum ICA PSV differed by baseline severity (interaction P = 0.006). The modeled rate of change was +1.20 cm/s per day (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.28 to 2.12) in moderate and -0.21 cm/s per day (95% CI: -0.58 to 0.17) in severe stenosis (difference 1.41 cm/s per day, 95% CI: 0.42 to 2.40; P = 0.005). Secondary analyses were consistent: moderate stenosis accelerated with stable inflow, whereas severe stenosis showed no further ICA acceleration but a fall in distal CCA PSV (-3.0 cm/s; P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: The rate of hemodynamic change during the waiting period depends on baseline severity: moderate stenosis accelerates, whereas severe stenosis shows little further ICA acceleration, consistent with behavior near a velocity ceiling. Maximum ICA PSV and distal CCA PSV are best read as separate, time-sensitive variables rather than as a single ratio.

METHODS: Serial duplex examinations in symptomatic patients awaiting carotid endarterectomy were analyzed with a linear mixed-effects model, using an extended, prospectively maintained database. Maximum internal carotid artery peak systolic velocity (ICA PSV) was modeled as a linear function of time from the index event interacting with baseline severity (moderate 125-229, severe ≥230 cm/s), with a random intercept per patient.

title: Outcomes of Open Versus Endovascular Repair of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Involving the Iliac Bifurcation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aneurysmal involvement of the iliac bifurcation increases the complexity of both open and endovascular repair of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA), potentially raising the risk of postoperative complications. Randomized trials comparing endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) and open aortic repair (OAR) for AAA showed that EVAR is associated with a lower postoperative mortality rate. However, it remains unclear whether these results apply to AAA involving the iliac bifurcation (AAAIB). Several small single-institutional studies have shown conflicting results. This study aims to compare the outcomes of EVAR and OAR for AAAIB in a real-world, multi-institutional setting. METHODS: The Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database was queried for patients who underwent repair for AAAIB. The cohort was divided into 2 groups based on the intervention: EVAR versus OAR. Baseline demographic, clinical, and perioperative characteristics, as well as outcomes such as overall 30-day mortality, in-hospital mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: death, myocardial infarction, stroke), intestinal ischemia, overall reinterventions, and 1-year survival, were compared between the groups. Univariable analysis, multivariable inverse probability-weighted regression (IPWR), survival analysis with the Kaplan-Meier method, log-rank test, and Cox proportional hazards regression were performed. RESULTS: Of all reviewed patients, 7,535 were included in the final analysis, of whom 5,742 (76.2%) underwent EVAR, whereas 1,793 (23.8%) underwent OAR. In IPWR models, patients who underwent EVAR had significantly lower odds of overall in-hospital mortality (odds ratio [OR]: 0.25, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.18-0.34, P < 0.001), 30-day mortality (OR: 0.31, 95% CI: 0.23-0.42, P < 0.001), MACE (OR: 0.24, 95% CI: 0.19-0.31, P < 0.001), and other postoperative adverse events compared to OAR. The Cox proportional hazards model demonstrated a significantly higher 1-year survival rate for EVAR compared to OAR (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.61, 95% CI: 0.50-0.76, P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: In this real-world, multi-institutional study, EVAR for AAAIB was associated with lower odds of overall in-hospital mortality, 30-day mortality, MACE, as well as a higher 1-year survival rate, compared to the OAR. EVAR should be considered the primary method for repairing aortoiliac aneurysm involving the iliac bifurcation in anatomically suitable patients. Longer follow-up studies are needed to confirm these findings and compare the long-term reintervention and aorta-related mortality rates between the 2 treatment modalities.

Randomized trials comparing endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) and open aortic repair (OAR) for AAA showed that EVAR is associated with a lower postoperative mortality rate. However, it remains unclear whether these results apply to AAA involving the iliac bifurcation (AAAIB).

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of the BlueDop Vascular Expert for Detecting Peripheral Arterial Disease in People with Suspected Intermittent Claudication Referred to Secondary Care: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Manual ankle-brachial pressure index (ABI) assessment reqiuires significant time and expertise, precluding its use in primary care. Automated vascular assessment tools may offer a simple and efficient alternative for detecting peripheral arterial disease (PAD). However, further evidence is needed before they can be recommended. This study considers the diagnostic accuracy of the BlueDop vascular expert (BVE) in people with suspected intermittent claudication. METHODS: We performed a cross-sectional cohort study including people referred to our nurse-led intermittent claudication clinic. BVE measurements were compared to the manual resting ABI/toe brachial index (TBI) method, using traditional cutoff values of <0.9 and < 0.7, respectively. RESULTS: 217 participants and 430 limbs were included, with an overall PAD prevalence of 46%. Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictor values (PPVs) and negative predictor values (NPVs) for the BVE were 88.5%, 80.7%, 81.3% and 88.1% respectively, when compared to the manual ABI. When compared to the manual TBI, the sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV for the BVE were 45.5%, 88%, 62.5%, and 78.6% respectively, though this analysis included only 38 limbs. No BVE diagnoses were based on ABI alone, 71% were based on waveform alone and 29% were based on a combination of ABI and waveform. The BVE assessment was significantly quicker to perform than the manual method (P < 0.01). CONCLUSION: The BVE demonstrated favorable sensitivity and specificity for detecting or excluding PAD compared to the manual ABI. Further work is needed comparing this device to others, across a range of clinical populations and settings before it can be considered in routine clinical practice.

Automated vascular assessment tools may offer a simple and efficient alternative for detecting peripheral arterial disease (PAD). However, further evidence is needed before they can be recommended.

title: The axillary vein and its tributaries: anatomical variations, morphometry, and surgical implications.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Precise morphometric data of the axillary vein (AV) network are essential for surgical and endovascular safety. This study aims to characterize main-trunk morphometry, formation patterns (Types A/B), tributary variations, and the lateral venous channel (LVC), providing an anatomical framework potentially relevant to surgical navigation and vascular access. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Forty formalin-fixed upper extremities from adult whole-body donors were dissected. Two independent investigators measured external venous diameters at standardized landmarks and the AV to coracoid apex distance; terminal drainage patterns were recorded during dissection. The LVC was operationally defined as a distinct longitudinal venous channel coursing along the lateral axillary wall, separate from the main AV and from the principal course of its distal communicating vein, while forming an additional distal-to-proximal venous connection within the axillary venous system. RESULTS: Mean proximal AV diameter was 10.42 ± 2.06 mm; distance from the coracoid apex to the AV was 44.01 ± 13.08 mm. Male donors showed significantly larger proximal AV (p = 0.016) and subscapular vein (p = 0.033) diameters. Brachial vein termination comprised Type A (independent, 75.0%) and Type B (common trunk, 25.0%). An LVC was identified in 62.5% of specimens, most frequently showing distal communication with the lateral brachial vein and proximal termination in the AV. Cephalic vein absence was 10.0%. CONCLUSIONS: The axillary venous network displays marked variability. The LVC represents a recurrent lateral axillary venous configuration with variable distal communications; in the present series, all identified channels joined the AV proximally. These findings provide a detailed anatomical framework that may assist procedural planning and recognition of venous variations during axillary interventions.

This study aims to characterize main-trunk morphometry, formation patterns (Types A/B), tributary variations, and the lateral venous channel (LVC), providing an anatomical framework potentially relevant to surgical navigation and vascular access. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Forty formalin-fixed upper extremities from adult whole-body donors were dissected.

title: Imaging and Outcomes in the Treatment of Sacral Dural Arteriovenous Fistulas.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Spinal dural arteriovenous fistulas (DAVFs) in the sacral region are extremely rare, and their intradural retrograde draining system has not been investigated in detail. The aim of this study was to characterize the venous drainage patterns of sacral DAVFs based on our clinical experience in treating patients with this condition. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed the clinical data of patients with sacral DAVFs treated at our institution from January 2016 to January 2024. Preoperative spinal angiography was used to evaluate the positional relationship between the shunt point of sacral DAVF and the vertebral midline. We proposed that if the location of the shunt point was located on the midline, the draining vein would be the filum terminale vein (FTV); if the shunt point was located off the midline, the draining vein would be the radiculomedullary vein (RMV). RESULTS: A total of 17 patients with sacral DAVFs treated with direct surgery were included in this study. All patients presented with lower extremity weakness and numbness. Sphincter dysfunction was present in 15 patients (88.2%). The mean interval from the symptom onset to diagnosis was 14.1 months (range, 1-96 months). Preoperative magnetic resonance imaging detected T2 hyperintensity at the level of the conus medullaris and intradural flow voids in all patients. Spinal angiography confirmed the diagnosis of sacral DAVFs in all cases, and complete fistula occlusion was achieved with surgical ligation in all patients. Intraoperatively, 4 patients with the midline location of the shunt point were confirmed to have the FTV as the draining vein, whereas the other 13 patients with off-midline shunt point were confirmed to have the RMV as the draining vein. The intraoperative findings were completely consistent with the preoperative assessment of the draining veins based on the location of the shunt point. CONCLUSIONS: The draining veins of sacral DAVFs are not always the FTVs; in fact, most sacral DAVFs drain via the RMV. With our simple imaging-based method, the 2 different types of draining veins in sacral DAVFs can be preliminarily identified before surgery.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed the clinical data of patients with sacral DAVFs treated at our institution from January 2016 to January 2024.

title: Anatomic Level as a Modifier of Racial/Ethnic Disparities in Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia: Outcomes after First-Time Endovascular Revascularization.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Racial and ethnic disparities in chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) outcomes are well documented, but whether these disparities vary by anatomic level of endovascular intervention remains unclear. We evaluated racial and ethnic differences in limb outcomes following endovascular revascularization for CLTI stratified by intervention level. METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network, including adults undergoing first-time lower extremity endovascular revascularization for CLTI between 2015 and 2024. Patients were stratified by intervention level: iliac, femoropopliteal, tibioperoneal, or combined femoropopliteal and tibioperoneal (multilevel). Propensity score matching balanced demographics and comorbidities across racial/ethnic cohorts. The primary outcomes were rates of 1-year major amputation and amputation-free survival. Outcome comparisons were reported as risk ratios (RRs). RESULTS: Among 14,786 patients, there were 3,071 iliac, 5,178 femoropopliteal, 2,363 tibioperoneal, and 3,718 multilevel interventions. After matching, Black patients demonstrated increased major amputation risk following iliac intervention (RR: 1.80, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.13-2.88, P = 0.012) and femoropopliteal intervention (RR: 1.83, 95% CI 1.39-2.41, P < 0.001) compared with White patients. No significant differences in amputation were observed following tibioperoneal or multilevel interventions. Hispanic patients exhibited increased amputation risk only in the multilevel cohort (RR: 1.57, 95% CI: 1.02-2.40, P = 0.037). Despite differences in amputation, amputation-free survival remained similar across racial and ethnic groups. CONCLUSION: Racial and ethnic disparities in CLTI outcomes following endovascular revascularization varied by anatomic intervention level. Disparities were most pronounced after proximal interventions and attenuated in distal disease, suggesting anatomic disease pattern may modify inequities in limb outcomes after revascularization.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network, including adults undergoing first-time lower extremity endovascular revascularization for CLTI between 2015 and 2024.

title: Ultrasound-guided central venous access in the NICU: indications, insertion and management.
abstract: UNLABELLED: Ultrasound-guided cannulation of deep veins has advanced in little more than a decade from the operating room to the neonatal bedside and from a rescue maneuver to a planned procedure. Centrally inserted central catheters (CICCs) and femorally inserted central catheters (FICCs) are quite different from epicutaneo-cava catheters: they are 3-4 Fr power-injectable polyurethane catheters that are easy to tunnel, secured by subcutaneous anchorage, and suitable for blood transfusion, high-flow infusions, repeated blood sampling, and hemodynamic monitoring. This narrative review examines the indications, materials, insertion bundles for CICCs and FICCs in newborns, as well as their management, complications, and the training gap that now limits their diffusion more than any technical obstacle. In published studies, procedural success is 97-100%, immediate complications are absent or rare (when an insertion bundle is used), and the bloodstream infection rate is severalfold lower in infants below 1,500 g and below 1,000 g compared with the epicutaneo-cava catheter. Since the evidence comes mainly from a few high-volume centers with high procedural expertise, the priority for future research is to define strategies - structured programs, simulation, proctoring - to build and maintain the same level of competence in lower-volume units. CONCLUSION: Though the supporting evidence is observational, Ultrasound-guided CICCs (or FICCs, if in selected cases) appear to be the most appropriate central venous access for the critically ill newborn. WHAT IS KNOWN: • Ultrasound-guided CICCs and FICCs can be placed at the bedside in neonates, including extremely low birth weight infants, and outperform epicutaneo-cava catheters in safety, flow, dwell time, and range of use. • The adoption of insertion bundles reduces immediate and late complications of central venous catheterization in neonates and children. WHAT IS NEW: • Multicenter and comparative neonatal data show reproducible procedural success across centers and several-fold lower bloodstream infection rates in the smallest infants, compared with epicutaneo-cava catheters. • The limiting factor is no longer technical feasibility but structured training; tunneling remains the most frequently omitted step in the insertion bundle and the least easily replaced.

title: Canadian Cardiovascular Society/Canadian Society of Cardiovascular Surgery/Canadian Association of Interventional Cardiology Clinical Practice Update on Transcatheter Mitral and Tricuspid Valve Intervention: Patient Evaluation and Management.
abstract: The management of mitral valve (MV) and tricuspid valve (TV) regurgitation has undergone significant transformation during the past decade. This change has been driven by a growing understanding of the adverse clinical consequences of these conditions, particularly their strong association with heart failure progression, reduced quality of life, and increased mortality-and by the emergence of effective transcatheter options for valve intervention. Among these, transcatheter MV edge-to-edge repair and replacement and transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair and replacement have become important therapeutic tools that provide a less invasive alternative to surgery in appropriately selected patients. In this clinical practice update we aim to provide contemporary, evidence-based guidance for clinicians in the evaluation and management of patients with severe, symptomatic MV or TV regurgitation who might benefit from transcatheter intervention. Key topics include the clinical presentation of these valve lesions, the diagnostic evaluation with emphasis on multimodality imaging and hemodynamics, criteria for patient selection, and current data on procedural and long-term clinical outcomes. A central theme is the role of timely referral and structured assessment to avoid missed opportunities for intervention. Optimal outcomes require active engagement from referring physicians and close collaboration within a multidisciplinary heart team, including cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, imaging specialists, heart failure specialists, and nursing partners-to ensure careful patient selection, procedural planning, and comprehensive post-intervention follow-up. By integrating clinical judgement with guideline-based recommendations and procedural expertise, transcatheter edge-to-edge repair or transcatheter valve replacement can offer substantial symptomatic relief and improved quality of life for selected patients, while minimizing procedural risk and enhancing overall cardiovascular outcomes.

title: One-Year Outcomes of Endovascular Repair of Zone 0/1 Aortic Arch Lesions With a Thoracic Branched Endoprosthesis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The GORE TAG thoracic branch endoprosthesis pivotal nonrandomized, multicenter, prospective trial evaluated 1-year outcomes in patients at high risk for open-surgical repair undergoing aortic arch and descending thoracic aorta endovascular repair (zone 0/1). METHODS: End points evaluated from endovascular procedure through 12 months included aortic-related death, disabling stroke, permanent paraplegia or paraparesis, new onset renal failure, and unanticipated reintervention. Core lab identified end points included aortic rupture or enlargement (≥5 mm), type I/III endoleak, device integrity, device migration, fistula, patency, and new dissection. RESULTS: The 77 patients enrolled had aneurysm (n = 50), dissection (n = 24), or other isolated lesion types (n = 3); 90.9% had a zone 0 proximal stent landing zone. Patients had a mean age of 70.8±10.8 years, 66.2% were men, and 57.1% were White. All had the aortic and side branch component implanted. Technical success was 94.8%. Early outcomes to 12 months included 8 aortic-related deaths (10.4%), 6 disabling strokes (7.8%, all in the aneurysm cohort), 4 unanticipated reintervention (5.2%), 2 aortic ruptures (2.6%), and 1 renal failure (1.3%). Type IA/IB or type III endoleaks occurred in 6 patients (7.8%). Loss of side branch patency occurred in 1 patient (1.3%). There was no permanent paraplegia or paraparesis or loss of device integrity or migration. A total of 5 patients had aortic enlargement; none required reintervention. CONCLUSIONS: Early data from this prospective investigation of the thoracic branch endoprosthesis device in zone 0/1 applications signal that the device is a reasonable therapeutic alternative in patients with appropriate anatomy deemed high risk for open arch surgery.

title: Venous Thromboembolism after Laparotomic and Laparoscopic Myomectomy with Large Myoma Burden.
abstract: STUDY OBJECTIVE: To investigate the incidence of venous thromboembolism (VTE) in patients undergoing myomectomy. To evaluate the impact of route of surgery, myoma burden, and operative time in the development of VTE in this population. DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study (Canadian Task Force Classification II2) of targeted myomectomy data from the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program. SETTING: National Surgical Quality Improvement Program Database. PATIENTS OR PARTICIPANTS: Women aged ≥18 years undergoing laparotomic and laparoscopic myomectomy between 2011 and 2022. Patients were classified by current procedural terminology codes as having low or high myoma burden (>250 g or >4 fibroids). Patients undergoing hysterectomy, vaginal or hysteroscopic myomectomy, with malignant pathology, or missing operative time were excluded. INTERVENTIONS: Cases were identified by current procedural terminology codes. Variables including age, ethnicity, body mass index, smoking status, diabetes, hypertension, blood transfusion, inpatient status, and American Society of Anesthesiologists classification system scores were collected. Clinical predictors of VTE were evaluated by stratifying cases according to surgical route, operative time, year of procedure, and myoma burden. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: A total of 38 167 myomectomies occurring between 2011 and 2022 were included. Of these, 20 943 (54.9%) patients underwent laparotomy, and 17 224 (45.1%) patients underwent laparoscopy. The incidence of VTE after myomectomy was 0.28%. Patients undergoing laparotomy had twice the VTE rate (0.36%) compared with those undergoing laparoscopy (0.18%). Patients undergoing laparotomy were more likely to be younger, of non-Hispanic African American ethnicity, inpatient, with higher body mass index, require blood transfusion, have higher myoma burden, and have shorter operative times. After multivariable adjustment, neither myoma burden nor surgical route was independently associated with VTE. However, longer operative time (>186 minutes, 75 percentile) was independently associated with increased odds of VTE (adjusted odds ratio 2.73; confidence interval: 1.52-4.90). CONCLUSION: The occurrence of VTE after laparoscopic and laparotomic myomectomy is uncommon. The rate of VTE is higher with longer operative times, but this outcome is not significantly associated with surgical route or myoma burden.

To evaluate the impact of route of surgery, myoma burden, and operative time in the development of VTE in this population. DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study (Canadian Task Force Classification II2) of targeted myomectomy data from the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program.

title: Spectral coupling of arteriovenous fistula sound and flow-induced wall vibrations.
abstract: A native arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred vascular access for connecting a patient's circulation to a haemodialysis machine, but it can fail due to adverse vascular remodelling. AVFs produce characteristic sounds, likely generated by flow-induced high-frequency vessel wall vibrations. The aim of this study was to provide evidence of the relationship between AVF sounds and computed flow-induced wall vibrations, through a multi-domain characterisation of AVFs that integrated acoustic analyses and fluid structure interaction (FSI) simulations. Spectrograms of recorded AVF sounds from four patients showed frequency content comparable to FSI-derived vascular wall vibrations. This spectral coupling suggests that sound analysis could serve as a simple, non-invasive tool for early detection of AVF dysfunction.

title: Multicenter outcomes of peripheral vascular interventions in patients with active cancer.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Cancer is typically associated with venous thrombosis, but its impact on patients undergoing peripheral vascular interventions (PVIs) for concomitant peripheral arterial disease remains unclear. This multicenter study examines the characteristics of patients with active cancer and their outcomes after PVI. METHODS: Institutional Vascular Quality Initiative PVI data from three tertiary care centers (2019-2023) were combined and expanded through a retrospective chart review to include the presence and types of cancer. All adult patients undergoing endovascular intervention for peripheral arterial disease, including those with claudication, chronic limb-threatening ischemia, and acute limb ischemia, were included. The primary outcome was the composite of major amputation or mortality at 4 years in patients with cancer compared to those without. Additional long-term outcomes included reintervention, mortality, and major amputation at both 1 and 4 years. Secondary outcomes included perioperative outcomes. RESULTS: A total of 3072 patients were included. The incidence of active cancer was 2.2% (N = 68). Lung cancer was the most common, affecting 30.9% (N = 21) of patients. 53% (N = 36) presented with advanced stages (3/4) irrespective of cancer type. Patients with cancer were less likely to have diabetes. There was no significant difference in indication, but patients with cancer were more likely to get treated for aortoiliac disease and undergo stenting. Patients with cancer had a higher incidence of distal embolization (4.4% vs 0.6%; P = .012) and perioperative major amputation (4.4% vs 1.3%; P = .046). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed significantly higher mortality or amputation in patients with cancer up to 4 years (63% vs 35.1%; P < .001). Late outcomes in patients with cancer were driven by significantly higher mortality (52.2% vs 28.3%; P < .001) rather than adverse limb events (amputation: 14.7% vs 11.4%, P = .50; reintervention: 47.8% vs 48.3%, P = .80). Regression analysis demonstrated independent association of cancer with the composite outcome of mortality or major amputation (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.24; 95% confidence interval, 1.61-3.10). CONCLUSIONS: Active cancer affects a small proportion of patients undergoing PVI but has a significant impact on perioperative limb outcomes and long-term survival. This multicenter collaboration, combining registry data and electronic medical record review, can shed light on less common risk factors affecting lower-extremity revascularization.

title: Outcomes among patients with single-vessel tibial runoff undergoing revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia, and the role of peroneal communicating branch quality.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Data evaluating outcomes among patients with single-vessel tibial runoff are limited. Our aim was to compare outcomes across patients with sole anterior tibial (AT), peroneal, or posterior tibial (PT) runoff following revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), and to evaluate whether the quality of peroneal communicating branches (PCBs) affects outcome risk within the peroneal runoff population. METHODS: All patients undergoing first-time revascularization for CLTI were retrospectively reviewed (2005-2022) and stratified by sole runoff vessel (AT, peroneal, and PT). Primary outcomes were wound healing, major amputation, major adverse limb events (MALE), and amputation/death, assessed by Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression. A subset analysis stratified single-vessel peroneal runoff patients into a three-tiered, PCB grade: Both branches present with at least one robust (PCB grade 1), a single robust branch (PCB grade 2), or no robust branch (PCB grade 3), and compared each with the single-vessel AT/PT reference group. RESULTS: Overall, 732 patients had single-vessel below-knee runoff: 225 AT, 315 peroneal, and 192 PT. Groups differed significantly in age, sex, and diabetes prevalence. Unadjusted 2-year major amputation rates were significantly higher in the peroneal group [19% vs 9.4% (AT) vs 8.7% (PT); P < .001], as were MALE rates (30% vs 14% vs 26%; P = .01). After adjustment, peroneal runoff was independently associated with higher risk of major amputation [hazard ratio (HR), 1.81; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.04-3.13] and MALE (HR, 1.52; 95% CI, 1.03-2.25) compared with AT/PT runoff. These associations persisted in the endovascular cohort (major amputation: HR, 2.09; 95% CI, 1.06-4.13; MALE: HR, 1.59; 95% CI, 1.08-2.35) but did not reach significance in the bypass cohort, which was limited by low-event rates. When patients with single-vessel peroneal runoff were stratified by PCB grades, unadjusted 1-year major amputation rates followed a clear anatomically-driven pattern [6.9% (AT/PT) vs 5.4% (PCB grade 1) vs 15% (PCB grade 2) vs 32% (PCB grade 3); P < .001]. After adjustment, when compared with AT/PT runoff, patients without any robust branch (PCB grade 3) had significantly higher risk of major amputation (HR, 3.21; 95% CI, 1.76-4.84) and MALE (HR, 2.41; 95% CI, 1.53-3.79), whereas those with two communicating branches with at least one being robust (PCB grade 1) demonstrated higher rates of complete wound healing (HR, 1.69; 95% CI, 1.09-2.62) and no difference in major amputation or MALE. CONCLUSIONS: Peroneal runoff is independently associated with worse limb outcomes following revascularization for CLTI, but this risk may be primarily driven by patients with absent or diminutive communicating branches. Patients with robust branching demonstrate outcomes comparable with AT/PT runoff, underscoring the importance of further evaluation and preoperative assessment of PCB quality - using the proposed PCB grading system - in revascularization planning.

METHODS: All patients undergoing first-time revascularization for CLTI were retrospectively reviewed (2005-2022) and stratified by sole runoff vessel (AT, peroneal, and PT).

title: Endoscopic Endonasal Ligation of the Internal Carotid Artery: A Cadaveric Study and Case Series.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Internal carotid artery (ICA) sacrifice is occasionally required in complex skull-base pathology. Endovascular techniques remain the primary strategy, but intravascular metallic devices may complicate subsequent surgery and imaging surveillance in selected patients. We evaluated the anatomical feasibility and clinical application of endoscopic endonasal ICA ligation. METHODS: Three fresh cadaveric heads (6 sides) were dissected to identify accessible distal ligation sites and define the requirements for circumferential ICA dissection and direct ligation. The technique was subsequently applied in 5 selected patients, whose records were retrospectively reviewed. RESULTS: Circumferential ICA exposure and mobilization were achieved on all 6 sides. The lower paraclival ICA, caudal to its entry into the cavernous sinus, provided reproducible working space for ligature passage. A fibrous band extending from the middle cranial fossa dura toward the foramen lacerum was consistently identified and provisionally termed the meningolingual band; its division facilitated circumferential ICA mobilization. Endoscopic endonasal ICA ligation was completed in all 5 patients without stroke, embolic complication, or major neurological deficit; one patient developed ipsilateral postoperative miosis. CONCLUSIONS: Endoscopic endonasal ICA ligation may provide direct vascular control in highly selected patients who already require an endonasal approach and direct management of the diseased ICA. The paraclival ICA below the cavernous sinus is a practical distal ligation target when safe circumferential dissection and secure ligation are possible. This technique should be considered complementary to contemporary endovascular strategies.

title: Associations of Glycemic Control, Age, and Sex with Diabetic Foot Risk and Active Foot Ulceration among Patients with Diabetes in Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Diabetic foot disease is one of the most severe complications of diabetes mellitus, contributing substantially to hospitalization, lower limb amputation, and premature mortality. This study evaluated the associations of glycemic control (glycated hemoglobin [HbA1c]), age, and sex with diabetic foot risk and ulceration among patients attending a tertiary diabetes center in Qassim, Saudi Arabia. METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study included a census sample of 710 eligible electronic medical records of patients with a confirmed diagnosis of diabetes mellitus and a documented diabetic foot assessment between January 2022 and December 2024. No a priori sample size calculation was performed. The primary outcome was at-risk diabetic foot status (International Working Group on the Diabetic Foot category ≥ 1), and the secondary outcome was active foot ulceration. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with each outcome. RESULTS: The mean age was 57.6 ± 14.0 years; 337 patients (47.5%) were male and 373 (52.5%) were female, and 93.2% had type 2 diabetes mellitus. At-risk diabetic foot status was present in 53.2% of patients, and active foot ulceration was present in 3.0%. Ulcer prevalence increased across HbA1c categories (1.9%, 2.6%, and 6.3%), and at-risk status increased with age (39.6-62.1%). Older age (odds ratio [OR] = 1.028; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.016-1.039; P < 0.001) and male sex (OR = 1.403; 95% CI 1.036-1.901; P = 0.029) were independently associated with the at-risk status. HbA1c was not independently associated with at-risk status (P = 0.422) or ulceration (P = 0.077). CONCLUSIONS: Ulcer prevalence increased with poorer glycemic control; however, the adjusted HbA1c-ulceration association was not significant in the primary model. Key confounders were unavailable in the dataset, including diabetes duration, neuropathy and peripheral arterial disease severity, and renal function. Therefore, residual confounding cannot be excluded, and HbA1c's role in diabetic foot risk should not be discounted. These findings suggest that diabetic foot screening and preventive care should be tailored to specific age and sex groups, involving multiple healthcare disciplines.

title: Hypoxia and right ventricular dysfunction in patients with acute pulmonary embolism.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In patients with acute pulmonary embolism (PE), hypoxia may increase pulmonary vascular resistance and worsen right ventricular dysfunction (RVD), which is a key prognostic factor. However, associations between hypoxia, RVD and clinical outcomes have not been well described. AIM: To describe associations between hypoxia, RVD and clinical outcomes in patients with PE. METHODS: We performed a retrospective, single-center cohort study of patients treated by the Massachusetts General Hospital Pulmonary Embolism Response Team (PERT) from 10/2012 to 08/2021. Inclusion criteria included confirmed PE, recorded oxygen saturation prior to PERT activation, and echocardiogram within three days of PERT activation. Patients were categorized into four subgroups based on (1) hypoxia status (SaO₂ below vs. above 95%) and, (2) oxygen support (below vs. above 3 L/min). Our primary outcome was the presence of RVD on echocardiogram. Our secondary outcome was clinical deterioration within 7 days. RESULTS: We included 894 PE patients. The mean age was 61 (± 16 SD), 614/894 (69%) were hypoxic, and 624/894 (70%) had RVD on echocardiogram. Overall, hypoxic patients were more likely to have RVD than non-hypoxic patients (467/614 [76%] vs. 157/280 [56%], p < 0.0001). On subgroup analysis, RVD prevalence was highest in the "hypoxic with oxygen support ≥3L" group (n = 216/266, 81%) followed by the "not hypoxic with oxygen support ≥3L" group 53/70 (76%); 198/278 (71%) in the "hypoxic with oxygen support <3L" and 157/280 (56%) in the "not hypoxic with oxygen support <3L" groups. Clinical deterioration occurred in 199/894 (22%) patients and was more common in hypoxic patients than non-hypoxic patients (157/614 [26%] vs. 42/280 [15%], p < 0.0001), and most common in the "hypoxic with oxygen support ≥3L" subgroup 88/266 (33%). CONCLUSIONS: Hypoxia is associated with RVD and clinical deterioration in patients with PE. More research is needed to understand the risk associated with hypoxia and the physiology of supplemental oxygen support in PE. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

title: A steerable microcatheter-stabilizer strategy for stent-assisted coiling of a wide-neck middle cerebral artery aneurysm with an acutely angulated incorporated branch.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Wide-neck middle cerebral artery (MCA) aneurysms incorporating acutely angulated branches remain among the most technically challenging lesions in neuroendovascular therapy. Selective branch catheterization and subsequent catheter exchange may be difficult using conventional techniques. METHODS: A 79-year-old man with an enlarging unruptured right MCA aneurysm underwent stent-assisted coil embolization. A 2.0-Fr SwiftNINJA (LEONIS Mova Selective, Merit Medical/SB-Kawasumi Laboratories, Kanagawa, Japan) steerable microcatheter was used to achieve distal access to the incorporated branch through active tip deflection and angle locking. After distal access had been secured, a Stabilizer device (The Medilizer Anchor Guiding Device; Bolt Medical, Carlsbad, CA, USA) was deployed to facilitate catheter exchange to a stent-delivery microcatheter. RESULTS: The incorporated branch was successfully catheterized despite severe angulation. Distal anchoring with the Stabilizer device enabled safe catheter exchange, followed by successful deployment of a Neuroform Atlas stent (Stryker Neurovascular, Kalamazoo, MI, USA) and subsequent coil embolization. Complete aneurysm occlusion was achieved while preserving the incorporated branch, and no procedural complications occurred. CONCLUSION: This technical note describes a stepwise steerable microcatheter-stabilizer strategy that addresses two major procedural challenges - branch access and catheter exchange. The technique may represent a useful option for selected aneurysms requiring branch preservation and complex endovascular navigation.

Selective branch catheterization and subsequent catheter exchange may be difficult using conventional techniques. title: Post-thrombotic syndrome after thrombotic venous thoracic outlet syndrome.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Thrombotic venous thoracic outlet syndrome (T-vTOS), including Paget-Schrotter syndrome, is a rare form of upper extremity deep vein thrombosis that mainly affects young, active individuals. Its optimal management remains debated, and the medium-term outcomes have been poorly documented. METHODS: This retrospective study included consecutive patients diagnosed with T-vTOS at the vascular medicine department of a university hospital between 2014 and 2024. Patients were stratified according to the presence of post-thrombotic syndrome (PTS) using the modified Villalta score at the last follow-up (<5 vs ≥5). Clinical characteristics, therapeutic strategies, and outcomes were systematically assessed through a standardized evaluation performed by the same physician. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses, using Firth's penalized-likelihood method to account for the limited number of events, were performed to identify the factors associated with PTS. RESULTS: A total of 50 patients were included: 28 with a Villalta score of <5 and 22 with a Villalta score of ≥5 at the last follow-up. Patients with a Villalta score of <5 achieved higher rates of complete subclavian vein recanalization at follow-up (63% vs 32%; P = .045) and were less likely to have persistent subclavian vein occlusion (26% vs 59%; P = .023). Patients with a Villalta score of ≥5 more often required prolonged anticoagulation (73% vs 29%; P = .004) and more frequently underwent acute-phase endovascular treatment (36% vs 4%; P = .007). In the multivariable analysis, endovascular treatment alone without thoracic outlet surgery was associated with an increased risk of PTS (odds ratio, 10.6; 95% confidence interval, 1.15, 98.09) (P = .037), whereas no association was found between the risk of PTS and patients who had undergone both endovascular treatment and TOS surgery (odds ratio 1.3; 95% confidence interval, 0.26, 6.87) (P = .736). CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights the central role of venous patency in the clinical course of T-vTOS, with persistent subclavian vein occlusion associated with an increased risk of PTS. The association observed between acute-phase endovascular treatment alone and the risk of PTS does not support a clear benefit of this strategy. However, endovascular therapy in conjunction with surgical decompression of the thoracic outlet may reduce the risk of PTS.

Its optimal management remains debated, and the medium-term outcomes have been poorly documented. METHODS: This retrospective study included consecutive patients diagnosed with T-vTOS at the vascular medicine department of a university hospital between 2014 and 2024.

title: A comparison of aspiration thrombectomy with catheter-directed thrombolysis in the management of Paget-Schroetter syndrome.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Acute subclavian vein thrombosis secondary to thoracic outlet syndrome (Paget-Schroetter syndrome [PSS]) requires the prompt clearing of thrombus from the subclavian vein through catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) or aspiration thrombectomy (ASP). Our goal is to systematically compare the outcomes of CDT and ASP in the management of PSS. METHODS: Consecutive patients with PSS at a single institution from 2020 through 2025 were reviewed for management with CDT or ASP. Venograms were assessed for patency, stenosis, and subclavian post-thrombotic changes (PTC). PTC were graded based on the degree of luminal encroachment and vessel irregularity: mild (<10%), moderate (10%-50%), and severe (50%-99%). Interventions were assessed: (1) within 1 week of the procedure, (2) before subclavian vein decompression, (3) 2 weeks after subclavian vein decompression, and (4) patency on the last venogram. Standardized outcomes were assessed. RESULTS: A total of 110 patients with PSS were treated over 5 years. Of these patients, 54 met the inclusion criteria: 28 underwent CDT and 26 underwent ASP. At 1 week following the procedure, rethrombosis occurred in 1 (3.6%) patient who underwent CDT and 6 (23.1%) patients who underwent ASP (P < .5). Failure to clear thrombosis occurred in 13.8% of patients who underwent ASP. The composite rate of early thrombosis and procedural failure was higher in the ASP cohort. Before PSS surgery, occlusion was noted in 1 (3.6%) patient who underwent CDT and 8 (30.8%) patients who underwent ASP (P < .05). PTC was mild in 13 (46.4%) patients receiving CDT and 5 (19.2%) receiving ASP (P < .05); moderate in 5 (17.9%) receiving CDT and 5 (19.2%) receiving ASP; and severe in 9 (32.1%) receiving CDT and 8 (30.8) receiving ASP. At early follow-up after PSS surgery, PTC was mild in 10 (43.5%) patients receiving CDT and 4 (23.5) receiving ASP; moderate in 2 (8.7%) receiving CDT and 1 (5.9%) receiving ASP; and severe in 9 (39.1%) receiving CDT and 6 (35.3%) receiving ASP. Occlusion was noted in 2 (8.7%) patients receiving CDT and 6 (35%) receiving ASP. Recanalization resulted in final patency in 22 (95%) patients receiving CDT and 15 (88%) receiving ASP. CONCLUSIONS: Both ASP and CDT may be employed for clearing thrombus in PSS; however, they differ in early efficacy, PTC, and patency. Our results suggest that while often more rapid and convenient, ASP may be inferior to CAT in the management of PSS.

Our goal is to systematically compare the outcomes of CDT and ASP in the management of PSS. METHODS: Consecutive patients with PSS at a single institution from 2020 through 2025 were reviewed for management with CDT or ASP.

title: Sex-specific association between preoperative foot infection and vein graft stenosis after distal bypass for chronic limb-threatening ischemia.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Sex differences in lower-extremity bypass outcomes remain controversial, and the mechanism is unclear. We examined whether female sex is associated with vein graft stenosis (VGS), predominantly due to intimal hyperplasia, after distal bypass for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), and whether preoperative foot infection contributes. METHODS: We studied 318 limbs with CLTI undergoing para- or inframalleolar autogenous vein bypass at a single center (2000-2014; 74 women, 23%). All analyses were restricted to single-vein grafts; after excluding grafts occluding within 30 days, 232 formed the analytic cohort (182 men, 50 women). Female vs male outcomes were compared by 1:1 optimal matching (Mahalanobis distance within a propensity-score caliper on six covariates) and by inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting, which was the primary inference; death was treated as a competing risk. Stenosis was diagnosed by duplex surveillance, with histologic examination of excised segments. Wound, ischemia, and foot infection grades and preoperative C-reactive protein and fibrinogen were analyzed by sex with sex-by-exposure interaction terms; wound cultures were reviewed. RESULTS: After matching (48 pairs), the 5-year cumulative incidence of VGS remained higher in women (44% vs 9%; log-rank P = .004), and primary patency was lower (52% vs 88%; P = .003); secondary patency (85% vs 98%; P = .06) and limb salvage (P = .60) did not differ significantly. Weighting confirmed the excess [adjusted hazard ratio (HR), 2.13; 95% confidence interval, 1.13-4.02; P = .019]. Five-year mortality was 55% in men vs 35% in women; with death as a competing risk, stenosis incidence remained higher in women (34% vs 16%). Preoperative high-grade foot infection was associated with stenosis in women (HR, 4.27; 95% confidence interval, 1.56-11.70; P = .005) but not men (HR, 0.87; P = .74), with a significant sex-by-infection interaction (P = .026); wound and ischemia grades showed no sex difference. C-reactive protein and fibrinogen showed the same direction without a significant interaction. All 25 excised stenotic segments showed intimal hyperplasia without active inflammation, and organism type was unrelated to stenosis. In women, foot infection, poor vein quality, and run-off resistance were independent correlates. CONCLUSIONS: Women undergoing single-vein distal bypass for CLTI have a higher incidence of VGS despite balanced baseline risk, with the excess concentrated in those with preoperative foot infection. The findings suggest a sex-specific vein-wall response to infection-related inflammation and support intensified, infection-aware graft surveillance in women.

METHODS: We studied 318 limbs with CLTI undergoing para- or inframalleolar autogenous vein bypass at a single center (2000-2014; 74 women, 23%).

title: Faculty narrative feedback in the vascular surgery entrustable professional activity pilot is disproportionately focused on patient care and medical knowledge competencies.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Performance feedback is critical to guide vascular surgery trainees' skill development across competency domains. Workplace-based assessment of entrustable professional activity (EPA) allows faculty frequent opportunities to provide and document clinical performance feedback. Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) Milestones were previously mapped to each EPA and accompanying behavioral anchors reflect the range of competencies required to execute each clinical activity. It is unclear how faculty use this information to guide and focus the content of their feedback. We sought to identify the core competencies reflected in narrative feedback in a multi-institutional study of EPA assessments. METHODS: EPA assessments were collected during a 3-month national Vascular Surgery EPA Pilot in 2024. Trainees were rated on their performance of EPAs on a 4-point Likert scale and faculty had the opportunity to provide feedback. Narrative feedback was qualitatively analyzed using focused coding guided by the Vascular Surgery Milestones 2.0 framework. Feedback was coded using the six ACGME core competencies-patient care (PC), medical knowledge (MK), professionalism, interpersonal and communication skills, practice-based learning and improvement, and systems-based practice (SBP)-to characterize the domains emphasized in feedback. Quality assessment scores were assigned to all narrative feedback using the Quality of Assessment of Learning framework. Descriptive analysis was completed using R (R Foundation for Statistical Computing). RESULTS: Faculty completed 983 EPA assessments of 78 trainees across 17 institutions (n = 16 integrated residencies, n = 12 fellowships). Narrative feedback was included in 760 (77%) assessments. Feedback most frequently addressed PC (n = 662, 82%), followed by MK (n = 418, 55%), whereas feedback about practice-based learning and improvement (n = 42, 6%), interpersonal and communication skills (n = 42,6%), professionalism (n = 20, 3%), and SBP (n = 26, 3%) were less common. Most assessments were completed for postgraduate year-3 (29%) and postgraduate year-4 trainees (22%). Most assessments occurred during the intraoperative phase of care (88%), with relatively few occurring in preoperative (7%) or postoperative (5%) phases. In addition, feedback-referencing PC was associated with higher odds of high-quality feedback in comparison with feedback about the other competencies (odds ratio, 25.56; 95% confidence interval, 6.13-106.55). CONCLUSIONS: In this multi-institutional study of vascular surgery EPA assessments, faculty most frequently provided trainees with feedback on their performance of PC and MK competencies. Feedback on performance related to SBP was infrequently provided and, when provided, was of generally low quality. This has important implications for the use of EPAs to inform ACGME Milestones ratings and suggests alternative assessment tools will continue to be needed to capture performance across all competency domains required of a physician.

Workplace-based assessment of entrustable professional activity (EPA) allows faculty frequent opportunities to provide and document clinical performance feedback. Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) Milestones were previously mapped to each EPA and accompanying behavioral anchors reflect the range of competencies required to execute each clinical activity.

title: A Novel Hybrid Endovascular Technique for Tympanojugular Paraganglioma: Flow Diversion Followed by Direct Transauricular Squid Embolization.
abstract: Skull-base paragangliomas with persistent internal carotid artery (ICA) supply can be challenging to devascularize safely. We report a 17-yearold male with an Succinate Dehydrogenase Complex Iron Sulfur Subunit B (SDHB)-associated tympanojugular paraganglioma treated using a staged hybrid endovascular strategy after subtotal resection. Persistent supply from a short ICA feeder and circumferential involvement of the petrous ICA precluded safe conventional transarterial embolization. A Surpass Elite flow-diverting stent was deployed across the feeder after dual antiplatelet therapy to preserve parent-vessel patency, reduce tumour inflow, and reinforce the arterial wall. Four months later, protected direct transauricular and transcervical puncture embolization with Squid 12 was performed under intermittent ICA balloon occlusion. Marked tumor devascularization was achieved without embolic or thromboembolic complication, and definitive resection was completed without new neurological or cranial nerve deficit. This staged approach may provide a useful adjunct for selected skull-base paragangliomas with persistent ICA supply when conventional embolization carries unacceptable risk.

title: Association of Estimated Arterial Stiffness with Collateral Status and Functional Outcome after Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Secondary Analysis of the OPTIMAL-BP Trial.
abstract: PURPOSE: Estimated pulse wave velocity (ePWV) is a surrogate of arterial stiffness that may influence stroke outcomes and potentially affect collateral circulation. We examined the association of ePWV with collateral status and 3-month functional outcome after successful endovascular thrombectomy and explored the contribution of collateral status to this relationship across blood pressure (BP) management strategies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this secondary analysis of the Outcome in Patients Treated With Intra-Arterial Thrombectomy-Optimal Blood Pressure Control trial, 285 patients were analyzed. Collateral status was assessed using the Tan scale (poor, 0-1; good, 2-3). Poor functional outcome was defined as 3-month modified Rankin Scale score of 3-6. Multivariable logistic and mediation analyses were performed to evaluate the association between ePWV and functional outcomes and to explore direct and indirect pathways. RESULTS: A total of 285 patients were included (mean age, 73.3±11.3 years; 40.4% women). Each 1 m/s increase in ePWV was associated with poor collaterals (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 1.276, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.083-1.503) and poor functional outcome (adjusted OR 1.338, 95% CI 1.121-1.597). In mediation analyses, collateral status accounted for only a small proportion of the association between ePWV and poor functional outcome (indirect effect: adjusted β 0.022, 95% CI 0.001-0.053), whereas the direct effect remained significant (adjusted β 0.237, 95% CI 0.115-0.359). Neither the direct effect of ePWV on functional outcome nor the indirect effect through collateral status differed according to BP management strategy. CONCLUSION: Higher ePWV was associated with poor collateral status and unfavorable functional outcome after successful reperfusion. Collateral status accounted for only a small proportion of the observed association between ePWV and functional outcome.
englishSummary: PURPOSE: Estimated pulse wave velocity (ePWV) is a surrogate of arterial stiffness that may influence stroke outcomes and potentially affect collateral circulation. We examined the association of ePWV with collateral status and 3-month functional outcome after successful endovascular thrombectomy and explored the contribution of collateral status to this relationship across blood pressure (BP) management strategies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this secondary analysis of the Outcome in Patients Treated With Intra-Arterial Thrombectomy-Optimal Blood Pressure Control trial, 285 patients were analyzed.

title: Phenotypes of diabetic kidney disease and cardiovascular outcomes.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To quantify the association between diabetic kidney disease (DKD) phenotypes and cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality and incident major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), atrial fibrillation (AF), and peripheral artery disease (PAD). METHODS: [2] In this longitudinal analysis of adults with diabetes from NHANES (N = 5035) and the UK Biobank (UKBB, N = 26,968), participants were categorized by estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR, ml/min per 1.73m) and urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR, mg/g) into four phenotypes: no DKD (eGFR≥60, UACR<30), albuminuria-only (eGFR≥60, UACR≥30), low eGFR only (eGFR<60, UACR<30), and albuminuria+low eGFR (eGFR<60, UACR≥30). We estimated absolute and relative risk of CVD mortality (both cohorts) and incident non-fatal CVD (UKBB), adjusting for demographics, anthropometric and laboratory values, and medications. RESULTS: In both cohorts, the albuminuria+low eGFR phenotype was associated with the highest cardiovascular risk versus no DKD (reference). In NHANES, albuminuria-only was more strongly associated with CVD mortality than low eGFR only: albuminuria-only HR 2.56 (95%CI 1.86-3.53), low eGFR only HR 1.92 (1.35-2.73), albuminuria+low eGFR HR 3.16 (2.27-4.41). In UKBB, the low eGFR only phenotype was associated with higher risk of CVD mortality than the albuminuria-only phenotype: albuminuria-only HR 1.88 (1.66-2.13), low eGFR only HR 2.42 (1.99-2.95), albuminuria+low eGFR HR 4.65 (3.78-5.71). In UKBB, the albuminuria+low eGFR phenotype exhibited the strongest association with MACE, AF, and PAD. Similar patterns were observed with absolute risk calculations. CONCLUSIONS: Across two large cohorts, DKD phenotypes conferred distinct cardiovascular risk profiles. Consistent measurement of both eGFR and UACR in clinical practice may facilitate targeted, preventative cardiovascular care in diabetes.

title: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement in bicuspid versus tricuspid aortic valves among patients with mixed aortic valve disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Mixed aortic valve disease (MAVD), defined as the coexistence of significant aortic stenosis (AS) and aortic regurgitation (AR), presents unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Prior studies rarely distinguished bicuspid valve morphology in MAVD populations, and no study has evaluated long-term transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) outcomes between bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) and tricuspid aortic valve (TAV) patients in this setting. The aim is to investigate the clinical outcomes of BAV versus TAV morphology in patients with MAVD undergoing TAVR. METHODS: Between March 2013 and December 2024, 610 MAVD patients undergoing TAVR were included. Patients with severe AS and concomitant presence of moderate or more severe aortic regurgitation were defined as the MAVD. Clinical outcomes, functional status and echocardiography were followed and compared. RESULTS: A total of 610 patients were included in this study, 220 (36.1%) of whom were BAV morphology. BAV patients were younger (73 vs. 75 years, p < 0.001) and had a lower Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) score (3.47% vs. 4.15%, p < 0.001) compared to TAV patients. The five-year mortality rate was lower in bicuspid than tricuspid patients (10.5% vs. 18.7%, log-rank p = 0.014), while Cox regression analysis did not indicate BAV as an independent predictor of five-year all-cause mortality after multivariable adjustment (hazard ratio [HR] 0.75, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.47-1.22, p = 0.253). During the one-year follow-up after procedure, BAV patients exhibited a greater increase in AVA and LVEF (p for interaction = 0.012 and 0.011, respectively), and a greater reduction in mean gradient and peak velocity (both p for interaction < 0.001). Meanwhile, similar left ventricular reverse remodelling was found during follow-up (both p for trend < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: In MAVD patients undergoing TAVR, bicuspid and tricuspid valve morphologies demonstrated comparable long-term clinical outcomes. BAV patients demonstrated greater improvements in left ventricular function and transvalvular hemodynamics, suggesting that bicuspid morphology itself does not confer an adverse long-term prognostic effect in appropriately selected patients with MAVD undergoing TAVR. TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT02803294.

The aim is to investigate the clinical outcomes of BAV versus TAV morphology in patients with MAVD undergoing TAVR.

title: Intravenous thrombolysis in acute ischemic stroke after reversal of warfarin anticoagulation in patients with mechanical heart valve prostheses and an INR > 1.7.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute ischemic stroke (IS) frequently occurs in patients receiving oral anticoagulant (OAC) therapy. Although warfarin has largely been replaced by direct oral anticoagulants in routine clinical practice, it remains the only approved anticoagulant for certain indications, particularly in patients with mechanical heart valve protstheses. In these patients, the international normalized ratio (INR) is the key determinant of eligibility for intravenous thrombolysis (IVT). We present a potentially effective therapeutic strategy involving rapid reversal of warfarin anticoagulation with four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate (4F-PCC) followed by IVT. METHODS: We report two patients with similar clinical presentations who were receiving long-term warfarin therapy because of a mechanical aortic valve replacement. 76-year-old man with AIS had complete paralysis of the right lower limb, paresis of the right upper limb, and right central facial palsy. INR was 3.2. The second patient was a 76-year-old woman with dysarthria, left central facial palsy and left-sided hemiparesis. Her admission INR was 1.91. In both patients, CT angiography did not demonstrate arterial occlusion suitable for endovascular therapy. RESULTS: In both patients, four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate (4F-PCC) was administered to achieve rapid normalization of the INR. This was immediately followed by standard IVT. Both patients experienced marked neurological improvement, with no hemorrhagic or thromboembolic complications. At the 3-month follow-up, both had achieved complete functional recovery without residual neurological deficits. In conclusion, it can be stated that the chosen procedure led to an excellent clinical outcome in accordance with previously published cases, in the absence of other standard options for recanalization therapy.

In these patients, the international normalized ratio (INR) is the key determinant of eligibility for intravenous thrombolysis (IVT).

title: Postpartum venous thrombosis in Sweden: a nationwide family study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Postpartum venous thromboembolism is a serious complication. The importance of family history of venous thromboembolism remains unclear in the postpartum period. OBJECTIVE: To assess the importance of family history of venous thromboembolism for postpartum venous thromboembolism among primiparous women without previous venous thromboembolism. STUDY DESIGN: This nationwide population-based cohort study included 856,380 Swedish primiparous women between 1992 and 2018, without a history of venous thromboembolism, followed for incident postpartum venous thromboembolism within 90 days after discharge day. Relatives were identified through the Swedish Multi-Generation Register. The exposure was family history of venous thromboembolism in grandparents, parents, full siblings, half siblings, cousins, and spouses. A hereditary score consisting of 4 categories was constructed based on affected biological relatives and their degree of genetic relatedness. Venous thromboembolism in a grandparent contributed 0.5 points, venous thromboembolism in a parent 1 point, venous thromboembolism in a full sibling 1 point, venous thromboembolism in a half sibling 0.5 points, and venous thromboembolism in a cousin 0.25 points. Reference category 0=0 points, category 1=0.25 to 1 points, category 2=1.25 to 1.5, and category 3≥1.75 points. Cox proportional hazards models with multivariable adjustment were used to estimate hazard ratios with 95% confidence intervals. RESULTS: A total of 788 women (0.09%) developed postpartum venous thromboembolism. Family history in grandparents (hazard ratio=1.41; 95% confidence interval, 1.21-1.64), parents (hazard ratio=2.03; 95% confidence interval, 1.60-2.56), full sibling (hazard ratio=2.55; 95% confidence interval, 1.53-4.26), and half siblings (hazard ratio =2.28; 95% confidence interval, 1.08-4.80) was associated with increased venous thromboembolism risk. The hereditary score showed a clear dose-response pattern compared with those without family history: the fully adjusted hazard ratio was 1.50 (95% confidence interval 1.29-1.74) for the hereditary score category 1, hazard ratio=2.89 (95% confidence interval 2.01-4.16) for the score category 2, and hazard ratio=3.66 (95% confidence interval 2.06-6.51) for the score category 3. Additional independent predictors for venous thromboembolism in the fully adjusted model were obesity, cancer, systemic lupus erythematosus, varicose veins, gestational hypertension, preeclampsia or eclampsia, placental abruption, endometritis or puerperal fever, caesarean delivery, and postpartum hemorrhage-blood transfusion status. CONCLUSION: Family history of venous thromboembolism is a dose-graded risk factor for postpartum venous thromboembolism, with the risk increasing according to the number of affected relatives and degree of genetic relatedness.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Postpartum venous thromboembolism is a serious complication. The importance of family history of venous thromboembolism remains unclear in the postpartum period. OBJECTIVE: To assess the importance of family history of venous thromboembolism for postpartum venous thromboembolism among primiparous women without previous venous thromboembolism.

title: Primary Aortic Wall Myxoma Presenting With Recurrent Systemic Embolization: A Hybrid Surgical Management Strategy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Primary aortic wall myxoma is exceptionally rare and may mimic mural thrombus or acute aortic dissection. CASE SUMMARY: A 38-year-old man presented after approximately 12 hours of acute left lower-limb ischemia with concomitant left upper-limb occlusion. Computed tomography angiography showed filling defects in the ascending and descending thoracic aorta. Recurrent embolization after peripheral thromboembolectomy prompted emergency ascending aortic exploration. A friable intramural myxoma was excised with ascending aortic graft replacement; the descending lesion was excluded by staged thoracic endovascular aortic repair while therapeutic anticoagulation was maintained. DISCUSSION: Histopathology confirmed an aortic wall myxoma. The case illustrates the limitations of imaging and an individualized hybrid strategy for suspected multifocal aortic involvement. TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Recurrent embolization after embolectomy should prompt urgent proximal-source control. Hybrid repair may be considered when anatomy and clinical urgency support it.
